questions.rationale: Roth IRA contributions can be withdrawn anytime tax- and penalty-free because they come out before earnings.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is allocated a $5,000 charitable contribution on a partnership K-1. How is this reported on the individual's return?
options: It is a separately stated item carried to the partner's Schedule A as an itemized charitable contribution, subject to the individual's AGI limits
It is deducted on Schedule C as a business expense
It is nondeductible
It reduces partnership ordinary income directly
questions.rationale: A K-1 charitable contribution is a separately stated item reported on the partner's Schedule A, subject to AGI limits.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a $20,000 distribution from a 529 qualified tuition plan. Of this, $14,000 was used for qualified higher education expenses and $6,000 was not. The $6,000 nonqualified portion includes $2,000 of earnings. How is the nonqualified portion taxed?
options: The full $6,000 is taxable
None of it is taxable
Only the earnings portion of the nonqualified distribution ($2,000) is taxable, generally subject to a 10% additional tax, while the return of contributions is tax-free
The entire $20,000 is taxable
questions.rationale: On a nonqualified 529 distribution, only the earnings portion is taxable and generally subject to a 10% penalty; the contribution portion is tax-free.

questions.stem: Marcus and Dana married on December 30, 2024. They lived apart all year and each maintained a separate household. What is the earliest filing status they may use for the 2024 tax year?
options: They must file Head of Household separately
They may file Married Filing Jointly or Married Filing Separately
They may not file together until 2025
They must file as single because they married at year-end
questions.rationale: Marital status for the whole year is determined as of December 31, so a December 30 marriage allows MFJ or MFS for 2024.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Lena's spouse died in March 2023. In 2024 she remains unmarried and pays over half the cost of keeping up a home that is the principal residence of her dependent 6-year-old son. Which filing status gives her the most favorable result for 2024?
options: Married Filing Jointly
Qualifying Surviving Spouse
Head of Household
Single
questions.rationale: For the two tax years following the year of a spouse's death, a taxpayer with a dependent child may use Qualifying Surviving Spouse status, which is more favorable than HOH.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Which of the following individuals is required to have a Social Security number or ITIN to be claimed for the Child Tax Credit (not just as a dependent) in 2024?
options: A nonrelative member of the household
A qualifying child claimed for the Child Tax Credit
The taxpayer's adult roommate
The taxpayer's elderly parent claimed as a dependent
questions.rationale: A qualifying child must have an SSN valid for employment issued before the return due date to be eligible for the Child Tax Credit.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Two unmarried parents, Tom and Sara, never married and live together all year with their 4-year-old daughter, who qualifies as a qualifying child of both. They cannot agree on who claims her. Under the tie-breaker rules, who is entitled to claim the child?
options: Whichever parent files first
The parent with the higher adjusted gross income
The parent who provides more than half of the child's support
The parent with whom the child lived the longer time during the year
questions.rationale: When two parents can claim the same qualifying child and cannot agree, the tie-breaker awards the child to the parent with the higher adjusted gross income.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Robert, age 67, is unmarried and his only income for 2024 is $13,500 of Social Security benefits and $3,200 of taxable interest. Is he required to file a 2024 federal income tax return based on gross income alone?
options: Yes, because Social Security plus interest exceeds his filing threshold
No, because his gross income for the filing test is below his threshold
Yes, because anyone over age 65 must file
No, because Social Security recipients never have to file
questions.rationale: For the filing requirement, generally only taxable income counts; with only modest taxable interest below the threshold, Robert is not required to file based on gross income.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes who may be claimed as a 'qualifying relative' dependent in 2024?
options: A person who lived with the taxpayer for more than half the year and is under age 19
A person whose gross income is below the exemption amount and for whom the taxpayer provided over half the support
Any sibling regardless of income who lives in the same state
Anyone the taxpayer financially helped during the year
questions.rationale: A qualifying relative must meet a gross income test (below $5,050 for 2024) and a support test, among others; there is no age limit.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Jenna is a U.S. citizen. Her boyfriend's mother lived with Jenna the entire year, had gross income of $2,000, and Jenna provided more than half her support. The boyfriend's mother is not related to Jenna by blood or marriage. Can Jenna claim her as a dependent?
options: No, because only blood relatives qualify
Yes, as a qualifying relative because she lived with Jenna all year as a member of the household
Yes, but only as a qualifying child
No, because she is not related to Jenna
questions.rationale: An unrelated individual can be a qualifying relative if they live with the taxpayer all year as a household member and satisfy the gross income and support tests.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: For 2024, a dependent single taxpayer (claimed on another return) who is not blind and under 65 has $400 of wages and $1,600 of taxable interest. What is this dependent's standard deduction for 2024?
questions.rationale: A dependent's 2024 standard deduction is the greater of $1,300 or earned income plus $450, capped at the regular standard deduction; here $1,300 applies.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: A married couple wants to file separately. Which statement about Married Filing Separately is correct for 2024?
options: Both spouses may always claim the Earned Income Tax Credit
If one spouse itemizes deductions, the other spouse must also itemize (or take a zero standard deduction)
MFS filers may claim the American Opportunity Credit without restriction
MFS filers automatically qualify for the full Child and Dependent Care Credit
questions.rationale: When married taxpayers file separately and one itemizes, the other must also itemize; many credits are also restricted for MFS filers.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Which document is used by an employer to report wages and federal income tax withheld to an employee for the year?
options: Form 1099-NEC
Form 1098
Form W-2
Schedule K-1
questions.rationale: Employers report employee wages and withholding on Form W-2.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Mei is a resident alien for the entire 2024 tax year and her husband is a nonresident alien. They wish to file a joint return. What is generally required?
options: Only the resident spouse's income is reported on the joint return
They cannot file jointly under any circumstances
They must first obtain permanent resident status for both
They may elect to treat the nonresident alien spouse as a U.S. resident for the entire year, reporting worldwide income
questions.rationale: A U.S. resident and a nonresident alien spouse may elect to treat the nonresident as a resident for the whole year, filing jointly and reporting worldwide income.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally NOT included in gross income for federal tax purposes?
options: Tips received from customers
Child support received
Gambling winnings
Unemployment compensation
questions.rationale: Child support is excluded from the recipient's gross income, unlike tips, gambling winnings, and unemployment compensation.

questions.stem: An employee received $60,000 in salary plus the use of an employer-provided vehicle worth $4,000 (a taxable fringe benefit) and $250 in qualified de minimis benefits. What amount is includible in the employee's gross income from these items?
questions.rationale: Taxable fringe benefits such as personal use of an employer vehicle are includible, while qualified de minimis benefits are excluded.

questions.stem: In 2024, Donna cashed in a Series EE U.S. savings bond and received $5,000, of which $1,400 was interest. She paid qualified higher education expenses of $5,000 for her dependent and meets all requirements of the education savings bond exclusion. Her modified AGI is below the phase-out. How much of the interest is taxable?
questions.rationale: When qualified higher education expenses equal or exceed the redemption proceeds and all requirements are met, the savings bond interest is fully excludable.

questions.stem: Which of the following is taxable income to the recipient?
options: Gifts received from a family member
Compensatory damages for physical personal injuries
A qualified scholarship used for tuition and required fees
Interest on a federal income tax refund
questions.rationale: Interest on a tax refund is taxable, even though scholarships for tuition, physical-injury damages, and gifts are generally excluded.

questions.stem: Greg owns 200 shares of XYZ stock and received a nontaxable 2-for-1 stock split, giving him 400 shares. His original basis in the 200 shares was $8,000. After the split, what is his per-share basis?
options: $20 per share
$80 per share
$8,000 total with no per-share change
$40 per share
questions.rationale: A stock split does not change total basis; the original basis is reallocated across the increased number of shares.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of income is reported on Schedule B when total taxable interest and ordinary dividends each exceed the reporting threshold?
options: Self-employment income
Wages and salaries
Capital gains from stock sales
Taxable interest and ordinary dividends
questions.rationale: Schedule B reports taxable interest and ordinary dividends, generally required when either exceeds $1,500.

questions.stem: Alicia received a distribution from a Roth IRA. The account was opened 6 years ago, she is age 60, and the distribution is $20,000 (consisting of $12,000 of contributions and $8,000 of earnings). How much, if any, is taxable?
options: $8,000 of earnings
$0 because it is a qualified distribution
$12,000 of contributions
$20,000 fully taxable
questions.rationale: A qualified Roth IRA distribution (account held 5+ years and owner age 59 1/2 or older) is entirely tax-free, including earnings.

questions.stem: Hank loaned $10,000 to a friend with no interest charged. The applicable federal rate would have produced $400 of interest. Assume the below-market loan rules apply and no exception is met. What is the general tax consequence?
options: Hank may deduct the $10,000 as a bad debt immediately
No tax consequence because no interest was actually paid
The borrower must report $10,000 as income
Imputed interest of $400 is treated as transferred and may have income tax effects
questions.rationale: Below-market loans can trigger imputed interest under the AFR, creating interest income to the lender and a deemed transfer to the borrower.

questions.stem: Jury duty pay received by a taxpayer is:
options: Reported as a capital gain
Always nontaxable
Taxable income reported on the return
Taxable only if it exceeds $600
questions.rationale: Jury duty pay is taxable income, though amounts surrendered to an employer may be offset by a corresponding adjustment.

questions.stem: Theo, age 45, took a $15,000 distribution from his traditional IRA in 2024. He had made $30,000 of nondeductible contributions over the years, and the total value of all his traditional IRAs at year-end plus this distribution was $75,000. Using the pro-rata rule, approximately how much of the $15,000 distribution is nontaxable?
questions.rationale: Under the pro-rata rule, the nontaxable portion equals the ratio of after-tax basis to total IRA value times the distribution: 40% of $15,000 = $6,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally taxable as ordinary income rather than capital gain?
options: Long-term gain on the sale of stock held 3 years
Interest earned on a certificate of deposit
Gain on the sale of a personal residence within the exclusion
Qualified dividends
questions.rationale: Interest income, such as from a CD, is taxed as ordinary income, unlike long-term gains and qualified dividends taxed at preferential rates.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $1,200 in cryptocurrency as payment for freelance services in 2024. The fair market value of the crypto at receipt was $1,200. How is this treated?
options: A capital gain of $1,200
Ordinary income of $1,200 at the time of receipt
Not taxable until the crypto is sold
Excluded as a digital asset
questions.rationale: Cryptocurrency received for services is ordinary income at its fair market value on the date received; later sales may generate capital gain or loss.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of constructive receipt of income in 2024?
options: Income deferred under a valid retirement plan
A bond's accrued interest not yet payable
Stock appreciation that has not been realized
A bonus check made available on December 31, 2024 but not picked up until January 2025
questions.rationale: Constructive receipt occurs when income is made available without substantial restriction, even if not physically taken until later.

questions.stem: Nadia's employer paid $80,000 of group-term life insurance coverage on her behalf. The cost of the first $50,000 is excludable. The IRS Table I cost of the excess $30,000 of coverage for the year is $66. How much must Nadia include in income?
questions.rationale: Employer-provided group-term life insurance over $50,000 results in includible income equal to the Table I cost of the excess coverage.

questions.stem: A taxpayer paid $9,000 in state income taxes and $5,500 in real estate property taxes in 2024 and itemizes. What is the maximum deduction allowed for state and local taxes on Schedule A?
questions.rationale: The combined deduction for state and local income, sales, and property taxes is limited to $10,000 ($5,000 MFS).

questions.stem: Sam, single, has AGI of $100,000 and paid $12,000 of unreimbursed medical expenses in 2024. How much of the medical expense is deductible as an itemized deduction?
questions.rationale: Medical expenses are deductible only to the extent they exceed 7.5% of AGI; here that allows a $4,500 deduction.

questions.stem: In 2024, a married couple filing jointly with two qualifying children under age 17 has a tax before credits of $4,000 and modified AGI of $90,000. What is the maximum Child Tax Credit (nonrefundable portion) they can use to reduce their tax to zero?
questions.rationale: The Child Tax Credit is up to $2,000 per qualifying child; two children allow up to $4,000 to offset tax liability, with phase-outs beginning at higher income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer paid $4,000 of qualified tuition for the first four years of a degree program for a dependent who is enrolled at least half time. The taxpayer's MAGI is within limits. What is the maximum American Opportunity Tax Credit available?
questions.rationale: The AOTC equals 100% of the first $2,000 plus 25% of the next $2,000 of qualified expenses, for a maximum of $2,500.

questions.stem: Which of the following expenses qualifies for the Child and Dependent Care Credit?
options: Babysitting so the parents can go to a movie
Overnight summer camp for a 9-year-old
Day care for a 5-year-old so both parents can work
Private school tuition for a 7-year-old
questions.rationale: Work-related care expenses for a qualifying child under 13, such as day care, qualify for the Child and Dependent Care Credit; overnight camp and tuition do not.

questions.stem: For the Earned Income Tax Credit in 2024, which of the following would disqualify an otherwise-eligible taxpayer?
options: Having one qualifying child
Investment income above the annual limit ($11,600 for 2024)
Filing as Head of Household
Earning wages of $20,000
questions.rationale: A taxpayer is ineligible for the EITC if investment income exceeds the annual limit ($11,600 for 2024).

questions.stem: A taxpayer placed a new qualifying central air conditioner in service in their existing main home in 2024 that meets the energy efficiency standards, costing $2,000. What is the general limit on the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit for this type of property, assuming no other improvements?
options: 30% of cost with no annual limit
100% of cost
A flat $500 lifetime credit
30% of cost up to a $600 annual limit for the qualifying air conditioner
questions.rationale: The Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit is generally 30% of cost subject to item-specific annual limits, such as $600 for qualifying central air conditioners.

questions.stem: A taxpayer bought a new qualifying clean vehicle (EV) in 2024 for personal use and meets all income and vehicle requirements. What is the maximum new clean vehicle credit potentially available?
questions.rationale: The maximum new clean vehicle credit is $7,500, subject to sourcing requirements and income/MSRP limits.

questions.stem: A taxpayer made a $3,000 cash contribution to a qualified public charity and a $2,000 contribution of long-term appreciated stock (FMV $2,000, basis $500) to the same charity in 2024. Assuming AGI limits are not exceeded, what is the total charitable deduction?
questions.rationale: Cash to a public charity is deductible at the amount given, and long-term appreciated stock is generally deductible at fair market value, subject to AGI limits.

questions.stem: Which of the following individuals may be subject to the Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT) for 2024?
options: A taxpayer with MAGI of $80,000 and investment income
A taxpayer with only wage income of $300,000
A single taxpayer with MAGI of $150,000 and $20,000 of net investment income
A single taxpayer with MAGI of $250,000 and $30,000 of net investment income
questions.rationale: NIIT applies a 3.8% tax when MAGI exceeds the threshold ($200,000 single) and there is net investment income.

questions.stem: The Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) is designed to:
options: Replace the regular tax entirely for high earners
Provide an additional refundable credit
Ensure taxpayers with substantial economic income pay at least a minimum amount of tax
Tax only capital gains
questions.rationale: The AMT is a parallel tax ensuring taxpayers with substantial income pay a minimum amount despite preferences and deductions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an adjustment or preference item that may increase Alternative Minimum Taxable Income?
options: Charitable contributions to public charities
Mortgage interest on acquisition debt for a main home
Qualified dividends
The standard deduction (added back for AMT)
questions.rationale: The standard deduction is disallowed for AMT and added back, increasing alternative minimum taxable income.

questions.stem: Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends for most taxpayers in 2024 are taxed at preferential rates of:
options: A flat 25%
Ordinary income rates
0%, 15%, or 20% depending on taxable income
A flat 10%
questions.rationale: Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends are taxed at 0%, 15%, or 20% depending on taxable income.

questions.stem: An individual has $5,000 of short-term capital gains and $8,000 of long-term capital losses in 2024, with no other capital transactions. What is the net capital result?
options: $3,000 net long-term loss, with $3,000 deductible against ordinary income
$5,000 gain
$13,000 net loss
$8,000 loss carried forward entirely
questions.rationale: Capital gains and losses net together; a net capital loss is deductible against ordinary income up to $3,000 per year, with the excess carried forward.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has taxable income consisting of $44,000 of ordinary income and $10,000 of net long-term capital gain in 2024, filing single. The 0% long-term capital gains rate bracket for single filers tops out at $47,025 of taxable income for 2024. Approximately how is the long-term gain taxed?
options: Part of the gain at 0% (up to the bracket top) and the remainder at 15%
questions.rationale: Long-term gains stack on top of ordinary income; gain falling within the 0% bracket is untaxed and the remainder is taxed at 15% at this income level.

questions.stem: The 'kiddie tax' applies to:
options: Wages earned by a teenager
Certain unearned income of a child above a threshold, taxed partly at the parent's rate
All income of any minor
Self-employment income of a college student
questions.rationale: The kiddie tax taxes a child's unearned income above the threshold at the parent's rate to limit income shifting.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sold collectibles (a coin collection held 5 years) for a $12,000 long-term gain in 2024. What maximum federal rate applies to this collectibles gain?
questions.rationale: Long-term gains on collectibles are subject to a maximum federal rate of 28%, higher than the general long-term capital gains rates.

questions.stem: Self-employment tax for 2024 is computed on:
options: 100% of net self-employment profit at 15.3%
Only the Medicare portion
Gross receipts at 7.65%
Net self-employment earnings (generally 92.35% of net profit) at 15.3% up to the Social Security wage base for the OASDI portion
questions.rationale: SE tax applies 15.3% to net earnings (92.35% of net profit), with the Social Security portion capped at the wage base and Medicare uncapped.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $30,000 in unemployment compensation in 2024. For federal purposes, how is it taxed?
options: Only half is taxable
Taxable only if the taxpayer also had wages
Fully excluded from income
Fully included in gross income and taxable
questions.rationale: For 2024 there is no exclusion for unemployment compensation; it is fully taxable.

questions.stem: Up to what maximum percentage of Social Security benefits may be included in gross income for a high-income taxpayer in 2024?
questions.rationale: At higher income levels, up to 85% of Social Security benefits may be includible in gross income.

questions.stem: To avoid an underpayment penalty for 2024, an individual whose prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000 must generally pay (through withholding and estimates) at least:
options: 100% of the current-year tax only
90% of the current-year tax or 100% of the prior-year tax
80% of the current-year tax
90% of the current-year tax or 110% of the prior-year tax
questions.rationale: Higher-income taxpayers (prior-year AGI over $150,000) must pay 90% of current-year tax or 110% of prior-year tax to meet the safe harbor.

questions.stem: A taxpayer age 52 wants to maximize 2024 IRA contributions. What is the maximum, including the catch-up amount?
questions.rationale: For those age 50 or older, the 2024 IRA contribution limit is $7,000 plus a $1,000 catch-up, totaling $8,000.

questions.stem: Required minimum distributions (RMDs) from traditional IRAs must generally begin by April 1 of the year following the year the account owner reaches what age under current law (for someone who turns that age in 2024)?
questions.rationale: Under SECURE 2.0, the required beginning age for RMDs is 73 for those reaching that age in 2024.

questions.stem: A taxpayer expects a large capital gain late in 2024 and wants to avoid an estimated tax penalty. Which strategy is most directly effective in treating tax as paid evenly throughout the year?
options: Reducing 401(k) contributions
Filing for an extension
Making a single estimated payment in January 2025
Increasing federal income tax withholding from wages
questions.rationale: Withholding is treated as paid evenly across the year, so boosting withholding can cover a late-year gain and avoid an underpayment penalty.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to make a 2024 IRA contribution. What is the deadline to make it and have it count for the 2024 tax year?
options: The unextended due date of the 2024 return (generally April 15, 2025)
Anytime during 2025
December 31, 2024
October 15, 2025
questions.rationale: IRA contributions for a tax year may be made up to the unextended return due date (generally April 15 of the following year).

questions.stem: A 60-year-old taxpayer rolled over a $50,000 distribution from a 401(k) into a traditional IRA within 30 days, using a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer. What is the tax consequence?
options: A 10% early withdrawal penalty applies
Only the earnings portion is taxable
No tax is due; a direct rollover is not a taxable distribution
$50,000 is taxable in the year of the rollover
questions.rationale: A direct trustee-to-trustee rollover from a 401(k) to a traditional IRA is tax-free and avoids early withdrawal penalties.

questions.stem: Which of the following distributions from a traditional IRA before age 59 1/2 is exempt from the 10% additional tax (early withdrawal penalty)?
options: A distribution up to $10,000 for a first-time home purchase
A distribution to pay off credit card debt
Any distribution if the taxpayer is unemployed for one month
A distribution used to buy a vacation home
questions.rationale: A distribution up to $10,000 used for a first-time home purchase is exempt from the 10% early withdrawal penalty.

questions.stem: The 2024 elective deferral limit for an employee contributing to a 401(k) plan (under age 50) is:
questions.rationale: The 2024 401(k) elective deferral limit is $23,000 (under 50), or $30,500 with the catch-up at 50 or older.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to make a Roth IRA contribution for 2024 but has high income. Above which mechanism may a high earner still get funds into a Roth even when direct contributions are phased out?
options: There is no legal way to fund a Roth at high income
A SIMPLE IRA rollover that bypasses limits
A spousal exemption regardless of income
A nondeductible traditional IRA contribution followed by a conversion (a 'backdoor' Roth)
questions.rationale: High earners phased out of direct Roth contributions may use a nondeductible traditional IRA contribution and convert it (a backdoor Roth), subject to the pro-rata rule.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who failed to take a required minimum distribution may face an excise tax. Under SECURE 2.0, the excise tax on the missed RMD amount is generally:
options: 25%, reduced to 10% if timely corrected
questions.rationale: SECURE 2.0 lowered the missed-RMD excise tax to 25%, reduced to 10% if the shortfall is corrected timely.

questions.stem: A married couple, only one of whom has earned income of $90,000, wants to fund IRAs for both spouses for 2024. Can the nonworking spouse contribute?
options: Only if the nonworking spouse is over 65
No, IRAs require the contributor to have earned income
Only into a Roth, never a traditional IRA
Yes, through a spousal IRA based on the working spouse's earned income
questions.rationale: A spousal IRA allows a nonworking spouse to contribute based on the working spouse's earned income on a joint return.

questions.stem: A member of the U.S. Armed Forces serving in a designated combat zone receives combat pay. How is enlisted combat pay generally treated for federal income tax?
options: Excluded from gross income for enlisted members (with limits for officers)
Excluded only if the member is married
Fully taxable like regular wages
Taxable only for the Medicare portion
questions.rationale: Combat pay is excluded from gross income for enlisted members, with a cap for commissioned officers.

questions.stem: A taxpayer may elect to include nontaxable combat pay in earned income for purposes of which credit, when doing so increases the credit?
options: The Foreign Tax Credit
The Earned Income Tax Credit
The Premium Tax Credit
The Adoption Credit
questions.rationale: Taxpayers may elect to include nontaxable combat pay in earned income for the EITC when it increases the credit.

questions.stem: A member of the clergy receives a designated housing (parsonage) allowance. For income tax purposes, the housing allowance is:
options: Fully excluded from both income and self-employment tax
Fully taxable for both income and self-employment tax
Taxable only if the minister owns the home
Excludable from income tax up to the lesser of the amount used for housing or the fair rental value, but generally still subject to self-employment tax
questions.rationale: A clergy housing allowance is excludable from income tax up to qualifying limits but generally remains subject to self-employment tax.

questions.stem: When a taxpayer dies, the final Form 1040 generally reports income:
options: No income at all
For the entire calendar year regardless of date of death
Only income received after death
Through the date of death, on the cash method for cash-basis decedents
questions.rationale: A decedent's final Form 1040 reports income and deductions through the date of death; post-death income goes on the estate's or beneficiary's return.

questions.stem: An estate or trust files which income tax return form?
options: Form 706
Form 709
Form 1040
Form 1041
questions.rationale: Form 1041 is the income tax return for estates and trusts; Form 706 is the estate tax return.

questions.stem: A taxpayer needs to correct an error on a previously filed Form 1040. To claim a refund, the amended return (Form 1040-X) generally must be filed within:
options: 5 years from filing
1 year of the original due date
There is no time limit for refunds
3 years from the date the original return was filed or 2 years from when the tax was paid, whichever is later
questions.rationale: A refund claim on Form 1040-X must generally be filed within 3 years of filing the original return or 2 years of paying the tax, whichever is later.

questions.stem: A surviving spouse who has not remarried may file a joint return with the deceased spouse for which year?
options: Any of the three years after death
The year of the spouse's death
Only if a court appoints an executor first
Never; death ends joint filing eligibility
questions.rationale: A surviving spouse who has not remarried may file a joint return with the decedent for the year of death.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's 23-year-old child was a full-time student for five months in 2024, lived at home all year, and earned $4,000. The parents provided more than half the child's support. Can the parents claim the child as a qualifying child?
options: Yes, if the child was a full-time student for at least five months and under age 24 at year-end
No, because the child is over age 19
No, because the child earned income
Yes, but only as a qualifying relative due to the income
questions.rationale: A full-time student under age 24 (at least five months) who meets residency and support tests is a qualifying child, regardless of income.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: A landlord received a $1,500 security deposit from a tenant in 2024 that the landlord must return at lease-end if no damage occurs. How is the deposit treated in 2024?
options: Not income when received because it is a refundable deposit held for the tenant
Taxable only if the lease is over one year
Taxable rental income when received
A capital gain
questions.rationale: A refundable security deposit is not rental income when received; it becomes income only if the landlord keeps it.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sold their main home in 2024 for a $400,000 gain. They are single, owned and used the home as their main residence for the last 3 years, and have not used the exclusion in the past two years. How much gain is taxable?
questions.rationale: A single taxpayer meeting the ownership and use tests may exclude up to $250,000 of gain on a main home; the excess ($150,000 here) is taxable.

questions.stem: In 2024, a single taxpayer with no children, age 30, earned $12,000 in wages and has $0 investment income. They are not a dependent. Are they potentially eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit?
options: Yes, but only if over age 65
Yes, childless workers age 25 to 64 may qualify within income limits
No, only married couples qualify
No, the EITC requires a qualifying child
questions.rationale: Childless workers aged 25 to 64 within the income limits may qualify for the EITC, though the credit is smaller than with qualifying children.

questions.stem: A taxpayer made qualified charitable contributions of cash equal to 70% of AGI to a public charity in 2024. What is the general AGI limitation on the cash contribution deduction, with any excess carried forward?
options: 20% of AGI
60% of AGI
30% of AGI
100% of AGI
questions.rationale: Cash contributions to public charities are generally limited to 60% of AGI, with a five-year carryforward of the excess.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has a wash sale: they sold stock at a $2,000 loss and bought substantially identical stock 10 days later. What is the tax treatment of the $2,000 loss?
options: Half deductible now and half later
Disallowed currently; the loss is added to the basis of the replacement shares
Treated as a long-term gain
Fully deductible in the current year
questions.rationale: Under the wash sale rule, a loss on a security repurchased within 30 days is disallowed and added to the basis of the replacement shares.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has a passive rental loss of $30,000 in 2024 and actively participates in the rental. Their modified AGI is $110,000. Under the $25,000 special allowance rules, how much of the loss can offset nonpassive income?
questions.rationale: The $25,000 active-participation rental loss allowance phases out 50% of MAGI over $100,000; at $110,000 MAGI, $20,000 is allowed.

questions.stem: Which type of income is generally NOT subject to self-employment tax?
options: Income from a side gig reported on Schedule C
Net rental real estate income for a non-dealer landlord
Net profit from a sole proprietorship
A general partner's distributive share of trade or business income
questions.rationale: Rental real estate income (for a non-dealer landlord) is generally not subject to self-employment tax, unlike sole proprietorship and partnership business income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer made a $7,000 traditional IRA contribution for 2024 but is an active participant in an employer plan with MAGI above the deduction phase-out. What is the result?
options: The contribution is prohibited
The contribution is allowed but nondeductible, creating basis in the IRA
The entire contribution must be refunded
The contribution converts automatically to a Roth
questions.rationale: An active participant above the deduction phase-out may still make a nondeductible traditional IRA contribution, creating basis reported on Form 8606.

questions.stem: A taxpayer claims the Foreign Tax Credit for income taxes paid to a foreign country on foreign-source income. A key benefit of the credit (versus a deduction) is that it:
options: Eliminates the need to report foreign income
Reduces U.S. tax liability dollar for dollar, subject to limitation
Is fully refundable in all cases
Reduces taxable income dollar for dollar
questions.rationale: The Foreign Tax Credit reduces U.S. tax liability dollar for dollar (subject to limitation), generally more valuable than a deduction.

questions.stem: To qualify as Head of Household, a taxpayer must generally pay more than what portion of the cost of keeping up the home?
options: All of it
One-quarter
More than half
One-third
questions.rationale: Head of Household requires paying more than half the cost of keeping up the home for a qualifying person.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $5,000 in qualified dividends and $3,000 in nonqualified (ordinary) dividends in 2024. How are these taxed?
options: Qualified dividends at preferential capital gains rates; ordinary dividends at ordinary rates
Both at preferential capital gains rates
Both at ordinary rates
Both are tax-exempt
questions.rationale: Qualified dividends are taxed at preferential capital gains rates; nonqualified (ordinary) dividends are taxed at ordinary rates.

questions.stem: A taxpayer contributes to a Health Savings Account (HSA) in 2024 with self-only HDHP coverage. The 2024 self-only HSA contribution limit (under age 55) is:
questions.rationale: The 2024 HSA self-only contribution limit is $4,150 (family is $8,300), with a $1,000 catch-up at age 55 or older.

questions.stem: A taxpayer exercised an incentive stock option (ISO) in 2024 and did not sell the stock by year-end. The bargain element was $20,000. For regular tax, there is no income at exercise. What is the AMT consequence?
options: No effect on AMT
The $20,000 is a capital loss
The $20,000 bargain element is an AMT adjustment increasing AMTI in the year of exercise
The $20,000 is ordinary income for both regular and AMT
questions.rationale: Exercising an ISO and holding the stock creates a positive AMT adjustment equal to the bargain element, even though regular tax recognizes no income at exercise.

questions.stem: Estimated tax payments for individuals are generally due in how many installments during the year?
options: Four
One
Two
Twelve
questions.rationale: Individual estimated taxes are generally paid in four installments during the tax year.

questions.stem: A clergy member who has not elected exemption from self-employment tax computes SE tax on:
options: Only the cash salary, excluding any housing allowance
Zero, because clergy are always exempt
Net earnings including the housing allowance value
Only the housing allowance
questions.rationale: Ministers generally include both salary and housing allowance in net earnings for self-employment tax, absent an approved exemption.

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally tax-free to the employee when provided by an employer?
options: Year-end gift of cash
Cash bonuses
Personal use of a company car
Employer contributions to a qualified health plan (employee's share of premiums paid by employer)
questions.rationale: Employer-provided health coverage is generally excludable from the employee's income, unlike cash bonuses or personal car use.

questions.stem: A taxpayer with three qualifying children claims the Child Tax Credit but owes only $1,200 in tax before credits, with $30,000 of earned income. How does the Additional Child Tax Credit help?
options: It doubles the per-child credit
It can refund a portion of the unused CTC, up to $1,700 per child for 2024, based on earned income over $2,500
It is unavailable when tax liability is low
It only applies to taxpayers with no earned income
questions.rationale: The Additional Child Tax Credit refunds part of the unused CTC, up to $1,700 per child for 2024, based on 15% of earned income over $2,500.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has $4,000 of gambling winnings and $5,000 of documented gambling losses in 2024 and itemizes. How much can they deduct for gambling losses?
questions.rationale: Gambling losses are deductible as an itemized deduction only up to the amount of gambling winnings reported.

questions.stem: A taxpayer underpaid estimated taxes and owes a penalty. The penalty is generally NOT imposed if the balance due after withholding is:
options: Less than $10,000
Less than $1,000
Less than $5,000
Any amount, penalties always apply
questions.rationale: No estimated tax underpayment penalty applies if the balance owed after withholding and credits is less than $1,000.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a distribution from a qualified disaster-related retirement account under special rules. Which is a typical feature of qualified disaster distributions?
options: They are always tax-free
They must be fully repaid within 30 days
The 10% early withdrawal penalty may be waived and income may be spread over three years
They are limited to $1,000
questions.rationale: Qualified disaster distributions typically waive the 10% penalty and allow income to be spread over three years, with a repayment option.

questions.stem: A U.S. citizen child lived with the taxpayer for exactly 6 months and with the other parent for 6 months in 2024. For determining the custodial parent, the child is treated as living with:
options: The parent with higher income automatically
Both parents equally with no custodial parent
The parent with whom the child spent the greater number of nights
Neither parent
questions.rationale: The custodial parent is the one with whom the child spent the greater number of nights during the year.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: An employee participated in a nonqualified deferred compensation plan and deferred $20,000 of salary in 2024 under a valid arrangement that meets Section 409A. When is the $20,000 generally taxed?
options: In 2024 when deferred
Half in 2024 and half later
When actually or constructively received in a later year
Never
questions.rationale: Validly deferred nonqualified compensation is taxed when received in a later year, not at the time of deferral.

questions.stem: A cash charitable contribution of $300 made by check to a qualified charity in 2024 is deductible:
options: Only if the taxpayer itemizes deductions
Always as an above-the-line deduction
Never
Only if it exceeds $500
questions.rationale: For 2024, charitable contributions are deductible only by taxpayers who itemize; the temporary above-the-line deduction is no longer available.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sold equipment used in a sole proprietorship for a gain that includes depreciation previously taken. The portion attributable to depreciation recapture is generally taxed as:
options: Tax-exempt
A nondeductible loss
Ordinary income to the extent of Section 1245 recapture
Long-term capital gain
questions.rationale: Gain attributable to prior depreciation on Section 1245 property is recaptured and taxed as ordinary income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to convert a $50,000 traditional IRA to a Roth IRA in 2024. What is the tax consequence of the conversion (assuming all pre-tax dollars)?
options: Only the earnings are taxed
No tax now or later
A 10% penalty always applies to conversions
The $50,000 is included in income in the year of conversion
questions.rationale: Converting pre-tax traditional IRA funds to a Roth IRA includes the converted amount in income for the conversion year, but no 10% penalty applies to the conversion.

questions.stem: A nonresident alien is generally taxed by the United States on:
options: Worldwide income
No income at all
U.S.-source income and income effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business
Only foreign-source income
questions.rationale: Nonresident aliens are taxed on U.S.-source income and income effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business, not worldwide income.

questions.stem: Which of the following relationships does NOT meet the relationship test for a qualifying child?
options: Son or daughter
Brother or sister
Cousin
Stepchild
questions.rationale: A cousin does not satisfy the qualifying child relationship test, unlike a child, sibling, or stepchild.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a $10,000 inheritance and $400 of interest earned on the inherited funds after receiving them. What is taxable?
options: The $10,000 inheritance only
Both the $10,000 and the $400
The $400 of interest only
Neither amount
questions.rationale: An inheritance is not taxable income, but income earned on inherited assets after receipt (such as interest) is taxable.

questions.stem: A taxpayer with MAGI of $95,000 (single) paid $5,000 in mortgage interest, $4,000 in state taxes, and made a $1,000 cash gift to charity in 2024. Their total itemized deductions are $10,000. Compared to the $14,600 standard deduction, what should they generally do?
options: They must itemize because they have a mortgage
Itemize because it is always better
Take the standard deduction because it exceeds their itemized total
Take whichever is smaller
questions.rationale: A taxpayer should generally take the larger of the standard or itemized deduction; here the $14,600 standard deduction beats $10,000 itemized.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has wages of $50,000 and net self-employment income of $20,000 in 2024. Which statement about the deduction for one-half of SE tax is correct?
options: No deduction is allowed for SE tax
One-half of the self-employment tax is an above-the-line deduction
The full SE tax is deductible
SE tax is deductible only if itemizing
questions.rationale: One-half of self-employment tax is deductible as an above-the-line adjustment to income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer may generally avoid the estimated tax penalty by ensuring withholding and estimated payments equal at least 90% of:
options: Twice the current year's tax
Last year's tax
The current year's tax
The standard deduction
questions.rationale: One estimated tax safe harbor is paying at least 90% of the current year's tax liability through withholding and estimates.

questions.stem: A taxpayer serving in a combat zone receives an automatic extension of time to file and pay. The extension generally lasts:
options: No extension is available for combat zone service
At least 180 days after the last day in the combat zone, plus additional days
Until April 15 only
30 days after leaving the combat zone
questions.rationale: Combat zone service generally extends filing and payment deadlines by at least 180 days after leaving the zone, plus additional days.

questions.stem: Twins, age 16, are claimed as dependents by their parents. The parents are divorced and have equal custody (equal nights), but one parent (the father) has AGI of $80,000 and the mother has AGI of $95,000. Absent a Form 8332 release, who may claim the children under the tie-breaker rule?
options: The father, with lower AGI
Neither parent
They split one child each automatically
The mother, with higher AGI
questions.rationale: When a child lives with each parent an equal number of nights, the tie-breaker awards the dependency to the parent with the higher AGI.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: The adoption credit for 2024 is best described as:
options: A refundable credit for all adoption costs
A nonrefundable credit for qualified adoption expenses up to an annual maximum, subject to income phase-out
An above-the-line deduction
Available only for foreign adoptions
questions.rationale: The adoption credit is a nonrefundable credit for qualified adoption expenses up to an annual maximum, phased out at higher incomes.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has a net capital loss of $9,000 in 2024 with no capital gains. How much can be deducted against ordinary income in 2024 and how is the rest treated?
options: $9,000 all this year
$3,000 this year; remainder lost
$0; all carried forward
$3,000 this year; $6,000 carried forward
questions.rationale: A net capital loss offsets ordinary income up to $3,000 per year ($1,500 MFS), with the excess carried forward indefinitely.

questions.stem: A taxpayer made an excess contribution to a Roth IRA. If not corrected by the deadline, the excess is subject to an excise tax of:
options: No penalty
6% per year on the excess until corrected
10% one time
25% one time
questions.rationale: An uncorrected excess IRA contribution incurs a 6% excise tax per year until the excess is removed or absorbed.

questions.stem: A decedent's estate received $5,000 of interest income after the date of death that the decedent had not yet received. On which return is this income reported if the estate collects it?
options: Form 706
The estate's Form 1041 (or the beneficiary's return if distributed)
The decedent's final Form 1040
It is never reported
questions.rationale: Income in respect of a decedent collected by the estate is reported on Form 1041 (or by the beneficiary if distributed), not the final 1040.

questions.stem: A taxpayer and their spouse are both nonresident aliens with no U.S. trade or business but have U.S.-source dividend income. Which filing status consideration applies?
options: Nonresident aliens generally cannot file as Head of Household
They must file a joint resident return
They may file Head of Household
They are exempt from all U.S. tax
questions.rationale: Nonresident aliens generally cannot file as Head of Household and report U.S.-source income on Form 1040-NR.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: Workers' compensation benefits received for a job-related injury are:
options: Fully taxable
Generally excluded from gross income
Taxable only above $10,000
Taxed at capital gains rates
questions.rationale: Workers' compensation benefits for job-related injury or sickness are generally excluded from gross income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's only income is $2,000 of interest and $40,000 of long-term capital gain, filing single in 2024. Much of the long-term gain could fall in the 0% bracket. This illustrates that long-term capital gains:
options: Are always taxed at 20%
Are never taxable
Can be taxed at 0% when total taxable income is low enough
Are taxed at ordinary rates
questions.rationale: Long-term capital gains can be taxed at 0% when taxable income is low enough to fall within the 0% bracket.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is unmarried at year-end and has no dependents. The only filing status available is generally:
options: Head of Household
Single
Married Filing Jointly
Qualifying Surviving Spouse
questions.rationale: An unmarried taxpayer with no dependents and no special circumstances files as Single.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a Form 1099-C reporting $8,000 of canceled credit card debt in 2024. Immediately before the cancellation, the taxpayer was insolvent by $10,000 (liabilities exceeded assets). How much of the canceled debt is taxable?
options: $0 because the insolvency exclusion covers it
questions.rationale: Canceled debt is excluded from income to the extent the taxpayer was insolvent immediately before cancellation; here insolvency exceeds the canceled amount, so none is taxable.

questions.stem: Which of the following taxes is generally deductible as an itemized deduction (subject to the SALT cap)?
options: Social Security tax withheld
Federal excise taxes
Federal income tax
State and local real estate taxes
questions.rationale: State and local real estate taxes are deductible itemized deductions, subject to the $10,000 SALT cap; federal taxes are not deductible.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's qualified business income (QBI) from a sole proprietorship is $100,000, and taxable income before the QBI deduction is below the threshold. What is the general maximum QBI deduction?
questions.rationale: The qualified business income deduction is generally 20% of QBI for taxpayers below the income threshold, here $20,000.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to reduce 2024 taxable income before year-end. Which action accomplishes this for the 2024 tax year?
options: Paying next year's rent on an apartment
Buying a personal car
Receiving a year-end bonus
Making a deductible traditional IRA contribution before the filing deadline
questions.rationale: A deductible traditional IRA contribution reduces taxable income, while personal purchases and additional income do not.

questions.stem: A self-employed minister who has an approved exemption from self-employment tax (Form 4361) on ministerial earnings:
options: Pays SE tax on all income anyway
Is exempt from income tax as well
Does not pay SE tax on the exempt ministerial earnings
Must still pay income tax on the exempt amount and SE tax
questions.rationale: An approved Form 4361 exemption relieves a minister of SE tax on exempt ministerial earnings, though income tax still applies.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $600 in punitive damages and $20,000 in compensatory damages for a physical injury. What is taxable?
options: Both amounts
Neither amount
Only the $600 punitive damages
Only the $20,000 compensatory damages
questions.rationale: Punitive damages are generally taxable, while compensatory damages for physical injury are excluded from income.

questions.stem: A married couple filing jointly has modified AGI of $410,000 in 2024 with two qualifying children under 17. The Child Tax Credit begins to phase out above $400,000 MAGI for MFJ. By how much is their potential $4,000 credit reduced?
questions.rationale: The Child Tax Credit phases out $50 for each $1,000 (or fraction) of MAGI over the threshold; $10,000 over reduces the credit by $500.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sold stock held for 11 months at a gain. The gain is characterized as:
options: Ordinary dividend income
Short-term capital gain taxed at ordinary rates
Long-term capital gain
Tax-exempt
questions.rationale: Stock held for one year or less yields short-term capital gain, which is taxed at ordinary income rates.

questions.stem: A taxpayer realizes they will owe additional tax and wants more time to file. Filing Form 4868 provides:
options: An extension of time to file and to pay
An automatic extension of time to file, but not to pay
A waiver of all penalties
Six extra months to pay only
questions.rationale: Form 4868 extends the time to file but not the time to pay; tax owed is still due by the original deadline.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is a U.S. resident alien under the substantial presence test. They are taxed:
options: On worldwide income like a U.S. citizen
Not at all
Only on wages
Only on U.S.-source income
questions.rationale: A resident alien (meeting the substantial presence test) is taxed on worldwide income like a U.S. citizen.

questions.stem: A taxpayer and their unmarried partner each have their own qualifying child living in the same household. They want to maximize benefits. Which statement is correct about Head of Household?
options: Neither can be Head of Household if they live together
Both can be Head of Household if each pays more than half the cost of keeping up a home for their own qualifying child and meets the other requirements
Only one person per household can ever be Head of Household
Head of Household requires marriage
questions.rationale: Two unmarried taxpayers may each qualify for Head of Household if each maintains a separate household for their own qualifying person and meets the cost test.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: The Child and Dependent Care Credit is based on a percentage of qualifying expenses up to a maximum of:
options: $3,000 for one qualifying person and $6,000 for two or more
$5,000 for any number
$8,000 for one and $16,000 for two
$1,000 per person
questions.rationale: The Child and Dependent Care Credit applies to up to $3,000 of expenses for one qualifying person or $6,000 for two or more.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has $200,000 of wages and $60,000 of self-employment income in 2024 (single). The Additional Medicare Tax threshold for single filers is $200,000. The 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies to:
options: All $260,000 of earned income
The combined earned income over $200,000, here $60,000
Only the wages over $200,000
Only the self-employment income
questions.rationale: The 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies to combined wages and self-employment income exceeding the threshold; here the $60,000 excess is taxed.

questions.stem: A surviving spouse filing the decedent's final return who is due a refund and is not a court-appointed representative may need to file:
options: Form 709
Form 1310 (Statement of Person Claiming Refund Due a Deceased Taxpayer)
Form 706
Form 2555
questions.rationale: Form 1310 is used to claim a refund due a deceased taxpayer when the claimant is not a court-appointed personal representative.

questions.stem: A taxpayer holds a bond that pays $500 of tax-exempt municipal bond interest in 2024. How is this interest treated?
options: Fully taxable as ordinary income
Subject to self-employment tax
Taxed at capital gains rates
Excluded from gross income for federal tax, though reportable for informational purposes
questions.rationale: Interest on qualifying municipal bonds is excluded from federal gross income, though it is reported and can affect items like the taxable portion of Social Security.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $3,000 in ordinary dividends, all of which are qualified, and has taxable income placing them in the 15% capital gains bracket. The tax on the qualified dividends is:
questions.rationale: Qualified dividends are taxed at the applicable capital gains rate; $3,000 at 15% equals $450 of tax.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to make a qualified charitable distribution (QCD) from an IRA in 2024. Which statement is correct?
options: A taxpayer age 70 1/2 or older may directly transfer up to $105,000 (2024) from an IRA to a qualified charity, excluded from income
QCDs are limited to $1,000 per year
QCDs are fully taxable but deductible
Anyone of any age may make a QCD
questions.rationale: A QCD lets a taxpayer 70 1/2 or older transfer up to $105,000 (2024) directly from an IRA to charity, excluded from income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer paid $5,000 of qualified education expenses for a graduate program. They cannot claim the AOTC because it is graduate-level and beyond four years. Which credit may still be available?
options: Saver's Credit
American Opportunity Tax Credit
Child Tax Credit
Lifetime Learning Credit
questions.rationale: The Lifetime Learning Credit applies to graduate and continuing education, unlike the AOTC, which is limited to the first four years of undergraduate study.

questions.stem: The basis of property received as a gift, for purposes of determining gain, is generally:
options: The fair market value on the date of the gift
The donor's adjusted basis (carryover basis)
The amount the donee paid
Zero
questions.rationale: For gifted property, the donee generally uses the donor's adjusted basis (carryover basis) to determine gain.

questions.stem: A taxpayer realizes in November 2024 that their withholding will leave them owing $4,000 at filing. To avoid a penalty using the safe harbor, which is the most reliable approach if they cannot increase withholding?
options: Ignore it because penalties are rare
Wait and pay it all in April
File late to delay the penalty
Make a fourth-quarter estimated payment and consider annualizing income to match payments to when income was earned
questions.rationale: A timely estimated payment plus annualizing income (Form 2210) can align payments with when income was earned and reduce underpayment penalties.

questions.stem: A taxpayer claims the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion and also has foreign taxes paid on the excluded income. Can they also take a Foreign Tax Credit on that same excluded income?
options: Yes, without any limitation
Yes, fully
Yes, but only half
No, foreign taxes attributable to excluded foreign earned income cannot also generate a Foreign Tax Credit
questions.rationale: Foreign taxes attributable to income excluded under the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion cannot also be claimed as a Foreign Tax Credit; no double benefit is allowed.

questions.stem: For 2024, the gross income filing threshold for a single taxpayer under 65 is generally equal to:
options: The standard deduction for that filing status ($14,600)
The personal exemption amount
questions.rationale: The gross income filing threshold generally equals the standard deduction; for a single filer under 65 in 2024 that is $14,600.
questions.source: Part 1 – Preliminary Work and Taxpayer Data

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $1,000 in dividends that were reported as 'ordinary dividends' on a 1099-DIV but none were 'qualified.' How are they taxed?
options: Tax-exempt
At ordinary income tax rates
At long-term capital gains rates
At a flat 28% rate
questions.rationale: Ordinary (nonqualified) dividends are taxed at ordinary income tax rates, not preferential capital gains rates.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to claim both the American Opportunity Tax Credit and a tax-free 529 distribution for the same student. What is the key rule?
options: 529 distributions disqualify any education credit
The AOTC disqualifies any 529 use
They can use the same expenses for both
The same expenses cannot be used for both benefits; expenses must be allocated to avoid double-dipping
questions.rationale: Education benefits cannot be claimed on the same expenses; the AOTC and tax-free 529 distributions must use separate qualified expenses.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has rental property that is a passive activity and has $40,000 of suspended passive losses. They sell the entire interest in the activity in a fully taxable transaction in 2024. What happens to the suspended losses?
options: Half are allowed
They carry forward another year
They are permanently lost
They are generally allowed in full in the year of the complete disposition
questions.rationale: Upon a fully taxable disposition of an entire passive activity, previously suspended passive losses are generally allowed in full.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who is a dual-status alien (part of the year nonresident, part resident) for 2024 must:
options: File only Form 1040
File as Head of Household automatically
Report income according to dual-status rules, generally taxed on worldwide income for the resident period and U.S.-source income for the nonresident period
Pay no U.S. tax
questions.rationale: A dual-status alien is taxed on worldwide income for the resident period and on U.S.-source income for the nonresident period.

questions.stem: A taxpayer contributed $4,000 to a traditional IRA and qualifies for the Saver's Credit at the 10% rate based on their AGI. The credit is based on a maximum of $2,000 of contributions per person. What is the Saver's Credit?
questions.rationale: The Saver's Credit applies a percentage to up to $2,000 of contributions per person; at 10%, that is a $200 credit.

questions.stem: A taxpayer cashed out an old employer's pension and received a Form 1099-R coded as a normal distribution. The taxpayer is age 65. The taxable amount shown is fully taxable. This distribution is:
options: Tax-free because of age
Subject to the 10% early withdrawal penalty
Ordinary income subject to income tax
A capital gain
questions.rationale: A taxable pension distribution is ordinary income; at age 65 there is no early withdrawal penalty.

questions.stem: A taxpayer materially participates in their S corporation business. Their share of the S corporation's ordinary business income is:
options: Not subject to self-employment tax, though reasonable wages must be paid as W-2 compensation
Subject to the 10% penalty
Tax-exempt
Subject to self-employment tax
questions.rationale: An S corporation shareholder's pass-through business income is not subject to SE tax, but reasonable wages must be paid and reported on a W-2.

questions.stem: Maria, age 30, lived apart from her spouse the entire 2024 tax year but is not legally separated. Her child lived with her all year and she paid all household costs. Her spouse refuses to file jointly. Which filing status may Maria use to claim head of household?
options: Single, because they live apart
Qualifying surviving spouse
Married filing jointly without spouse's consent
Head of household, because she is considered unmarried under the abandoned-spouse rules
questions.rationale: Under the abandoned-spouse rules, a married taxpayer who lived apart from the spouse for the last six months of the year and maintained a home for a qualifying child may be treated as unmarried and file head of household.

questions.stem: Two unmarried parents, Devon and Priya, live together with their child all year. Devon's AGI is $60,000 and Priya's is $48,000. They cannot agree who claims the child. Under the tie-breaker rules, who is entitled to claim the qualifying child?
options: Devon, because he has the higher AGI among the parents
They must split the dependency exemption equally
Neither, because they are not married
Priya, because she has the lower AGI
questions.rationale: When both claimants are the child's parents and cannot agree, the IRS tie-breaker awards the qualifying child to the parent with the higher AGI.

questions.stem: Grandmother Ruth, AGI $40,000, and the child's mother, AGI $25,000, both live with the child and both qualify to claim the child as a qualifying child. They cannot agree. Who is entitled to claim the child?
options: Whoever files first
They split the benefit
Ruth, because she has the higher AGI
The mother, because a parent always prevails over a non-parent who also qualifies
questions.rationale: When a parent and a non-parent both qualify to claim the same child, the parent always has priority regardless of who has the higher AGI.

questions.stem: Tom provided more than half the support of his 70-year-old father, whose only income was $4,800 of taxable pension and $9,000 of Social Security. For 2024, can Tom's father be claimed as a qualifying relative?
options: Yes, because the father's gross income is under the limit and Tom provided over half his support
No, because the father did not live with Tom
No, because the father received Social Security
No, because the father is over age 65
questions.rationale: A parent can be a qualifying relative without living with the taxpayer; only taxable gross income counts toward the gross income test, and nontaxable Social Security is excluded.

questions.stem: A noncustodial parent wants to claim the child tax credit for his daughter. The custodial parent signed Form 8332 releasing the exemption. Which benefit may the noncustodial parent NOT claim even with Form 8332?
options: The dependency for the qualifying child
The credit for other dependents if the child does not qualify for CTC
The child tax credit
Head of household filing status based on that child
questions.rationale: Form 8332 transfers only the dependency, child tax credit, and credit for other dependents. Head of household, EIC, and the child/dependent care credit remain with the custodial parent.

questions.stem: Lena's husband died on March 2, 2024. She has a dependent son and did not remarry. What is her most advantageous filing status for the 2024 return?
options: Single for 2024
Married filing jointly for 2024
Qualifying surviving spouse for 2024
Head of household for 2024
questions.rationale: For the year of a spouse's death, the survivor may file married filing jointly. Qualifying surviving spouse status applies to the following two tax years if a dependent child is maintained.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old full-time student earned $7,000 from a part-time job and lived with her parents all year, who provided over half her support. Can the parents claim her as a qualifying child for 2024?
options: Yes, but only if she agrees to be claimed
No, because her earned income exceeds $4,700
No, because she is over age 18
Yes, because as a full-time student under 24 she is not subject to a gross income test
questions.rationale: A qualifying child has no gross income test. A full-time student under 24 who does not provide more than half her own support can be claimed regardless of how much she earns.

questions.stem: Which of the following relatives must live with the taxpayer for the entire year to be claimed as a qualifying relative?
options: The taxpayer's grandchild
The taxpayer's mother
The taxpayer's cousin
The taxpayer's brother
questions.rationale: Certain relatives (parents, siblings, lineal descendants, etc.) qualify without living with the taxpayer. A cousin is not on that list, so a cousin must live with the taxpayer all year as a member of the household.

questions.stem: A taxpayer files head of household and claims a married daughter as a dependent. The daughter filed a joint return with her husband. In which situation can the taxpayer still claim her?
options: Only if the joint return was filed solely to claim a refund of withheld tax and neither spouse would owe tax filing separately
Only if the daughter is under age 19
Whenever the daughter lived with the taxpayer all year
Never, because a married person filing jointly can never be a dependent
questions.rationale: Generally a person who files a joint return cannot be claimed as a dependent, but an exception applies when the joint return is filed only to obtain a refund and neither spouse would owe tax on a separate return.

questions.stem: In a multiple support agreement, four siblings together provide 100% of their mother's support: Ann 40%, Bob 25%, Carl 20%, and Dan 15%. Who is eligible to claim the mother under a multiple support agreement?
options: Only Ann, because she provided over half
Any of Ann, Bob, or Carl, because each provided more than 10% and together they exceed 50%
All four siblings simultaneously
Only Dan, because he provided the least
questions.rationale: Under a multiple support agreement, when no one person provides over half the support, any contributor of more than 10% may claim the dependent if the others who contributed over 10% sign a waiver (Form 2120).

questions.stem: A U.S. citizen taxpayer wants to claim her foster child as a qualifying child. Which condition is required for the foster child to qualify?
options: The child must be related by blood
The foster child must be under age 13
The child must be placed with her by an authorized placement agency or court order
The taxpayer must receive no foster-care payments
questions.rationale: For tax purposes an eligible foster child is one placed with the taxpayer by an authorized placement agency or by court order; standard qualifying-child tests then apply.

questions.stem: A single taxpayer maintains a household and her elderly mother lives in a nursing home all year. The taxpayer pays more than half the cost of keeping up the mother's main home (the nursing home is the mother's residence). Can the taxpayer file head of household?
options: Yes, if the mother qualifies as the taxpayer's dependent and the taxpayer pays over half the cost of the mother's home
No, because the mother does not live with the taxpayer
Yes, but only if the mother has no income
No, head of household always requires the dependent to live in the taxpayer's home
questions.rationale: For head of household based on a dependent parent, the parent need not live with the taxpayer; the taxpayer must pay over half the cost of maintaining the parent's main home, which can include a nursing home.

questions.stem: For the credit for other dependents (ODC) on a 2024 return, what is the maximum credit per qualifying dependent who is not a qualifying child for the child tax credit?
questions.rationale: The credit for other dependents is a nonrefundable $500 per dependent who does not qualify for the child tax credit, such as a qualifying relative or a child over 17.

questions.stem: A taxpayer cashed Series EE U.S. savings bonds and paid qualified higher-education tuition for his daughter. His modified AGI is below the phase-out and he files jointly. To exclude the bond interest from income, which condition must be met?
options: The bonds must have been issued before the owner turned 18
The proceeds must be used for room and board
The bonds must be Series I only
The bond owner must have been at least 24 years old when the bonds were issued
questions.rationale: The education savings bond interest exclusion requires the bond owner to have been at least 24 before issuance, with proceeds used for qualified tuition and fees, subject to MAGI phase-outs.

questions.stem: A graduate student receives a $30,000 fellowship: $18,000 is designated for tuition and required fees, $7,000 for room and board, and $5,000 paid as compensation for required teaching duties. How much is taxable?
questions.rationale: Scholarship/fellowship amounts for tuition and required fees are tax-free for a degree candidate, but amounts for room and board and any compensation for services (teaching) are taxable.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $4,000 in gambling winnings from a casino and had $6,000 in documented gambling losses for the year. He does not itemize deductions. How are these reported?
options: Net $2,000 loss reduces other income
$4,000 winnings; $4,000 of losses offset directly on Schedule 1
$4,000 winnings as income; losses are not deductible because he takes the standard deduction
$0, because losses exceed winnings
questions.rationale: Gambling winnings are fully taxable income. Losses are deductible only as an itemized deduction up to winnings, so a taxpayer using the standard deduction deducts none of them.

questions.stem: Under the gambling 'session' method, a slot-machine gambler started a single session with $200, won and lost throughout, and cashed out $350. During that session his largest mid-session bankroll was $900. What is the reportable gain from this session?
options: $700, the peak bankroll minus the buy-in
$150, the cash-out minus the buy-in
$350, the entire cash-out
$0, because slot play is not taxable
questions.rationale: The session method measures gambling gain or loss per session as the net of what was put in versus cashed out, so $350 out minus $200 in equals a $150 reportable gain.

questions.stem: A divorce was finalized in 2017 and requires monthly alimony. In 2024 the payer paid $12,000 of qualifying alimony under that unmodified agreement. How is it treated on the 2024 returns?
options: Deductible by payer but tax-free to recipient
Deductible by the payer and taxable to the recipient
A nondeductible gift
Not deductible by payer and not income to recipient
questions.rationale: For divorce or separation agreements executed before 2019 and not modified to adopt the new treatment, alimony remains deductible by the payer and includible in the recipient's income.

questions.stem: A divorce decree executed in 2021 requires one ex-spouse to pay the other $1,500 per month. How is this alimony treated for 2024?
options: Half-deductible by the payer
Taxable only to the payer
Deductible by payer, taxable to recipient
Neither deductible by the payer nor taxable to the recipient
questions.rationale: Under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, alimony from agreements executed after 2018 is neither deductible by the payer nor taxable to the recipient.

questions.stem: An employee's employer provided $6,000 in dependent care benefits, all spent on qualifying day care, and the amount appears in box 10 of the W-2. The maximum excludable dependent care benefit for a married-filing-jointly employee in 2024 is $5,000. What is the result?
options: The full $6,000 is taxable
All $6,000 is excluded from wages
Nothing is taxable, but no dependent care credit may be claimed
$5,000 is excludable; the excess $1,000 must be added back to taxable wages
questions.rationale: Employer-provided dependent care benefits are excludable only up to $5,000 (MFJ); amounts above the limit are added back to the employee's taxable wages.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a Form 1099-C cancelling $20,000 of credit-card debt. Immediately before cancellation, his total liabilities were $80,000 and the FMV of his total assets was $70,000. How much of the canceled debt is excludable under the insolvency exclusion?
options: $0, because credit-card debt never qualifies
$70,000, the value of his assets
$10,000, limited to the amount of insolvency
$20,000, the entire canceled amount
questions.rationale: The insolvency exclusion is limited to the amount by which liabilities exceed the FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation; the rest of the canceled debt is taxable.

questions.stem: Which of the following canceled debts is generally NOT taxable as cancellation of debt income?
options: A reduced business loan negotiated with a bank
Debt canceled as a gift by a family member who never intended repayment
A forgiven personal credit-card balance for a solvent taxpayer
A settled medical-bill balance for a solvent taxpayer
questions.rationale: Debt forgiven out of love, affection, or generosity as a true gift is not cancellation of debt income; most other cancellations are taxable unless a specific exclusion applies.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a state income tax refund of $900 in 2024. In the prior year she used the standard deduction. How much of the refund is taxable in 2024?
options: Half the refund
questions.rationale: A state income tax refund is taxable only to the extent the taxpayer received a tax benefit from deducting state taxes as an itemized deduction in the prior year; a standard-deduction filer received no benefit.

questions.stem: A cash-basis individual landlord received in December 2024 a $1,200 advance rent payment for January 2025 and a $900 security deposit she must return at lease end. What amount is included in 2024 rental income?
questions.rationale: Advance rent is included in income in the year received, but a refundable security deposit is not income until the landlord is entitled to keep it.

questions.stem: A taxpayer engages in a side activity making crafts. Over five years she reported a profit in only one year and treats it as a hobby. In 2024 the hobby generated $3,000 of income and $4,200 of expenses. How are these reported on the 2024 return?
options: $3,000 income reported; hobby expenses are not deductible
Report nothing because it is a hobby
$3,000 income; $3,000 expenses deducted to break even
Net $1,200 loss deductible against other income
questions.rationale: Hobby income is reported in full, but related expenses are not deductible for tax years 2018 through 2025 because miscellaneous itemized deductions are suspended.

questions.stem: Which factor most strongly supports treating an activity as a business rather than a hobby under the relevant facts-and-circumstances test?
options: The taxpayer carries on the activity in a businesslike manner with complete records and intent to profit
The taxpayer has substantial income from other sources
The activity has never produced a profit
The taxpayer enjoys the activity
questions.rationale: The IRS evaluates many factors, but operating in a businesslike manner with complete records and an actual and honest profit objective strongly indicates a for-profit business.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $500 of interest on a money market account and $40 of interest credited to a frozen bank deposit that he cannot withdraw. How much interest is taxable in 2024?
questions.rationale: Interest is taxed when received or made available; interest credited to a frozen account the taxpayer cannot access is not currently includible.

questions.stem: A taxpayer holds a U.S. Treasury bill bought at a discount and a corporate bond with original issue discount (OID). Which statement about 2024 reporting is correct?
options: T-bill interest is subject to state income tax
