Yes, if he paid over half the cost of keeping up his father's home
questions.rationale: HOH requires being unmarried or considered unmarried, paying over half the cost of keeping up a home, and having a qualifying person.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's husband died in March. She did not remarry and has no dependents. How may she file for the year of his death?
options: Head of household, because she is now unmarried and keeps a home
Married filing jointly, reporting his income through the date of death
Single, because her spouse was not alive on December 31
Qualifying surviving spouse, starting in the year of his death
questions.rationale: Death of a spouse in the year: survivor may use MFJ for that year; the return is signed 'filing as surviving spouse'.

questions.stem: Peter is a U.S. citizen married to a nonresident alien who has no U.S. income. They want to file jointly. What must they do?
options: File Form 8840 to claim a closer connection to the United States
File Form 1040-NR jointly, since one spouse is a nonresident alien
Both spouses elect under section 6013(g) to treat him as a U.S. resident
Nothing is needed; the spouse of a U.S. citizen is automatically a resident alien
questions.rationale: Section 6013(g) election: statement attached to the first joint return; worldwide income of both spouses is taxed.

questions.stem: A citizen of Canada was physically present in the United States 120 days in each of 2023, 2024, and 2025. He holds no green card. Is he a U.S. resident alien for 2025 under the substantial presence test?
options: No; the weighted total is 180 days, below the 183-day threshold
Yes; he was present more than 31 days in the current year
Yes; 120 days three years running is automatically residency
No; Canadians are exempt from the substantial presence test
questions.rationale: Substantial presence: 31 days current year and 183 days under current + 1/3 prior + 1/6 second prior.

questions.stem: Which of the following alone makes an individual a U.S. resident alien for the entire calendar year, regardless of days spent in the United States?
options: Having a U.S. bank account and a U.S. mailing address
Filing Form W-8BEN with a U.S. bank to open an account
Being a lawful permanent resident (green card holder) at any time in the year
Owning a home in the United States for more than six months
questions.rationale: Residency tests: green card test and substantial presence test, plus first-year choice elections.

questions.stem: What is the due date of the FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) for calendar year 2025, and can it be extended?
options: April 15, 2026, with an automatic extension to October 15
December 31, 2026, filed together with Form 1040
April 15, 2026, with no extension available at all
June 15, 2026, with an automatic extension to December 15
questions.rationale: FBAR due date aligns to April 15 following the calendar year, automatic extension to October 15.

questions.stem: Which tax benefits require a paid preparer to complete and submit Form 8867, Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist, with the return?
options: EITC, CTC/ACTC/ODC, American opportunity credit, and head of household status
Only the earned income credit and the child tax credit
The standard deduction, the QBI deduction, and the foreign tax credit
Charitable deductions over $500 and the retirement savings credit
questions.rationale: Four due diligence requirements: complete the checklist, compute the credit, know the client, keep records for three years.

questions.stem: A client tells a preparer she is head of household and has two children, but her earnings look much higher than the amount she reports and she cannot explain how she supports the household. What is the preparer's obligation under the due diligence rules?
options: Report the client's inconsistent information to the IRS immediately
Make reasonable additional inquiries and document the answers before preparing the return
Refuse any engagement involving the earned income credit
Rely on the client's statements without question as long as they are signed
questions.rationale: Reasonable inquiries and contemporaneous documentation are central to due diligence and to avoiding the §6695(g) penalty.

questions.stem: How long must a paid preparer keep a copy of Form 8867 and the supporting worksheets for a return claiming an EITC?
options: One year from the date the return was filed with the IRS
Three years from the later of the due date or the date the return was filed
Until the client's refund has been received and the return accepted
Seven years from the due date of the return, including extensions
questions.rationale: Retain a copy of the return or list of clients (§6107(b)) and the due diligence records for three years.

questions.stem: A firm expects to file 25 individual income tax returns in the calendar year. Which statement about electronic filing is correct?
options: Yes, but only for returns on which the client expects a refund
No, e-filing is optional for every preparer regardless of volume
Yes, but only for corporate and partnership returns
Generally yes, unless the client elects in writing to file on paper
questions.rationale: The mandate applies to specified tax return preparers who expect to file 11 or more covered returns.

questions.stem: When must the taxpayer sign Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization, in relation to the transmission of the return?
options: After reviewing the return and before the return is transmitted
Any time within 30 days after the return is transmitted
Only if the return shows a balance due
Never; the preparer signs for the taxpayer
questions.rationale: ERO retains Form 8879 for three years from the return due date or the IRS received date, whichever is later.

questions.stem: Which dates are the due dates for individual estimated tax payments for a calendar-year taxpayer?
options: April 15, June 30, September 30, and December 31 of the same year
April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15 of the following year
April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 of the following year
March 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15 of the same year
questions.rationale: Weekend or holiday due dates move to the next business day.

questions.stem: A self-employed individual had net earnings from self-employment of $520 for the year and no other income. What is the filing requirement?
options: She must file only if she received a Form 1099-NEC
She must file only Schedule C, with no Form 1040
She does not need to file, because her income is below the standard deduction
She must file a return and pay SE tax because net SE earnings were $400 or more
questions.rationale: Net SE earnings = 92.35% of net profit; the $400 test is applied to net earnings from self-employment.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to know whether a filing requirement applies. Which factor does NOT determine whether an individual must file a federal income tax return?
options: The individual's age at the end of the tax year
The individual's state of residence
The individual's gross income for the tax year
The individual's filing status for the tax year
questions.rationale: Other triggers: net SE earnings of $400+, special taxes, advance payments of credits, and being a dependent with unearned income.

questions.stem: A preparer receives a signed Form 1099-R showing a distribution but the client says he did not receive one, and the amount shown looks inconsistent with his bank deposits. What is the appropriate course?
options: Report the form amount as shown without asking the client anything
File the return as is and wait for an IRS notice to sort it out
Ignore the Form 1099-R, because the client says it is wrong
Ask the client for documents, then correct the amount if the form looks wrong
questions.rationale: Reasonable inquiry and documented judgment protect both the client and the practitioner.

questions.stem: On December 28, an employee is handed a paycheck but does not cash it until January 3. In which year is the wages income reported by this cash-basis taxpayer?
options: The year it was earned, whether or not it had been received
The year he received it, under constructive receipt
The year the employer claims its deduction for the payroll
The year he cashed it, because that is when he had the cash
questions.rationale: Cash-basis taxpayers include income when actually or constructively received.

questions.stem: A tipped restaurant server receives $120 in cash tips during one month. When must the server report those tips to the employer?
options: Only tips over $500 for the month must be reported to the employer
By the 10th of the next month, if tips total $20 or more
Only at year end, on the tax return filed with Form 1040
Immediately after each shift, using a written tip report
questions.rationale: Tips are wages subject to FICA. Unreported tips are reported on Form 4137.

questions.stem: Which of the following interest is generally excluded from federal gross income?
options: Interest earned on a certificate of deposit at an insured bank
Interest on U.S. Treasury bills held for six months
Interest on a state or local government bond issued for a public purpose
Interest on a corporate bond issued by a large public company
questions.rationale: Muni bond interest is still reported on Form 1040 line 2a as tax-exempt interest, and may affect Social Security taxation.

questions.stem: To receive qualified dividend treatment on common stock, how long must a taxpayer generally hold the shares?
options: At least 30 days before the ex-dividend date arrives
At least 90 days within the 181-day period around the record date
More than one year in all cases, ending on the record date
More than 60 days during the 121-day period around the ex-dividend date
questions.rationale: Qualified dividends are taxed at 0%, 15%, or 20% depending on taxable income.

questions.stem: An investor sells stock held for exactly one year (bought on March 10, 2024 and sold on March 10, 2025) at a gain. How is the gain classified?
options: Long-term, since a full year has passed on the sale date
Section 1231 gain, since the stock was held for a year
Short-term, since long-term needs more than one year
Ordinary income, since the gain is not a capital gain
questions.rationale: Holding period: begins the day after acquisition and includes the day of disposition.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sells 100 shares of stock at a $2,000 loss on June 1 and buys 100 shares of the same stock on June 20. What is the tax result?
options: The loss is deferred until the new shares are sold, but the basis is unchanged
The loss is converted to ordinary loss
The loss is fully deductible in the year of sale
The loss is disallowed under the wash sale rule and added to the basis of the new shares
questions.rationale: Wash sale window: 30 days before through 30 days after the sale date (61 days total).

questions.stem: A taxpayer inherits stock from an aunt who bought it years ago, and sells it nine months after the aunt's death. How is any gain or loss treated?
options: Short-term, unless the aunt held it for more than one year
Ordinary income, since the property was received by inheritance
Short-term, since the taxpayer held the stock only nine months
Long-term, since inherited property is treated as held over a year
questions.rationale: Inherited property generally takes a basis equal to fair market value at death (or alternate valuation date).

questions.stem: Parents give their child stock with an adjusted basis of $10,000 and a fair market value of $6,000 at the time of the gift. The child later sells it for $4,000. What is the child's recognized loss?
options: $2,000, using the FMV at the gift date as basis for loss
$0, since property received by gift never produces a loss
$6,000, using the donor's $10,000 basis for the loss
$10,000, using the donor's basis for both gain and loss
questions.rationale: Dual basis rule: gain uses donor's basis; loss uses lower of donor's basis or FMV at gift. Sale between the two produces no gain or loss.

questions.stem: What are the ownership and use requirements for excluding gain on the sale of a main home?
options: Owned it at least five years and used it as a rental at least two years
Used it as a main home for at least ten years
Lived in it during the sale year only
Owned and used it as a main home for at least two of the five years before the sale
questions.rationale: Exclusion: up to $250,000 ($500,000 MFJ) if tests are met and no other §121 exclusion within two years.

questions.stem: A married couple filing jointly sold their main home for a $430,000 gain. Both spouses used the home as a main home for at least two years and neither claimed the exclusion in the prior two years. How much gain is taxable?
options: $0, because the gain does not exceed the $500,000 joint exclusion
$430,000, because the exclusion applies to gain over $500,000 only
questions.rationale: Report the sale on Form 8949/Schedule D only if the gain exceeds the exclusion or a Form 1099-S is received.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sold a home after claiming depreciation for a home office for several years. What is the effect on the §121 exclusion?
options: Gain from post-1997 depreciation cannot be excluded and is taxed up to 25%
The entire gain stays excludable because the home was a main home
The depreciation is added to the exclusion amount, increasing it
The exclusion is lost entirely for the sale because of the office use
questions.rationale: Report the depreciation gain on the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has $9,000 of net capital loss for the year and no other capital transactions. What is the maximum amount deductible against ordinary income, and what happens to the rest?
options: $1,500 now, with the remaining $7,500 carried forward
$9,000 in full, because capital losses are fully deductible
$3,000 now, with the remaining $6,000 expiring after five years
$3,000 now, with the remaining $6,000 carried forward indefinitely
questions.rationale: Capital loss carryover is figured on the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet in the Schedule D instructions.

questions.stem: A single taxpayer has modified AGI of $225,000, including $40,000 of net investment income. How does the net investment income tax (NIIT) apply?
options: 3.8% of $25,000, the excess of MAGI over $200,000
None, since the threshold for single filers is $250,000
3.8% of $225,000, the taxpayer's entire MAGI
3.8% of the full $40,000 of net investment income
questions.rationale: Thresholds: $200,000 single/HOH, $250,000 MFJ/QSS, $125,000 MFS. Not indexed for inflation.

questions.stem: A shareholder's section 1244 stock becomes worthless. She originally paid $80,000 for the stock as an individual and files as single. How much ordinary loss can she claim?
options: $80,000 ordinary, since all of it is section 1244 loss
$50,000 ordinary, with the other $30,000 a capital loss
$100,000 ordinary, using the joint filing limit
$30,000 ordinary, with the other $50,000 a capital loss
questions.rationale: §1244 requires original issuance to the individual and a domestic small business corporation.

questions.stem: Which property may be exchanged in a like-kind exchange under current section 1031?
options: Inventory and other property held for sale to customers
Business equipment such as machinery and vehicles
Real property held for business use or investment
Corporate stock and interests in a partnership
questions.rationale: Identify replacement property within 45 days and close within 180 days (or the due date of the return if earlier).

questions.stem: In a like-kind exchange of investment real estate, the taxpayer gives up property with an adjusted basis of $200,000 and receives like-kind property worth $350,000 plus $30,000 cash. What is the recognized gain?
options: $30,000, the cash boot received
$150,000, the gain on the property
$180,000, the full realized gain
$0, because the exchange is tax-free
questions.rationale: New basis = old basis + gain recognized − boot received, here $200,000.

questions.stem: A single filer has $20,000 of Social Security benefits, $14,000 of wages, and $1,000 of tax-exempt interest. How much of the Social Security benefits is taxable, if any?
options: $0, since provisional income does not exceed $25,000
$17,000, which is 85% of the benefits received
$10,000, which is half of the benefits
$20,000, which is all of the benefits received
questions.rationale: Base amounts: $25,000 single / $32,000 MFJ for the 50% tier and $34,000 / $44,000 for the 85% tier.

questions.stem: Which of the following is included in a recipient's gross income?
options: Child support received
A gift received from a friend
Unemployment compensation
Life insurance proceeds paid on the death of the insured
questions.rationale: Unemployment benefits are reported as other income on Schedule 1.

questions.stem: Under a divorce instrument executed in 2022, a taxpayer pays his former spouse $2,000 per month as alimony. How is it treated?
options: Deductible by the payer only if the recipient is a U.S. citizen
Not deductible by the payer and not income to the recipient
Deductible by the payer and taxable to the recipient
Taxable to the recipient only
questions.rationale: Pre-2019 instruments: alimony is deductible above the line by the payer and taxable to the recipient.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sells handmade crafts occasionally as a hobby, earning $4,000 of revenue and incurring $3,500 of related expenses. How is this reported?
options: Include the $4,000 in income; the expenses are not deductible
Report nothing, since hobby income is not taxable
Report $4,000 of income and deduct the $3,500 on Schedule A
Report only the $500 net profit as other income
questions.rationale: Factors for profit motive include manner of operation, expertise, time devoted, history of income, and expectation of asset appreciation.

questions.stem: A taxpayer with modified AGI of $120,000 who actively participates in rental real estate has a $30,000 rental loss. How much loss may she deduct under the special allowance?
options: $15,000, since the $25,000 allowance is cut by $10,000
$30,000, the entire rental loss
$0, since passive losses are never deductible
$25,000, the full special allowance
questions.rationale: The allowance is fully phased out at $150,000 MAGI ($75,000 MFS living apart).

questions.stem: What must a taxpayer show to qualify as a real estate professional under the passive activity rules?
options: Ownership of five or more rental properties during the tax year
Over 750 hours in real property trades, more than half of all personal service hours, and material participation
A real estate license and any amount of time spent in rental work
At least 500 hours of rental management and a state real estate license
questions.rationale: Real estate professionals can treat rental losses as nonpassive if they materially participate.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's $40,000 credit card debt is canceled by the lender while she is insolvent by $15,000 immediately before the cancellation. How much cancellation-of-debt income can she exclude?
options: $40,000, the full canceled debt
$15,000, the amount by which she was insolvent
$0, because only bankruptcy qualifies
questions.rationale: Exclusions: bankruptcy, insolvency (to extent of insolvency), qualified farm debt, qualified real property business debt, and certain student loan discharges.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a qualified distribution rule for a Roth IRA to be tax-free?
options: The distribution is due to the owner's disability and the five-year period is satisfied
The account has been open for at least five tax years and the owner is 59½ or older
Receiving the distribution within 12 months of making the first contribution
The distribution is due to the owner's death
questions.rationale: Contributions can always be withdrawn tax- and penalty-free because they are after-tax basis.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old withdraws $15,000 from a traditional IRA to pay for a first-time home purchase (the taxpayer has never owned a home in the prior two years). What is the penalty treatment?
options: No part is taxable or subject to the 10% additional tax
$10,000 is exempt from the 10% additional tax, but all $15,000 is taxable
The full $15,000 escapes the 10% additional tax but is taxed
The first-time homebuyer exception applies only to Roth IRAs
questions.rationale: Other exceptions: death, disability, SEPP, medical expenses over the floor, health insurance while unemployed, higher education expenses.

questions.stem: An IRA owner reached age 73 in 2025. By what date must the first required minimum distribution generally be taken, and what is the penalty for missing it?
options: April 1 of the next year; 25% excise tax, or 10% if corrected
April 15, 2026; no excise tax applies to a missed RMD
June 30, 2026; 6% excise tax on the shortfall
December 31, 2025; 50% excise tax on the shortfall
questions.rationale: Applicable age: 73 for those who turn 72 after 2022 and 73 before 2033; 75 for those born in 1960 or later.

questions.stem: An individual inherits a traditional IRA in 2025 from her uncle, who died before his required beginning date. She is not an eligible designated beneficiary. What distribution rule applies?
options: Entire balance emptied by the end of the tenth year after death
The entire balance must be distributed within 12 months
No distributions are ever required from an inherited IRA
Distributions may be stretched over her own life expectancy
questions.rationale: Eligible designated beneficiaries: surviving spouse, minor child of the owner, disabled, chronically ill, or not more than 10 years younger.

questions.stem: Which statement about incentive stock options (ISOs) is correct at the time of exercise?
options: No regular income, but the bargain element is an AMT adjustment
The employer deducts the bargain element in the year of exercise
The employee recognizes capital gain equal to the bargain element
The bargain element is wages subject to income tax withholding
questions.rationale: ISO details are reported on Form 3921; the AMT adjustment goes on Form 6251.

questions.stem: Under the general rule, how much qualified educational assistance can an employer provide to an employee tax-free under an educational assistance program?
options: Unlimited if the courses are job related
Up to $10,000 per year
Up to $5,250 per year
Up to $2,500 per year
questions.rationale: §127 programs must be a written plan and cannot favor highly compensated employees.

questions.stem: How is a nonqualified stock option (NQSO) generally taxed to an employee who exercises it when the stock is worth more than the exercise price?
options: No income arises until the employee sells the acquired stock
The spread is excluded from income if the stock is held one year
The spread is taxed as long-term capital gain at exercise
The spread is ordinary wages subject to withholding and FICA
questions.rationale: Employer withholds income tax and FICA, and reports the income on Form W-2.

questions.stem: A taxpayer meets the physical presence test for the foreign earned income exclusion. What does that test require?
options: Ownership of a foreign home for at least one full year
Residence in a foreign country for 330 days of the calendar year
183 days abroad within the calendar year of the claim
330 full days in foreign countries within any 12 consecutive months
questions.rationale: Alternatively, the bona fide residence test requires an uninterrupted period including an entire tax year.

questions.stem: How does an employer-provided achievement award or cash gift to an employee generally affect the employee's income?
options: Cash gifts are excluded if the employee did not request them
Cash gifts are excluded if given at holidays
Cash gifts under $500 are excluded as de minimis fringe benefits
Cash and cash equivalents are taxable wages regardless of amount
questions.rationale: Examples of de minimis benefits: occasional snacks, coffee, personal use of a copier, occasional tickets.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sells property under an installment sale: selling price $200,000, adjusted basis $120,000, and receives $40,000 in the year of sale. What gain is recognized that year?
options: $40,000, because all payments received are gain
$0, because installment sales are never taxed until the final payment
$80,000, because gain is recognized up front
$16,000, using a gross profit percentage of 40%
questions.rationale: Use Form 6252 to report. Depreciation recapture is recognized in the year of sale.

questions.stem: Spouses file married filing separately. One spouse itemizes deductions. What must the other spouse do?
options: Choose either method independently of the other spouse
Take the standard deduction regardless of what the spouse does
Itemize as well, because the standard deduction is zero
Take half of the regular standard deduction amount
questions.rationale: Itemizers on MFS must also use the same method as each other for deductions related to the community property rules.

questions.stem: For itemized deductions, medical expenses are deductible only to the extent they exceed what percentage of AGI?
questions.rationale: Deductible items include insurance premiums, doctor and hospital fees, prescription drugs, and travel for care.

questions.stem: What is the limit on the amount of acquisition debt on which a taxpayer can deduct mortgage interest for loans taken out after December 15, 2017?
options: $1,000,000 total for all loans originated after December 15, 2017
No limit applies if the loan is a first mortgage
$750,000 total ($375,000 if married filing separately)
$500,000 total on a main home and one second home
questions.rationale: Home equity interest is deductible only if the loan is used to buy, build, or substantially improve the home that secures it.

questions.stem: A taxpayer takes out a home equity line of credit and uses the money to pay off credit cards and buy a car. How is the interest treated?
options: Deductible up to $100,000 of home equity debt
Not deductible as mortgage interest, since it didn't buy or improve the home
Fully deductible as home mortgage interest, since the loan is secured by the home
Deductible as investment interest on Form 4952
questions.rationale: Tracing rules determine the use of the loan proceeds.

questions.stem: A donor makes a single cash contribution of $300 to a qualified charity. What substantiation is required to claim the deduction?
options: A canceled check alone is enough for any amount
No documentation is needed for gifts under $500
A contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charity
A Form 8283 must be attached for every gift over $250
questions.rationale: Noncash gifts: over $500 requires Form 8283; over $5,000 generally requires a qualified appraisal.

questions.stem: A taxpayer donates long-term appreciated stock to a public charity. What are the deduction and the percentage-of-AGI limit?
options: FMV, limited to 50% of AGI, with no carryover of any excess
Adjusted basis, limited to 60% of AGI, with a five-year carryover
FMV, with no limit based on the donor's AGI
FMV, limited to 30% of AGI, with a five-year carryover
questions.rationale: Cash to public charities: 60% of AGI; capital gain property: 30%; private non-operating foundations: 30% cash, 20% property.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT deductible as a charitable contribution?
options: Unreimbursed out-of-pocket costs of supplies purchased for a charity
Cash given to a church
The value of volunteer time donated to a qualified charity
Mileage at the charitable rate while driving for a charity
questions.rationale: Contributions to individuals, political groups, and for-profit entities are also not deductible.

questions.stem: What is the annual maximum student loan interest deduction, and who cannot claim it?
options: $5,000, with no income limit on who can claim it
$2,500, reduced by a MAGI phase-out; not allowed if MFS
$2,500, available only to taxpayers filing married filing separately
Unlimited, if the loan was used for graduate school
questions.rationale: The loan must be for qualified education expenses of the taxpayer, spouse, or dependent.

questions.stem: A single taxpayer covered by a workplace retirement plan makes a traditional IRA contribution. When is the deduction reduced or eliminated?
options: Only if the taxpayer also contributes to a Roth IRA in the same year
MAGI above the phase-out range for the taxpayer's filing status
Never; a covered taxpayer may always deduct the full contribution
Only if the taxpayer is older than 50 at the end of the year
questions.rationale: Nondeductible contributions are tracked on Form 8606. Spousal IRA rules apply when the other spouse is covered.

questions.stem: Which statement about a Health Savings Account (HSA) is correct?
options: Deductible above the line, grows tax-free, and tax-free for qualified medical use
Anyone who has any health insurance coverage may contribute
Deductible only as an itemized deduction on Schedule A
Distributions are tax-free when used for any expense
questions.rationale: Report on Form 8889. Employer contributions are excluded from wages.

questions.stem: Which of these taxpayers is NOT allowed the self-employed health insurance deduction for a month?
options: A sole proprietor who buys his own plan on the health insurance marketplace
A partner who pays premiums for her own plan, reported as guaranteed payments
A self-employed person eligible for a subsidized plan through a spouse's employer
A more-than-2% S corporation shareholder whose premiums are included in W-2 wages
questions.rationale: The deduction is taken above the line on Schedule 1 and reduces income tax, not SE tax.

questions.stem: To claim the child tax credit for a qualifying child, which requirement applies to the child?
options: The child must have lived with the taxpayer fewer than six months
An ITIN is enough to qualify the child for the full credit
The child must be age 18 or older at the close of the tax year
A Social Security number valid for employment, issued by the return due date
questions.rationale: The ACTC is the refundable portion, limited by earned income above a threshold.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wishes to claim the earned income credit. Which rule applies?
options: Nonresident aliens always qualify without making any election
Any amount of earned income qualifies, with no upper limit
Married filing separately status is always allowed to claim it
Investment income under the annual limit and a valid SSN
questions.rationale: Taxpayers without qualifying children must be age 25 to 64 and not be dependents.

questions.stem: A student pays $4,000 of qualified tuition during the student's first year of college. Which is the maximum American opportunity tax credit (AOTC) for this student, and how much of it may be refundable?
options: $2,000, all of it nonrefundable
$2,500, with up to $1,000 refundable
$1,000, fully nonrefundable against tax
$4,000, fully refundable to the taxpayer
questions.rationale: AOTC applies to the first four years of postsecondary education; the student must be enrolled at least half-time.

questions.stem: A married couple, both working full-time, paid $9,000 to a daycare center for their two children under age 13. What is the maximum amount of expenses that can be used to figure the child and dependent care credit?
options: $9,000, the full amount paid to the daycare center
$6,000, the cap for two or more qualifying persons
$3,000, the cap for one qualifying person
$4,000, half of the combined earned income
questions.rationale: Expenses are also limited to the lower earned income of the spouses. Employer-provided benefits reduce the limit.

questions.stem: A taxpayer paid $2,500 of foreign income tax on passive income reported on Form 1099-DIV. What is true about claiming the foreign tax credit without Form 1116?
options: Always allowed on Form 1040 without filing Form 1116 at any amount
Never allowed, since the credit always requires filing Form 1116
Allowed only if foreign taxes are $300 or less ($600 MFJ) and all income is passive
Allowed up to $5,000 of foreign taxes with no other conditions
questions.rationale: Taxpayers can alternatively deduct foreign taxes as an itemized deduction.

questions.stem: A taxpayer received advance premium tax credit payments during the year that exceeded the credit calculated on his return. What happens?
options: He must amend the prior year return to reflect the excess
No repayment is required once the advance payment is made
The excess is treated as a gift from the government
He repays the excess advance payments on Form 8962, subject to any cap
questions.rationale: Forms 1095-A from the marketplace provide the data needed for Form 8962.

questions.stem: Under current law, when is a personal casualty loss deductible by an individual itemizer?
options: Any loss over $500, with no limit based on AGI
Only when insurance was unavailable, up to the full amount of the loss
A federally declared disaster loss, after the $100 and 10% of AGI reductions
Whenever the property is damaged by any event, with no floor
questions.rationale: Insurance reimbursements reduce the loss. Business casualty losses follow different rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following employees can still deduct unreimbursed employee business expenses on Schedule 1 despite the suspension of miscellaneous itemized deductions?
options: A performing artist who meets the income and expense tests
A salaried sales employee who drives a personal car for work
A teacher who buys classroom decorations and supplies
A nurse who buys her own scrubs and shoes for work
questions.rationale: Reimbursements under an accountable plan are the usual way to cover employee costs.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has $12,000 of investment interest expense and $8,000 of net investment income for the year. How is the excess treated?
options: None of the interest is deductible because of the limit
$8,000 is deductible; the other $4,000 is carried forward
All $12,000 is deductible as an itemized deduction
$4,000 is deductible; the other $8,000 is lost
questions.rationale: Qualified dividends and net capital gain can be included in net investment income only if the taxpayer elects to tax them at ordinary rates.

questions.stem: A sole proprietor bought equipment for $50,000, claimed $30,000 of depreciation, and sold it for $45,000. How is the gain on the sale characterized?
options: $15,000 ordinary income and $10,000 section 1231 gain
$25,000 of ordinary income under section 1245 recapture
$30,000 of ordinary income equal to the depreciation taken
$25,000 of long-term capital gain under section 1231
questions.rationale: Section 1245 recapture = lesser of gain or depreciation allowed; reported on Form 4797 Part III.

questions.stem: An investor sells a rental building for $520,000. It cost $400,000, and straight-line depreciation of $80,000 was taken. What is the tax character of the $200,000 gain?
options: $200,000 of §1231 gain, all taxed at the 0%, 15% or 20% rates
$80,000 ordinary income recapture and $120,000 §1231 gain
$120,000 unrecaptured §1250 gain and $80,000 §1231 gain
$80,000 unrecaptured §1250 gain (25% max) and $120,000 §1231 gain
questions.rationale: Report on Form 4797 and the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet in the Schedule D instructions.

questions.stem: Parents want to report their 10-year-old child's income on their own return using Form 8814. Which condition must be met?
options: The child's income is only interest and dividends, under the limit
The child has wages from a part-time job and no investment income
The child has made estimated tax payments during the year
The child's gross income is more than the standard deduction
questions.rationale: Parents' election means the child files no return, but the parents may owe tax on the child's income at the parent's rate.

questions.stem: A homeowner pays a nanny $1,500 per calendar quarter in cash wages during the year. Which statement about the household employer's federal unemployment tax (FUTA) is correct?
options: FUTA applies because wages hit $1,000 in a quarter; report on Schedule H
FUTA applies only if wages exceed $10,000 for the year
FUTA never applies to household workers of any kind
FUTA applies, and it is reported on Form 941 each quarter
questions.rationale: FICA applies if cash wages reach the annual household threshold, which is indexed. Schedule H also reports withheld income tax.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has a $100,000 net operating loss from 2023 and taxable income before the NOL deduction of $90,000 in 2024. What is the NOL deduction allowed for 2024?
options: $90,000, which eliminates all taxable income
$72,000, because the deduction is limited to 80% of taxable income
$45,000, because the NOL is limited to 50% of taxable income
$100,000, creating a new NOL for 2024
questions.rationale: Most post-2020 NOLs cannot be carried back and carry forward indefinitely; farming losses have a two-year carryback.

questions.stem: Which taxpayer may elect to use Schedule J to average farm income over the three prior years?
options: A farmer or fisherman with elected farm income
A retiree with large IRA withdrawals
A real estate investor with capital gains
A salaried employee with a bonus
questions.rationale: The election is made on a year-by-year basis and may lower tax if prior-year brackets were lower.

questions.stem: A single taxpayer has taxable income of $85,000 and no qualified dividends or net capital gain. How is the regular tax generally figured?
options: Using Schedule D, because the taxpayer has income above $75,000
Using the Tax Rate Schedules, because income exceeds $50,000
From the Tax Table, because taxable income is under $100,000
Using Form 6251, because income exceeds the AMT exemption
questions.rationale: Qualified dividends and capital gains require the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet.

questions.stem: Which statement about the alternative minimum tax (AMT) is correct?
options: AMT applies only to corporations with income over $10,000,000
AMT is owed on top of regular tax and can never be credited later
AMT uses the same graduated rates as regular tax with no exemption
AMT uses 26% and 28% rates, with an exemption that phases out
questions.rationale: AMT is owed only to the extent tentative minimum tax exceeds regular tax.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old converts $20,000 from a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA, then withdraws the converted $20,000 two years later. What is the tax result for the withdrawal?
options: The 10% additional tax applies, since it came out within five years
A 25% additional tax applies, as for a SIMPLE IRA within two years
Ordinary income tax applies again to the full $20,000 withdrawn
No tax or penalty applies, since it is a return of converted funds
questions.rationale: Ordering rules: contributions first, then conversions (oldest first), then earnings.

questions.stem: An employee takes a lump-sum distribution from a 401(k) that includes employer stock with a cost basis of $20,000 and a value of $100,000. If the stock is distributed in kind, how is the net unrealized appreciation (NUA) treated?
options: The $80,000 NUA is taxed as ordinary income at distribution
The $80,000 NUA is taxed at 10% under a special lump-sum rule
The $80,000 NUA is never taxed because the plan is qualified
The $80,000 NUA is taxed as long-term capital gain when the stock is sold
questions.rationale: Appreciation after distribution is short- or long-term based on the holding period from the distribution date.

questions.stem: A dependent child has $800 of interest income and $3,000 of wages. How is the child's standard deduction generally determined?
options: The full regular standard deduction, regardless of earned income
Zero, since a dependent can never claim a standard deduction
The greater of a set minimum or earned income plus an add-on, capped
Only the earned income, with no minimum amount at all
questions.rationale: Dependents who can be claimed by another taxpayer check the box on Form 1040 and use the limited standard deduction.

questions.stem: A self-employed individual with net earnings of $100,000 after the self-employment tax deduction wants to contribute to a SEP-IRA. What is the maximum contribution percentage of net earnings?
options: 10% of net earnings from self-employment after the SE deduction
50% of net earnings from self-employment after the SE deduction
25% of net earnings from self-employment, with no other adjustment
20% of net earnings after the SE tax deduction
questions.rationale: Contributions are deductible above the line on Schedule 1 and can be made up to the due date of the return, including extensions.

questions.stem: For 2025, what is the standard deduction for a married couple filing jointly, neither spouse age 65 or blind, under current law?
questions.rationale: Additional standard deduction amounts for age 65 or blind are added per eligible taxpayer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the deduction for qualified tips for 2025?
options: It applies only to itemizers and is limited to $5,000
It applies to all tipped income without any occupation requirement
It is a credit that is refundable against self-employment tax
Up to $25,000, for itemizers or not, phasing out above $150,000 MAGI
questions.rationale: Qualified tips must be voluntary and reported on W-2, 1099, or Form 4137.

questions.stem: A married couple filing jointly has a $20,000 qualified overtime premium and MAGI of $120,000. What is true about the overtime deduction for 2025?
options: Up to $25,000 joint, so the full $20,000 premium is deductible
Up to $12,500 for the couple, so only $12,500 is allowed
The entire overtime wage amount is deductible with no limit
Nothing is deductible, because they must itemize to claim it
questions.rationale: The deduction is for tax years 2025 through 2028 and requires a valid SSN.

questions.stem: For 2025, an unmarried taxpayer age 67 with MAGI of $60,000 qualifies for which additional deduction under the 2025 tax act?
options: An extra $6,000 deduction, in addition to the age-65 standard deduction
No extra deduction, since it is available only to joint filers
A $12,000 deduction for any single taxpayer age 65 or older
A $6,000 credit that replaces the additional standard deduction
questions.rationale: The deduction is available to itemizers and non-itemizers.

questions.stem: Under the 2025 tax act, what is the state and local tax (SALT) itemized deduction cap for 2025 for a taxpayer with MAGI of $300,000 who is not married filing separately?
options: No cap applies
questions.rationale: Married filing separately has half the cap ($20,000 for 2025).

questions.stem: What is the Form 1099-K reporting threshold for third-party settlement organizations under current law (as restored by the 2025 tax act)?
options: $5,000 with no transaction minimum
$2,500 with more than 100 transactions
$600 with no transaction minimum
More than $20,000 in payments and more than 200 transactions
questions.rationale: All income is taxable even if no 1099-K is issued.

questions.stem: A farmer who receives at least two-thirds of gross income from farming may avoid the estimated tax penalty in which way?
options: Pay 50% of the prior-year tax by June 15 of the following year
Pay nothing until the return is filed on the extended October 15 date
Make four equal estimated payments on the regular due dates only
File and pay all tax by March 1, or pay one installment by January 15
questions.rationale: The test is two-thirds of gross income from farming in the current or prior year.

questions.stem: A payer must begin backup withholding on a payee who fails to provide a taxpayer identification number. What is the backup withholding rate?
questions.rationale: Payees can avoid backup withholding by providing a correct TIN on Form W-9.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's business equipment is destroyed in a fire, and the insurance proceeds exceed the adjusted basis. What allows deferral of the gain?
options: Replace the property with similar property within two years (§1033)
Deduct the gain in the year as a casualty loss on Form 4684
Replace it with any property within 45 days under §1031
Elect installment treatment for the insurance proceeds received
questions.rationale: Report on Form 4797 or Form 4684 depending on the property.

questions.stem: Under the rules for qualified small business stock issued after July 4, 2025, a noncorporate taxpayer sells QSBS held for four years. What percentage of the gain can generally be excluded?
options: 0%, because five years is required
questions.rationale: The per-issuer cap is $15 million (indexed) or 10 times basis, and the gross assets test is $75 million.

questions.stem: A taxpayer filed her 2022 return on April 15, 2023, and paid all tax then. She wants to claim a refund for an error. By what date must she file Form 1040-X to preserve the refund?
options: April 15, 2026, which is three years from the filing date
April 15, 2025, which is two years after filing
April 15, 2029, which is six years after filing
There is no deadline for claiming a refund
questions.rationale: Claims for refunds based on bad debts or worthless securities have a seven-year period.

questions.stem: The IRS generally has three years to assess additional tax after a return is filed. In which situation does the assessment period extend to six years?
options: The taxpayer later received a CP2000 notice from the IRS
The return omits over 25% of the gross income shown on the return
The taxpayer claimed an earned income credit on the return
The return was filed more than 30 days after the due date
questions.rationale: The statute for assessment (ASED) typically ties to the return filing date, with early returns treated as filed on the due date.

questions.stem: A client cannot pay her balance due in full but owes less than $50,000. Which IRS option lets her request monthly payments?
options: Wait for the IRS to levy her wages and then pay
File Form 9465 or apply online for an installment agreement
Submit Form 656 to settle for less than owed without any financial data
Request an extension of time to file on Form 4868
questions.rationale: The failure-to-pay penalty rate drops from 0.5% to 0.25% per month while an approved installment agreement is in effect, if the return was filed timely.

questions.stem: What is the interest rate on underpayments of tax, and how is it computed?
options: The prime rate plus 1 percentage point, compounded annually
The federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points, compounded daily
A fixed 6% simple interest rate
The federal short-term rate with no addition, compounded monthly
questions.rationale: Interest is not abated by reasonable cause, but may be reduced when the penalty is abated or if the IRS caused the delay.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who filed on time but did not pay the tax due by the due date is assessed the failure-to-pay penalty. What is the monthly rate?
options: 0.25% of the unpaid tax per month, up to a maximum of 50%
1% of the unpaid tax per month, up to a maximum of 100%
0.5% of the unpaid tax per month, up to a maximum of 25%
5% of the unpaid tax per month, up to a maximum of 25%
questions.rationale: Combined, the failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalties reach 5% per month for the first five months.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is suffering a significant hardship from an IRS collection action and the usual channels have failed to resolve the problem. What can she submit to the Taxpayer Advocate Service?
options: Form 8821, Tax Information Authorization
Form 843, Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement
Form 911, Request for Taxpayer Advocate Service Assistance
Form 12153, Request for a Collection Due Process Hearing
questions.rationale: Taxpayers experiencing economic harm or systemic problems can contact TAS.

questions.stem: A taxpayer moved after filing her return. Which form notifies the IRS of the new address?
options: Form 4506-T, Request for Transcript
Form 8821, Tax Information Authorization
Form 8822, Change of Address
Form 2848, Power of Attorney
questions.rationale: A return filed with a new address can also update the address, but Form 8822 is the standard method.

questions.stem: A client is just under the threshold to itemize and also gives to charity each year. Which strategy may increase the tax benefit of her giving?
options: Donate her services instead of property to the charity
Bunch two years of gifts into one year, then take the standard deduction
Give the same amount to charity every year, in cash
Skip giving until she retires, then give a large amount
questions.rationale: Gifts of appreciated stock held over a year avoid capital gains tax and are deductible at fair market value.

questions.stem: A client opened a 529 plan for her grandchild 15 years ago. Under SECURE 2.0, what is true about rolling leftover funds into the beneficiary's Roth IRA?
options: The rollover is allowed only into the beneficiary's traditional IRA
The 529 has been open 15 years; lifetime cap $35,000, within Roth limits
The beneficiary must be age 59½ before any rollover is allowed
The 529 has been open one year, and the rollover amount is unlimited
questions.rationale: The beneficiary must have earned income at least equal to the rollover amount.

questions.stem: A grandparent wants to front-load five years of annual gift exclusions into a 529 plan for a grandchild. Which election permits this treatment?
options: An election to treat the gift as a loan on Form 8996
A section 1031 election on Form 8824
A QCD election on Form 1040
A five-year gift averaging election on Form 709
questions.rationale: If the donor dies before the five years end, part of the contribution returns to the estate.

questions.stem: Beginning in 2025, a participant in a 401(k) plan who is age 61 may make a higher catch-up contribution. What is that higher catch-up limit based on?
options: An unlimited catch-up, for participants age 60 or older
The greater of $10,000 or 150% of regular catch-up, at ages 60–63
The same as the regular catch-up, at every age over 50
Double the regular catch-up, for anyone age 50 or older
questions.rationale: Starting in 2026, catch-up contributions by employees with prior-year FICA wages above an indexed amount must be made as Roth contributions.

questions.stem: A widow's late husband did not use all of his estate tax exemption. Which election lets the surviving spouse use the unused portion?
options: Portability election on a timely filed Form 706 (DSUE)
Section 6013(g) election made on the joint Form 1040
QTIP election made on Form 709 at the time of the gift
Section 754 election made on the partnership's Form 1065
questions.rationale: Late portability relief is available up to five years after death for estates not otherwise required to file.

questions.stem: An employee wants to exempt herself from federal income tax withholding for the year on Form W-4. What must be true, and how long does the exemption last?
options: She earns under $30,000 a year, and it lasts for three years
She is a full-time student, and it lasts until she changes jobs
She expects a refund this year, and the exemption never expires
No tax last year, none expected this year; expires February 15
questions.rationale: FICA taxes are still withheld even if income tax withholding is exempt.

questions.stem: A client's income this year was unusually low and she is considering converting a traditional IRA to a Roth. What is the main reason to convert in a low-income year?
options: The conversion avoids all tax on the pre-tax balance converted
The converted amount is taxed at a lower rate now, and later qualified withdrawals are tax-free
Roth conversions are deductible in the year of the conversion
Conversions can be undone at any time through recharacterization
questions.rationale: Consider the effect on Medicare premiums (IRMAA), the NIIT, and credits that phase out with MAGI.

questions.stem: Which life event allows a taxpayer to change her health coverage outside the open enrollment period and may affect her premium tax credit?
options: A change in her preferred doctor or hospital network
Reaching age 30, the threshold for adult coverage
A desire to switch plans after a new medical diagnosis
A qualifying event such as marriage, birth, or loss of other coverage
questions.rationale: Reconcile advance payments on Form 8962 at filing.

questions.stem: A client asks whether she should make estimated payments or increase her paycheck withholding to cover tax on freelance income. Which statement about withholding is accurate?
options: Withholding is treated as paid evenly through the year
Withholding is applied only to the January installment
Withholding is not counted toward the underpayment safe harbor
Withholding is treated as paid on the date it left the paycheck
questions.rationale: IRA rollover trustee-to-trustee transfers can also be treated as withholding in certain cases.

questions.stem: A client's income is temporarily high from a one-time stock sale. Which strategy could lower the tax on the gain?
options: Ask the buyer to pay the amount as wages instead
Sell the stock before holding it for more than one year
Harvest capital losses on other holdings to offset the gain
Realize additional short-term gains in the same tax year
questions.rationale: Avoid wash sales on loss harvesting by waiting more than 30 days to repurchase.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a limitation of an ABLE account?
options: The account must be owned by a parent of the beneficiary
Contributions are deductible on the federal return
Disability must begin before a set age, which is 46 starting in 2026
Distributions for housing are always taxed to the beneficiary
questions.rationale: Annual contributions are limited to the gift tax annual exclusion, with extra contributions possible for working beneficiaries.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a simple trust for income tax purposes?
options: A trust that must distribute all income currently, with no charity or principal payments
A trust that is treated as owned by its grantor
A trust whose only beneficiary is a qualified charity
A trust that may accumulate income and make principal distributions
questions.rationale: A complex trust gets a $100 exemption; an estate gets $600.

questions.stem: A trustee of a complex trust makes a distribution on February 20 and elects to treat it as made in the prior tax year. What is the election called, and how long does it last?
options: The 120-day rule: available to estates only
The 90-day rule: first-quarter distributions count as made in the prior year
The 65-day rule: first-65-day distributions count as made on December 31
The 30-day rule: available to simple trusts only
questions.rationale: This helps shift income to beneficiaries in lower brackets and deduct distributions through DNI.

questions.stem: A taxpayer gives her daughter $50,000 in cash in 2025. Which filing requirement applies if she has made no prior taxable gifts and is married to a U.S. citizen who does not join in the gift?
options: No gift return is needed, since the gift is to a family member
File Form 1040-GIFT and pay gift tax at a flat 40% rate
File Form 709 because the gift exceeds the exclusion; no tax is likely owed
Report the gift on Schedule A of her income tax return
questions.rationale: Spouses can elect gift splitting on Form 709 to use both annual exclusions.

questions.stem: A nonresident alien (not a U.S. trade or business filer) receives $10,000 in U.S.-source dividends. What is the default federal withholding treatment?
options: 30% on the gross amount, unless a treaty rate applies (Form W-8BEN)
Graduated rates, using the regular tax tables
None, since dividends are exempt for nonresident aliens
24% backup withholding on the gross amount
questions.rationale: Portfolio interest and certain capital gains of NRAs are generally exempt.

questions.stem: A foreign person sells U.S. real property for $600,000. What withholding applies under FIRPTA, and who is responsible?
options: The seller withholds 30% of the gain and remits it
The buyer withholds 15% of the amount realized and remits it
None, if the property was held for investment purposes
The title company withholds 24% of the gain realized
questions.rationale: A withholding certificate can reduce the amount if the expected tax is lower.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is a dual-status alien in the year she becomes a U.S. resident. Which statement about her return is correct?
options: She files Form 1040 as an ordinary resident and reports worldwide income for the entire year
She generally cannot claim the standard deduction and files a return with a dual-status statement
She is exempt from U.S. tax in the year of change
She files Form 1040-NR for the entire year
questions.rationale: A first-year choice election under section 7701(b)(4) can treat her as a resident for the full year if conditions are met.

questions.stem: Spouses live in a community property state. They file separately. How is community income reported?
options: The spouse who files first reports the community income
The higher-earning spouse reports all of the community income
Each reports half of the community income; Form 8958 allocates items
Each spouse reports only the income that he or she earned
questions.rationale: Community property states include California, Texas, Arizona, Washington, Nevada, Louisiana, Idaho, New Mexico, and Wisconsin.

questions.stem: A servicemember is serving in a combat zone. By how much is the deadline for filing a return and paying tax postponed?
options: None; combat zone service does not postpone deadlines
A flat 30 days after the servicemember returns home
Exactly 60 days after the close of the tax year
The time in the combat zone plus 180 days
questions.rationale: Combat pay is also excluded from gross income for enlisted personnel.

questions.stem: A minister receives a housing allowance designated in advance by the church as part of compensation. How is it treated?
options: Excluded from both income tax and self-employment tax
Excluded from income tax however the money is actually used
Excluded from income tax up to the lowest of three limits, but subject to SE tax
Fully taxable for both income tax and self-employment tax
questions.rationale: Ministers are treated as self-employed for Social Security purposes unless they have an approved exemption (Form 4361).

questions.stem: A farmer receives crop insurance proceeds in 2025 for crops damaged in 2025. Under what circumstances may she defer the proceeds to 2026?
options: She may defer them only if she uses the accrual method
She may always defer the proceeds for a full two years
No deferral is allowed for crop insurance proceeds
She may elect to defer them if she normally sells most crops the next year
questions.rationale: Federal disaster relief payments follow similar rules for livestock sales under §1033(e).

questions.stem: A taxpayer lives in a county declared a federal disaster area. What relief is generally available for deadlines?
options: Relief applies only if the taxpayer first files Form 4868
All tax for the affected year is forgiven
The IRS may postpone filing and payment deadlines for up to a year
The IRS waives interest but leaves filing deadlines in place
questions.rationale: Qualified disaster distributions and casualty loss elections may also be available.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sold digital assets (cryptocurrency) for a gain after holding them 18 months. How are the proceeds treated?
options: Short-term capital gain, since crypto prices are volatile
Long-term capital gain on Form 8949, since digital assets are property
Tax-exempt income, since crypto is not treated as currency
Ordinary income reported on Schedule 1 as other income
questions.rationale: Brokers report digital asset sales on Form 1099-DA beginning with 2025 transactions.

questions.stem: A taxpayer made $6,500 in nondeductible traditional IRA contributions over several years and now takes a distribution. Which form tracks the basis?
options: Form 1099-R, Distributions
Form 5329, Additional Taxes on Qualified Plans
Form 4797, Sales of Business Property
Form 8606, Nondeductible IRAs
questions.rationale: Basis should be tracked every year a nondeductible contribution is made.

questions.stem: A U.S. citizen files Form 8938 to report specified foreign financial assets. A single taxpayer living in the United States must file if assets exceed what thresholds?
options: Over $200,000 on the last day of the year only
Over $10,000 at any time during the year
Over $50,000 at year end or over $75,000 at any time
Any foreign account, whatever its value
questions.rationale: Filing Form 8938 does not replace the FBAR.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's spouse died in 2025. The executor files the decedent's final Form 1040. What date does the final return cover?
options: The full calendar year 2025, even if death was in March
The prior year only, ending December 31, 2024
The date of death through December 31, 2025
January 1, 2025 through the date of death
questions.rationale: A surviving spouse may file jointly for the year of death.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a Form 1099-R showing a distribution from a Roth IRA that was a return of her own contributions only. How is it taxed?
options: Subject to the 10% additional tax, but not income tax
Not taxed and not subject to the 10% additional tax
Fully taxable as ordinary income in the year received
Taxed at long-term capital gains rates in the year received
questions.rationale: Report on Form 8606 if the Roth distribution is nonqualified.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's home is foreclosed. The mortgage was nonrecourse, with a balance of $300,000, and the home's fair market value was $260,000. Her adjusted basis was $220,000. How is the foreclosure treated?
options: Amount realized is $300,000, producing an $80,000 gain and $40,000 of debt income
Amount realized is $300,000, producing an $80,000 gain with no cancellation of debt income
Amount realized is $220,000, producing no gain and $80,000 of debt income
Amount realized is $260,000, producing a $40,000 gain and $40,000 of debt income
questions.rationale: For recourse debt, the gain is computed on fair market value and the excess debt forgiven is COD income.

questions.stem: A taxpayer transfers property to her former spouse as part of a divorce settlement. The property has a basis of $50,000 and a fair market value of $120,000. What is the tax result for the transferor?
options: No gain is recognized, and the recipient takes a carryover basis of $50,000
A $70,000 gain is recognized by the transferor
The transfer is a taxable gift from the transferor
No gain is recognized, and the recipient takes a $120,000 basis
questions.rationale: A transfer is incident to divorce if it occurs within one year after the marriage ends or is related to its ending.

questions.stem: A homeowner rents her vacation home to tenants for 10 days during the year at fair rental value and uses it personally for 40 days. How is the rental income treated?
options: Reported on Schedule E, with expenses prorated by the days rented
Excluded from income, with no rental expense deductions allowed
Reported on Schedule C as income from a trade or business
Reported as hobby income, with all expenses disallowed
questions.rationale: The 'Augusta rule' provides the same result for short-term rentals under 15 days.

questions.stem: A landlord receives a $2,000 security deposit from a tenant and plans to return it at the end of the lease. When is the deposit taxable income?
options: Never, since deposits always remain the tenant's funds
Only if the landlord keeps it, such as to cover unpaid rent
In the year received, since it is treated as advance rent
In the year the lease is signed, whether or not paid
questions.rationale: A deposit used as a final month's rent is treated as advance rent.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a distribution from her IRA and, within 60 days, deposits it into a different IRA. Three months later she takes another IRA distribution and tries to roll it over too. What is the result?
options: Both are taxable, since rollovers are never allowed
Only the first one is taxable, and the second is tax-free
The second is taxable; only one IRA-to-IRA rollover per 12 months
Both are tax-free, since each was done within 60 days
questions.rationale: Direct trustee-to-trustee transfers avoid the once-per-year limit.

questions.stem: A taxpayer misses the 60-day rollover deadline because of a bank error. What relief may be available without a private letter ruling?
options: A Tax Court hearing request filed within 90 days
A self-certification that she qualifies for a Rev. Proc. 2020-46 waiver
A refund of the full distribution paid by the IRS
Nothing; a late rollover is always fully taxable
questions.rationale: The IRS can also grant waivers through a private letter ruling for a user fee.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wins $2,500 in a lottery with a payer that must withhold. What is the standard withholding rate on the winnings above the threshold?
options: 10%, and Form 1099-MISC is issued for the winnings
37%, and no information return is issued for them
28%, and Form 1099-B is issued for the winnings
24%, and Form W-2G is issued for reportable winnings
questions.rationale: Winnings are income regardless of whether a Form W-2G is issued.

questions.stem: A taxpayer takes the standard deduction. Under the 2025 tax act, which of these deductions is still available to her for 2025?
options: The deduction for qualified tips, in a listed tipped occupation
The deduction for cash gifts made to her church
The deduction for mortgage interest paid on her home
The deduction for state and local property taxes paid
questions.rationale: The new deductions are claimed below AGI on the 1040 and reduce taxable income.

questions.stem: Beginning in 2026, which charitable deduction becomes available to taxpayers who do not itemize?
options: Up to $5,000 for gifts of any kind of property
A credit equal to 25% of her cash gifts
Up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) for cash gifts to qualified charities
100% of any gift made to a donor-advised fund
questions.rationale: Itemizers also face a floor of 0.5% of AGI on charitable gifts beginning in 2026.

questions.stem: Beginning in 2025, to claim the child tax credit, what Social Security number requirement applies to the taxpayer?
options: Both the child and the filer need only an ITIN
No SSN is needed for anyone claiming the credit
One parent must have an employment-valid SSN, plus the child's SSN
Only the child needs an SSN, the same as before
questions.rationale: Credit for other dependents remains available to filers without an SSN who have qualifying dependents with an ITIN.

questions.stem: An employee has a health flexible spending arrangement (FSA) through her employer. What is the general rule on unused amounts at year end?
options: They are deductible as medical expenses on Schedule A
They are refunded to the employee as taxable wages automatically
They are forfeited unless the plan allows a limited carryover or a grace period
They roll over without limit to the next year
questions.rationale: Employees may be reimbursed only for expenses incurred during the coverage period.

questions.stem: A taxpayer pays $9,000 of K-12 tuition from a 529 plan distribution in the same year. What is the tax treatment?
options: Qualified in any amount, including room and board
Qualified for up to $10,000 per beneficiary per year in K-12 tuition
Taxable in full, with a 10% penalty on all of it
Not qualified, since 529 plans can pay only for college
questions.rationale: The 2025 tax act expanded qualified K-12 expenses beginning in 2026.

questions.stem: Under the 2025 tax act, what change applies to the Premium Tax Credit repayment of excess advance payments for tax years after 2025?
options: Repayment is no longer required of any amount
Repayment applies only to taxpayers with income below 100% of the poverty line
Repayment is capped at $500 for all filers
The caps on repayment of excess advance payments are eliminated
questions.rationale: Taxpayers should update their Marketplace income estimates during the year.

questions.stem: Under the 2025 tax act, how do Form 1099-DA reports apply to digital asset transactions for the 2025 tax year?
options: Only the buyer reports on Form 1099-DA for 2025
Brokers are exempt from reporting digital asset sales
Brokers report proceeds and basis starting in 2020
Brokers report proceeds for 2025; basis reporting starts for 2026
questions.rationale: Taxpayers must report all digital asset transactions regardless of whether they receive Form 1099-DA.

questions.stem: What is a feature of the 'Trump account' enacted by the 2025 tax act, available beginning July 4, 2026?
options: A tax-free savings account with no limit on contributions
A retirement account open to adults only
A minor's IRA-type account: $5,000 yearly limit, with a federal seed
A replacement for 529 plans with higher yearly limits
questions.rationale: Contributions cannot begin before July 4, 2026.

questions.stem: A client wants to contribute to a Roth IRA, but her income exceeds the Roth contribution phase-out. What strategy may allow funding a Roth indirectly?
options: Make a Roth contribution anyway, ignoring the income limit
Fund a 529 plan and then withdraw the money into a Roth
Defer the contribution until she reaches age 59½
Make a nondeductible IRA contribution, then convert, noting the pro-rata rule
questions.rationale: Form 8606 reports the nondeductible contribution and the conversion.

questions.stem: A client's employer offers a Dependent Care FSA. For 2025, what is the annual limit on pre-tax contributions per household, and what is the planned change for 2026?
options: $2,500 for 2025, with no change planned for 2026
$10,000 for 2025, falling to $5,000 for 2026
$3,000 for 2025, rising to $5,000 for 2026
questions.rationale: Excluded benefits reduce the expenses eligible for the dependent care credit.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives an IRS notice CP504. What does it generally indicate?
options: An examination report proposing changes
A notice of deficiency giving 90 days to petition Tax Court
A request for additional information on an amended return
Notice of intent to levy certain property, such as a state tax refund
questions.rationale: CP14 is the first balance due notice, followed by CP501, CP503, and CP504.

questions.stem: An individual who is a household employer wants to avoid underpaying estimated taxes for the household employee's taxes. What option is available?
options: Raise her own W-4 withholding or pay estimates to cover Schedule H tax
Pay nothing until the household employee leaves the job
Pay quarterly with a separate Form 941 for the employee
Wait until next year and pay with a Form 940 filing
questions.rationale: Schedule H is due with Form 1040, including extensions.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is a nonresident alien and is married to a U.S. citizen. She wants to file jointly. What election lets her do so?
options: A §754 election to adjust the basis of assets
A §1033 election to defer gain on a conversion
A §83(b) election made within 30 days of the transfer
A §6013(g) election to be taxed as a U.S. resident all year
questions.rationale: The election is made by attaching a statement to the first joint return.

questions.stem: A nonresident alien individual with U.S.-source wages for services performed in the United States must file which return?
options: Form 1120-F
Form 1042
Form 1040-NR
Form 1040 with a nonresident box checked
questions.rationale: NRAs generally cannot use the standard deduction, except for certain students and apprentices from India.

questions.stem: A foreign student on an F-1 visa has been in the United States for four calendar years. Is the student exempt from counting days toward the substantial presence test?
options: No; students are never treated as exempt individuals
No; students are exempt only for their first five calendar years
Yes; an F-1 student is exempt for as long as the visa lasts
Yes, but only for the student's first calendar year
questions.rationale: After five years, the student must count days unless the student shows no intent to remain permanently.

questions.stem: Maria operates a small flower shop by herself and has not filed any formation documents with her state. She reports the shop's income and expenses on her personal tax return. Which form does Maria most likely use to report this business activity?
options: Form 1065, U.S. Return of Partnership Income
Form 1120-S, U.S. Income Tax Return for an S Corporation
Schedule C, filed with her Form 1040
Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return
questions.rationale: An individual carrying on an unincorporated business as the sole owner is a sole proprietor and reports the activity on Schedule C of Form 1040.

questions.stem: Which of the following business entities is generally treated as a separate taxpaying entity that pays income tax at the entity level on its own taxable income?
options: A C corporation
An S corporation
A single-member LLC that has made no entity elections
A general partnership
questions.rationale: The C corporation is the classic separate taxpaying entity, paying tax at the corporate level, while partnerships, S corporations, and disregarded LLCs are pass-through structures.

questions.stem: Greenfield Partners is a general partnership with three equal partners. During the year it earned $90,000 of ordinary business income and made no distributions. How is this income taxed for federal purposes?
options: Only the managing partner reports the income because he controls the business
Each partner reports $30,000 of the income on his or her own return whether or not it was distributed
The partnership pays tax on the full $90,000 at the entity level
No partner reports any income because nothing was distributed
questions.rationale: Partners are taxed on their distributive share of partnership income for the year regardless of whether cash is actually distributed.

questions.stem: Which of the following would disqualify a domestic corporation from making a valid S corporation election?
options: Having a nonresident alien individual as a shareholder
Having a single class of stock with differing voting rights
Having 75 shareholders who are all U.S. individuals
Having an estate as a shareholder following a shareholder's death
questions.rationale: S corporation eligibility requires that shareholders be eligible persons; nonresident aliens are not permitted shareholders, unlike estates and certain trusts.

questions.stem: Dorian transfers a building with an adjusted basis of $40,000 and a fair market value of $100,000 to a newly formed corporation solely in exchange for 100% of its stock. He receives no cash or other property. Under the general rule of IRC §351, how much gain does Dorian recognize on the transfer?
questions.rationale: Section 351 allows tax-free incorporation when property is exchanged solely for stock and the transferor controls at least 80% of the corporation immediately after the exchange.

questions.stem: Lila contributes equipment with an adjusted basis of $30,000 and a fair market value of $50,000 to a corporation in a transaction qualifying under §351. In addition to stock, she receives $8,000 in cash (boot). How much gain must Lila recognize?
options: $50,000, the fair market value of the equipment
$8,000, limited to the amount of boot received
$0 because the transaction qualifies under §351
$20,000, the full built-in gain on the equipment
questions.rationale: In a §351 exchange, gain is recognized to the extent of boot (cash or other property) received, but not more than the realized gain.

questions.stem: A limited liability company (LLC) with two members and no entity classification election is, by default, treated as which of the following for federal income tax purposes?
options: A C corporation
An S corporation
A partnership
A disregarded entity
questions.rationale: Under the check-the-box rules, a domestic multi-member LLC defaults to partnership classification absent an election to be taxed as a corporation.

questions.stem: Theo is a 25% partner in a partnership. At the start of the year his outside basis is $10,000. His share of partnership ordinary income for the year is $7,000, and the partnership distributed $4,000 of cash to him during the year. What is Theo's outside basis at year-end?
questions.rationale: A partner's outside basis increases by the distributive share of income and decreases by cash distributions received.

questions.stem: Which statement about S corporation shareholder basis and loss deductions is correct?
options: A shareholder may deduct passed-through losses without limit regardless of basis
Losses are limited to the shareholder's stock basis plus basis in direct loans the shareholder made to the corporation
Suspended losses due to insufficient basis are permanently lost and cannot be carried forward
A shareholder's share of corporate debt to third parties automatically increases stock basis
questions.rationale: S corporation losses are limited to stock basis plus the shareholder's basis in direct loans to the corporation; corporate-level third-party debt does not create shareholder basis, and suspended losses carry forward.

questions.stem: A profitable C corporation distributes its after-tax earnings to its individual shareholders as dividends. From the shareholders' standpoint, this distribution illustrates which characteristic of the C corporation form?
options: Pass-through taxation that avoids any entity-level tax
Automatic conversion of the corporation to an S corporation
A complete exemption from tax on dividends received by individuals
Double taxation, because earnings are taxed at the corporate level and again as dividends to shareholders
questions.rationale: The defining tax disadvantage of the C corporation is double taxation: profits are taxed once at the corporate level and again when distributed as dividends.

questions.stem: Generally, by what date must a calendar-year corporation file Form 2553 to elect S corporation status effective for the current tax year?
options: By the 15th day of the third month of the tax year (March 15 for a calendar-year corporation)
An S election may be made at any time during the year with immediate effect
By April 15 of the following year
By December 31 of the prior year only
questions.rationale: Form 2553 must generally be filed by the 15th day of the third month of the tax year (March 15 for calendar-year filers) to take effect for that year.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a key non-tax advantage of forming a corporation or an LLC instead of operating as a sole proprietorship?
options: The business is exempt from all state filing requirements
Owners generally receive limited liability protection for business debts
The owner can avoid keeping any separate financial records
Income is never subject to federal tax
questions.rationale: Limited liability protection for owners is a principal non-tax reason to choose a corporation or LLC over a sole proprietorship.

questions.stem: Riverside LLC, taxed as a partnership, distributes $6,000 of cash to partner Anita when her outside basis is $9,000. The cash is a current (nonliquidating) distribution. What is the tax result to Anita?
options: She recognizes $3,000 of gain and her basis becomes zero
