questions.stem: Under the accrual method, an expense is generally deductible when:
options: All events have occurred to establish the liability, the amount is determinable with reasonable accuracy, and economic performance has occurred
The invoice is received
It is paid in cash
It is merely estimated
questions.rationale: Accrual-basis deductions require satisfying the all-events test plus economic performance under §461.

questions.stem: A small business taxpayer for 2024 generally may use the cash method if average annual gross receipts for the prior three years do not exceed:
options: $25 million
$30.5 million
$10 million
$1 million
questions.rationale: The §448(c) small business threshold is inflation-adjusted to $30.5 million for 2024, permitting use of the cash method.

questions.stem: Business meals are generally deductible at what percentage for 2024 (assuming the temporary 100% restaurant provision has expired)?
questions.rationale: With the temporary 100% restaurant-meal deduction expired, business meals revert to the general 50% limitation for 2024.

questions.stem: Which Schedule of Form 1120 reconciles book income to taxable income for corporations with total assets of $10 million or more?
options: Schedule G
Schedule M-3
Schedule M-1
Schedule L
questions.rationale: Corporations with $10 million or more in total assets use Schedule M-3 (rather than M-1) for the detailed book-tax reconciliation.

questions.stem: The qualified business income (QBI) deduction under §199A is generally:
options: 50% of W-2 wages only
A credit equal to 20% of tax
Up to 20% of qualified business income
10% of taxable income
questions.rationale: §199A allows up to a 20% deduction of qualified business income from pass-through entities, subject to limitations.

questions.stem: A specified service trade or business (SSTB) owner is subject to a phase-out of the §199A QBI deduction. For 2024, the deduction is fully phased out for married filing jointly when taxable income exceeds approximately:
questions.rationale: For 2024 MFJ, the SSTB phase-out range is roughly $383,900 to $483,900; above $483,900 the SSTB QBI deduction is eliminated.

questions.stem: A business writes off a wholly worthless business bad debt. Under the accrual method, the deduction is:
options: Deferred until the debtor files bankruptcy
An ordinary deduction in the year the debt becomes worthless
A nondeductible personal loss
A short-term capital loss
questions.rationale: Business bad debts produce an ordinary deduction in the year of worthlessness; nonbusiness bad debts are short-term capital losses.

questions.stem: For 2024, the Social Security wage base (maximum earnings subject to the 12.4% OASDI portion of self-employment tax) is:
questions.rationale: For 2024, only the first $168,600 of net earnings is subject to the 12.4% Social Security portion of SE tax; Medicare's 2.9% has no cap.

questions.stem: For an S corporation shareholder-employee, the IRS requires the corporation to pay:
options: Reasonable compensation for services before distributions
No salary, only distributions
Maximum salary equal to all profits
Compensation only if profits exceed $100,000
questions.rationale: S corporations must pay shareholder-employees reasonable compensation for services rendered before making distributions, to avoid recharacterization by the IRS.

questions.stem: An S corporation has accumulated E&P from prior C years and both an AAA and an Other Adjustments Account (OAA). Distributions are sourced first from:
options: OAA
Accumulated E&P
Paid-in capital
AAA
questions.rationale: The ordering of S corporation distributions with accumulated E&P is generally AAA first, then accumulated E&P (dividend), then OAA.

questions.stem: A cash-basis business receives a $5,000 advance payment in December 2024 for services to be performed in 2025. Under the general rule, the advance is:
options: Taxable half in 2024 and half in 2025
Not taxable until services are performed
Never taxable
Taxable in 2024 when received
questions.rationale: A cash-basis taxpayer reports income when received; the $5,000 advance is taxable in 2024 even though services occur in 2025.

questions.stem: A corporation must generally make estimated tax payments if it expects its tax to be at least:
questions.rationale: Corporations must pay estimated tax when the expected liability is $500 or more; the individual threshold is $1,000.

questions.stem: A taxpayer trades in a business truck (adjusted basis $8,000) plus $20,000 cash for a new business truck. Because personal property no longer qualifies for §1031, the trade-in is treated as:
options: A nontaxable involuntary conversion
A tax-free like-kind exchange
A taxable sale of the old truck and a separate purchase of the new truck
A §351 contribution
questions.rationale: With §1031 limited to real property, a vehicle trade-in is now a taxable sale of the old asset and a purchase of the new asset.

questions.stem: The §1245 depreciation recapture rules apply to gain on the sale of:
options: A personal residence
Land
Inventory
Depreciable personal property (such as equipment) to the extent of depreciation taken
questions.rationale: §1245 recaptures gain as ordinary income to the extent of depreciation claimed on depreciable personal property.

questions.stem: For 2024, the first-year depreciation cap under the luxury auto limits for a passenger automobile (without claiming bonus depreciation) is approximately:
questions.rationale: For 2024, the luxury auto first-year depreciation cap is $12,400 without bonus depreciation (and $20,400 with bonus).

questions.stem: A corporation's capital losses may be deducted only to the extent of:
options: 50% of taxable income
$3,000 per year against ordinary income
Ordinary income without limit
Capital gains; excess carries back 3 years and forward 5 years
questions.rationale: Corporations deduct capital losses only against capital gains, with a three-year carryback and five-year carryforward of excess.

questions.stem: Under the uniform capitalization (UNICAP) rules of §263A, a producer or reseller must capitalize:
options: Only selling expenses
Both direct costs and an allocable share of indirect costs into inventory
Only interest expense
Only direct material costs
questions.rationale: §263A (UNICAP) requires capitalizing direct and an allocable share of indirect costs into inventory or production costs.

questions.stem: A small business taxpayer meeting the gross receipts test is exempt from:
options: The UNICAP rules of §263A and the requirement to maintain inventories under the accrual method
Paying employment taxes
Filing any tax return
Filing information returns
questions.rationale: Qualifying small business taxpayers are exempt from UNICAP and the accrual-inventory requirement, simplifying their accounting.

questions.stem: A partnership has $200,000 of ordinary business income and pays $30,000 in guaranteed payments to a partner. The guaranteed payments are deducted in computing the partnership's ordinary business income. The partnership's reported ordinary business income on Form 1065, line 22, is:
questions.rationale: Guaranteed payments are deductible by the partnership, reducing ordinary business income: $200,000 − $30,000 = $170,000.

questions.stem: On Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), separately stated items such as charitable contributions and §179 deductions are reported separately because:
options: The partnership cannot deduct them
Their tax treatment may differ at the individual partner level
They are never deductible
They are always nontaxable
questions.rationale: Items whose tax treatment depends on a partner's situation are separately stated on the K-1 so each partner applies the correct rules.

questions.stem: An estate or trust computes distributable net income (DNI), which limits the amount of:
options: Taxable income at the entity level only
The estate tax
The trustee's fees
The income distribution deduction and the amount taxable to beneficiaries
questions.rationale: DNI limits the income distribution deduction for the entity and the amount taxable to beneficiaries, while preserving income character.

questions.stem: A simple trust is one that, among other requirements:
options: Accumulates all income
Has only corporate beneficiaries
Makes only charitable distributions
Is required to distribute all of its income currently and makes no charitable contributions
questions.rationale: A simple trust is required to distribute all income currently, makes no charitable gifts, and distributes no principal.

questions.stem: Unrelated business taxable income (UBTI) of an exempt organization is income from a trade or business that is:
options: Substantially related to the exempt purpose
Received from investments only
Regularly carried on and not substantially related to the exempt purpose
Always tax-exempt
questions.rationale: UBTI is income from a regularly carried on trade or business that is unrelated to the organization's exempt purpose; it is taxed.

questions.stem: An exempt organization reports and pays tax on unrelated business income using which form?
options: Form 990
Form 990-T
Form 1041
Form 1120-S
questions.rationale: Exempt organizations report and pay tax on unrelated business income on Form 990-T.

questions.stem: For estates, the income tax return (Form 1041) is generally required if the estate has gross income for the tax year of at least:
questions.rationale: An estate must file Form 1041 if it has gross income of $600 or more (or a nonresident alien beneficiary).

questions.stem: A decedent's estate may elect a fiscal year for income tax purposes. The estate may choose any fiscal year ending:
options: On the anniversary of death only
On the last day of any month within 12 months after the date of death
On December 31 only
Exactly six months after death
questions.rationale: Estates (unlike trusts) may elect a fiscal year ending on the last day of any month within 12 months of death.

questions.stem: Most trusts (other than tax-exempt and certain grantor trusts) must use which tax year?
options: A fiscal year of their choosing
The same year as the grantor's estate
A calendar year
A 52-53 week year
questions.rationale: Trusts are generally required to use a calendar year, unlike estates which may elect a fiscal year.

questions.stem: On a final Form 1041 for a terminating estate, excess deductions and unused capital loss carryovers:
options: Become a refund to the estate
Are lost entirely
Pass through to the beneficiaries succeeding to the property
Are carried back to the decedent's final 1040
questions.rationale: On termination, an estate's or trust's unused carryovers and excess deductions pass through to the beneficiaries.

questions.stem: A farmer reports income and expenses from farming operations on which schedule of Form 1040?
options: Schedule F
Schedule SE
Schedule E
Schedule C
questions.rationale: Farmers use Schedule F to report farm income and expenses; Schedule SE then computes self-employment tax.

questions.stem: A qualifying farmer who derives at least two-thirds of gross income from farming may avoid an estimated tax penalty by:
options: Paying no estimated tax at all
Paying estimated tax by January 15 and filing/paying in full by March 1, or making one estimated payment by January 15
Filing by April 15 only
Paying quarterly like other taxpayers
questions.rationale: Qualifying farmers (two-thirds of income from farming) avoid the estimated tax penalty by paying by January 15 or filing and paying by March 1.

questions.stem: Which return is used by a private foundation to satisfy its annual filing requirement?
options: Form 990
Form 990-EZ
Form 990-N
Form 990-PF
questions.rationale: Private foundations file Form 990-PF annually, regardless of their gross receipts.

questions.stem: A complex trust has DNI of $30,000, of which $4,000 is tax-exempt interest. The trust distributes $20,000 to its sole beneficiary. How much of the distribution is taxable to the beneficiary (assuming no other adjustments)?
questions.rationale: Distributions carry out DNI proportionately; the tax-exempt share ($4,000/$30,000) remains exempt, so $20,000 × (26,000/30,000) = $17,333 is taxable.

questions.stem: An estate's personal exemption on Form 1041 is:
questions.rationale: On Form 1041, an estate gets a $600 exemption, a simple trust $300, and a complex trust $100.

questions.stem: A nonresident alien-owned U.S. business or a foreign corporation engaged in a U.S. trade or business is taxed on income that is:
options: Effectively connected with the U.S. trade or business
Only foreign-source income
Worldwide income
Never taxable in the U.S.
questions.rationale: Foreign persons engaged in a U.S. trade or business are taxed on effectively connected income at regular U.S. rates.

questions.stem: A foreign corporation may be subject to the branch profits tax. The branch profits tax is designed to:
options: Replace the corporate income tax
Approximate the tax on dividends a foreign corporation would have paid had it operated through a U.S. subsidiary
Tax only capital gains
Exempt branch earnings
questions.rationale: The branch profits tax imposes a second-level tax on a foreign corporation's U.S. branch earnings, mimicking the tax on subsidiary dividends.

questions.stem: An S corporation that was formerly a C corporation may owe the built-in gains (BIG) tax if it sells appreciated assets within the recognition period of:
options: 10 years
7 years
3 years
5 years
questions.rationale: The built-in gains tax applies to appreciated assets sold within the five-year recognition period after a C-to-S conversion.

questions.stem: The built-in gains tax on an S corporation is imposed at what rate?
questions.rationale: The built-in gains tax equals the recognized built-in gain multiplied by the highest corporate rate of 21%.

questions.stem: An exempt organization engaged in lobbying that is a §501(c)(3) public charity risks loss of exemption if lobbying constitutes:
options: More than 50% of revenue
Only paid lobbying
A substantial part of its activities (unless it makes the §501(h) election)
Any amount of activity
questions.rationale: A public charity risks losing exemption if lobbying is a substantial part of its activities, absent a §501(h) election that sets dollar limits.

questions.stem: A §501(c)(3) organization is absolutely prohibited from:
options: Paying salaries to employees
Owning real estate
Earning any unrelated business income
Participating or intervening in any political campaign on behalf of or in opposition to a candidate
questions.rationale: Political campaign intervention is an absolute prohibition for §501(c)(3) organizations and can cause loss of exemption.

questions.stem: Cooperative organizations that distribute patronage dividends to members report using:
options: Form 1065
Form 1120-C
Form 990
Form 1120
questions.rationale: Cooperative associations file Form 1120-C and may deduct qualifying patronage dividends paid to members.

questions.stem: An S corporation shareholder's stock basis is increased by the shareholder's share of:
options: Nondeductible expenses
Distributions received
Corporate-level debt only
Tax-exempt income and separately and non-separately stated income items
questions.rationale: S corporation stock basis increases for the shareholder's share of taxable and tax-exempt income and decreases for distributions, losses, and nondeductible expenses.

questions.stem: When a partnership terminates and distributes all assets, the partners generally recognize gain only when:
options: The partnership has been profitable
Cash (or deemed cash) distributed exceeds the partner's outside basis
The partnership held the assets over one year
Any property is distributed
questions.rationale: On a liquidating distribution, a partner recognizes gain only if cash received exceeds outside basis; property generally takes a substituted basis.

questions.stem: Section 1250 recapture applies to depreciable real property. For property depreciated under straight-line MACRS, the amount of §1250 ordinary recapture is generally:
options: Zero, because only excess depreciation over straight-line is recaptured as ordinary income
50% of the gain
Equal to depreciation taken
The full gain
questions.rationale: Because MACRS real property is depreciated straight-line, §1250 ordinary recapture is generally zero, though unrecaptured §1250 gain is taxed at up to 25%.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sells real property in an installment sale to a related party who then resells it within two years. Under §453(e):
options: The original seller may have to accelerate remaining gain when the related party resells within two years
The gain is converted to a loss
Only the buyer is taxed
No acceleration applies
questions.rationale: The §453(e) related-party rule accelerates the original seller's deferred gain if the related buyer resells within two years.

questions.stem: A single-member LLC that does not elect corporate treatment is treated for federal income tax purposes as:
options: A C corporation
An S corporation
A partnership
A disregarded entity reported on the owner's return
questions.rationale: A single-member LLC is disregarded by default, with its activity reported directly on the owner's return.

questions.stem: A corporation makes a nondeductible payment, such as a fine or penalty paid to a government for violation of law. On Schedule M-1, this item is:
options: A subtraction from book income
A tax credit
Ignored
An addition (expense recorded on books but not deductible for tax)
questions.rationale: Fines and penalties are nondeductible; on Schedule M-1 they are added back to book income to arrive at taxable income.

questions.stem: A partnership reports a §179 deduction on Schedule K-1. The §179 limitation is applied:
options: At both the partnership level and again at the partner level
Only at the partnership level
Only at the partner level
Never, because §179 cannot pass through
questions.rationale: §179 is limited at the entity level and then again when the partner combines it with §179 from other sources.

questions.stem: A charitable remainder trust (CRT) is generally:
options: Exempt from income tax unless it has unrelated business taxable income
Taxed at the corporate rate
A taxable trust on all income
Disregarded for tax
questions.rationale: A qualified CRT is income-tax exempt, but UBTI triggers a 100% excise tax; distributions to beneficiaries are taxed under tiered rules.

questions.stem: Under §704(b), a partnership allocation will be respected for tax purposes if it has:
options: Any business purpose
IRS pre-approval
Equal sharing among partners
Substantial economic effect
questions.rationale: Special allocations are respected if they have substantial economic effect, tested through proper capital account maintenance and liquidation provisions.

questions.stem: A taxpayer placing more than 40% of total MACRS personal property in service during the last quarter of the year must use:
options: The half-year convention
The mid-month convention
Straight-line only
The mid-quarter convention
questions.rationale: The mid-quarter convention is required when over 40% of personal property is placed in service in the final quarter.

questions.stem: A C corporation's taxable income for 2024 is taxed at a flat rate of:
questions.rationale: Since 2018, C corporations pay a flat 21% federal income tax rate.

questions.stem: A C corporation has a $50,000 net capital gain and a $60,000 net capital loss in the same year. The net $10,000 capital loss:
options: Is permanently lost
Offsets ordinary income this year
Is deductible up to $3,000
Cannot offset ordinary income; it carries back 3 years and forward 5 years as a short-term capital loss
questions.rationale: Corporate net capital losses offset only capital gains, carrying back three years and forward five years as short-term losses.

questions.stem: An S corporation election terminates automatically if the corporation:
options: Pays dividends
Acquires a nonresident alien shareholder or a second class of stock
Earns more than $1 million
Has 90 shareholders
questions.rationale: An S election terminates if the corporation gains an ineligible shareholder or creates a second class of stock.

questions.stem: Wages, tips, and federal income tax withholding for employees are reported each quarter on:
options: Form 941
Form W-3
Form 1099-NEC
Form 940
questions.rationale: Employers report quarterly wages, withholding, and FICA on Form 941.

questions.stem: For 2024, the qualified business income deduction is generally available to estates and trusts:
options: Yes, the QBI deduction can apply to trusts and estates, with the deduction allocated between the entity and beneficiaries based on DNI
Only to grantor trusts
Only to charitable trusts
Never
questions.rationale: Estates and trusts may claim the §199A deduction, apportioning QBI items between the entity and beneficiaries based on relative DNI.

questions.stem: Amortization of §197 intangibles, such as purchased goodwill, is taken over a period of:
options: 5 years
40 years
15 years
10 years
questions.rationale: Purchased §197 intangibles, including goodwill, are amortized straight-line over 15 years.

questions.stem: In a §351 transfer, if the liabilities assumed by the corporation exceed the total adjusted basis of the property transferred, the transferor:
options: Receives a step-up in stock basis
Recognizes no gain
Cannot use §351
Recognizes gain equal to the excess of liabilities over basis
questions.rationale: Under §357(c), liabilities assumed in excess of the transferred property's basis create recognized gain to the transferor.

questions.stem: A partnership's recourse liabilities are generally allocated among partners based on:
options: Profit-sharing ratios
Equal shares always
Each partner's economic risk of loss
Capital contributions only
questions.rationale: Recourse liabilities are allocated to the partner(s) bearing the economic risk of loss; nonrecourse liabilities follow different rules.

questions.stem: A partnership's nonrecourse liabilities are generally allocated:
options: To the partner with the highest basis
Equally regardless of profit interest
Among partners according to profit-sharing ratios (with first allocating minimum gain and §704(c) amounts)
Entirely to the general partner
questions.rationale: Nonrecourse liabilities are allocated under a tiered approach ending with profit-sharing ratios, since no partner bears the risk of loss.

questions.stem: A homeowners association may elect under §528 to be taxed only on its:
options: Membership dues
Worldwide income
Net nonexempt function income at a flat rate, filing Form 1120-H
Total receipts at 21%
questions.rationale: Under §528, a qualifying HOA files Form 1120-H and is taxed only on nonexempt function income at a flat rate.

questions.stem: A business that overpaid its estimated taxes may apply the overpayment to the next year or:
options: Convert it to a credit against payroll tax
Deduct it as an expense
Only carry it forward
Request a refund
questions.rationale: Estimated tax overpayments may be refunded or applied to the following year's estimated tax.

questions.stem: A cash-method service business performs work in December 2024 but is not paid until January 2025. Under the constructive receipt doctrine, the income is taxable in:
options: Neither year
Either year at the taxpayer's choice
2025, when actually or constructively received
questions.rationale: Cash-method taxpayers report income when actually or constructively received; payment received in 2025 is 2025 income.

questions.stem: A trust that may accumulate income or distribute corpus, or that makes charitable contributions, is classified as:
options: A simple trust
A business trust
A grantor trust
A complex trust
questions.rationale: A complex trust is one that can accumulate income, distribute principal, or make charitable contributions.

questions.stem: A taxpayer using the LIFO inventory method during periods of rising prices generally reports:
options: Higher taxable income than FIFO
Lower taxable income than FIFO, because the most recent (higher) costs are charged to cost of goods sold
The same income as FIFO
No cost of goods sold
questions.rationale: In inflationary periods, LIFO matches the most recent higher costs against revenue, reducing taxable income versus FIFO.

questions.stem: A partner's outside basis in a partnership interest is initially:
options: Always zero
The fair market value of the interest
The basis of property contributed plus cash contributed, increased by the partner's share of liabilities
The partnership's total assets
questions.rationale: A partner's initial outside basis is the carryover basis of contributed property and cash, plus the share of partnership liabilities.

questions.stem: A taxpayer abandons depreciable business equipment that is not sold. The adjusted basis remaining is:
options: Nondeductible
Added to other asset basis
An ordinary loss under §165 in the year of abandonment
A capital loss
questions.rationale: Abandonment of business property (no sale or exchange) yields an ordinary §165 loss equal to the remaining adjusted basis.

questions.stem: For 2024, an estate's tax computation uses the highly compressed trust/estate brackets. This means estates and trusts reach high marginal rates:
options: At the same income as individuals
At higher income than individuals
Only on capital gains
At much lower income than individuals
questions.rationale: Trust and estate brackets are compressed, reaching the 37% rate at about $15,200 in 2024, far below individual thresholds.

questions.stem: A corporation that distributes property subject to a liability greater than the property's FMV recognizes gain measured by:
options: The liability (if greater than FMV) minus basis
Zero
The liability only
FMV minus basis
questions.rationale: Under §311(b), if the liability on distributed property exceeds FMV, the liability is treated as the FMV for measuring the corporation's gain.

questions.stem: A partner sells a partnership interest with a $25,000 capital gain, but $8,000 of that gain is attributable to §751 hot assets. The character of the gain is:
options: $25,000 ordinary income
$25,000 capital gain
$8,000 capital gain and $17,000 ordinary income
$8,000 ordinary income and $17,000 capital gain
questions.rationale: On a sale of a partnership interest, §751 recharacterizes the hot-asset portion ($8,000) as ordinary income; the rest is capital gain.

questions.stem: Foreign corporations engaged in U.S. business and certain foreign-owned U.S. corporations file which income tax return?
options: Form 1040-NR
Form 5471
Form 1120
Form 1120-F
questions.rationale: Foreign corporations report U.S. income on Form 1120-F.

questions.stem: Nonresidential real property (commercial buildings) placed in service under MACRS is depreciated over:
options: 27.5 years
31.5 years
50 years
39 years
questions.rationale: Commercial (nonresidential) real property is depreciated straight-line over 39 years.

questions.stem: A partnership makes a §754 election. This election allows the partnership to adjust the basis of partnership property on:
options: Dissolution only
A transfer of a partnership interest or certain distributions
Formation only
Annual income allocations
questions.rationale: A §754 election allows basis adjustments under §743(b) on interest transfers and §734(b) on certain distributions.

questions.stem: A corporation's contribution of inventory to a qualified charity may yield an enhanced deduction equal to:
options: Only the basis
Triple the basis
Fair market value with no limit
Basis plus one-half of the appreciation, not exceeding twice basis, for certain qualified contributions (e.g., care of the ill, needy, or infants)
questions.rationale: The enhanced charitable deduction for qualified inventory equals basis plus one-half of appreciation, capped at twice basis.

questions.stem: A §501(c)(3) organization's annual Form 990 is generally due by the 15th day of the:
options: 3rd month after year-end
5th month after year-end
6th month after year-end
4th month after year-end
questions.rationale: Form 990 is due the 15th day of the 5th month after year-end, which is May 15 for calendar-year organizations.

questions.stem: A partner's distributive share of partnership income is taxable to the partner:
options: Only when distributed in cash
In the year earned by the partnership, whether or not distributed
Only if the partner is a general partner
Only when the partnership is dissolved
questions.rationale: Partners are taxed on their distributive shares as income is earned by the partnership, regardless of actual distributions.

questions.stem: An employer that withholds FICA tax matches the employee's share. For 2024, the combined Social Security tax rate (employee plus employer) on wages up to the wage base is:
questions.rationale: The Social Security portion is 6.2% paid by each of the employee and employer, totaling 12.4%; Medicare adds 2.9%.

questions.stem: A taxpayer elects out of the installment method on a sale of property. The effect is that:
options: Gain is deferred indefinitely
All gain is reported in the year of sale
No gain is ever recognized
Gain is reported only when cash is received
questions.rationale: Electing out of §453 installment treatment causes the entire gain to be recognized in the year of sale.

questions.stem: The aggregation of a partner's items for the §704(d) loss limitation is applied:
options: Only when the partnership liquidates
Before basis adjustments
Only at year end without ordering rules
After increasing basis for the year's income items but before deducting losses
questions.rationale: Under §704(d), basis is increased for income items first, then losses are limited to the remaining outside basis.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who fails to deposit employment taxes on time may be subject to a failure-to-deposit penalty that increases based on:
options: The taxpayer's income
The number of employees
A flat $100
How late the deposit is, ranging from 2% to 15%
questions.rationale: The failure-to-deposit penalty rises with delay: 2% (1–5 days), 5% (6–15 days), 10% (16+ days), and 15% after notice.

questions.stem: An exempt §501(c)(3) organization that receives more than one-third of its support from gifts, grants, and contributions from the public is classified as:
options: A publicly supported charity (public charity)
A private foundation
A social club
A business league
questions.rationale: Meeting the public support test classifies a charity as a public charity rather than a private foundation.

questions.stem: A net operating loss is computed at which level for a partnership?
options: Not at the partnership level; losses pass through to partners who apply NOL rules individually
At the partnership level, then carried by the partnership
At the IRS level
NOLs do not apply to partnerships
questions.rationale: Partnerships pass losses through to partners; any NOL is determined at the partner level, not the partnership level.

questions.stem: When a corporation completely liquidates and distributes assets to shareholders, the shareholders generally recognize:
options: Only the corporation recognizes gain
No gain or loss
Gain or loss equal to the difference between the FMV of assets received and the stock basis
Ordinary income on all distributions
questions.rationale: Under §331, liquidation proceeds are treated as payment for stock; shareholders recognize capital gain or loss equal to FMV received minus basis.

questions.stem: A corporation pays its sole shareholder-employee a salary the IRS deems unreasonably high. The excess may be:
options: Carried forward as an NOL
Recharacterized as a nondeductible dividend
Fully deductible as compensation
Treated as a loan
questions.rationale: Excessive shareholder-employee compensation in a C corporation can be recharacterized as a nondeductible dividend.

questions.stem: A trust's income that is required to be distributed currently is taxed to:
options: The grantor only
The trust regardless of distribution
Neither party
The beneficiary, whether or not actually distributed
questions.rationale: For a simple trust, income required to be distributed currently is taxed to the beneficiary, whether or not actually distributed, limited by DNI.

questions.stem: A business that changes from the cash method to the accrual method generally must:
options: Restate prior returns
Apply a §481(a) adjustment to prevent omission or duplication of income/deductions
Ignore prior items
Get shareholder approval
questions.rationale: An accounting method change triggers a §481(a) adjustment to prevent income or deductions from being duplicated or omitted.

questions.stem: An S corporation with accumulated E&P may make a 'deemed dividend' election or a 'distribution ordering' election. If passive investment income exceeds 25% of gross receipts for three consecutive years while it has accumulated E&P, the S election:
options: Triggers immediate liquidation
Converts to a partnership
Terminates as of the beginning of the following tax year
Continues unaffected
questions.rationale: Excess passive investment income (over 25% of gross receipts) for three consecutive years with accumulated E&P terminates the S election.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's home office qualifies for a deduction if the space is used:
options: For any business purpose at any time
Regularly and exclusively as the principal place of business
Only for storage
Occasionally for business
questions.rationale: The home office deduction requires regular and exclusive business use, generally as the principal place of business.

questions.stem: A C corporation that wants to terminate its existence and distribute assets generally recognizes gain or loss under §336 as if it:
options: Made a tax-free distribution
Sold all assets at fair market value
Paid a deductible dividend
Contributed assets to a partnership
questions.rationale: Under §336, a liquidating corporation recognizes gain or loss as though it sold its distributed assets at fair market value.

questions.stem: Form 1120-S Schedule K-1 reports a shareholder's pro rata share of:
options: Officer compensation only
Only ordinary income
Each separately and non-separately stated item based on share ownership for the year
Distributions only
questions.rationale: The 1120-S K-1 allocates each income, deduction, and credit item to shareholders on a per-share, per-day basis.

questions.stem: A corporation makes estimated tax payments. A 'large corporation' (taxable income of $1 million or more in any of the 3 preceding years) may base its first installment on the prior year's tax but must base subsequent installments on:
options: Any amount it chooses
100% of the current year's tax (cannot use prior-year safe harbor for later installments)
The prior year's tax
50% of the prior year
questions.rationale: Large corporations may use the prior-year safe harbor only for the first installment and must base the rest on current-year tax.

questions.stem: The basis of stock received by a transferor in a §351 exchange equals the basis of property transferred, decreased by boot received and liabilities assumed, and increased by:
options: Any gain recognized by the transferor
The corporation's stock value
Future dividends
The corporation's E&P
questions.rationale: In a §351 exchange, stock basis = property basis − boot − liabilities assumed + gain recognized.

questions.stem: A pooled income fund and a charitable lead trust are split-interest arrangements. A charitable lead trust pays:
options: Nothing to charity
All income to private beneficiaries only
An income stream to charity for a term, with the remainder passing to noncharitable beneficiaries
The remainder to charity and income to private beneficiaries
questions.rationale: A charitable lead trust pays the lead interest to charity for a term, with the remainder to noncharitable beneficiaries, the inverse of a CRT.

questions.stem: A taxpayer expenses research and experimental (R&E) costs under §174. For tax years beginning after 2021, domestic R&E costs must be:
options: Capitalized and amortized over 5 years
Capitalized and amortized over 15 years
Deducted immediately
Never deductible
questions.rationale: Post-2021, §174 requires capitalizing R&E costs and amortizing over 5 years domestically (15 years for foreign research).

questions.stem: A disproportionate distribution of §751 hot assets relative to a partner's interest can cause:
options: A tax-free reorganization
A deemed exchange resulting in ordinary income recognition under §751(b)
A capital loss only
No tax consequences
questions.rationale: §751(b) treats disproportionate distributions of hot assets as deemed exchanges, triggering ordinary income to balance the partners' interests.

questions.stem: A business vehicle weighing over 6,000 pounds (gross vehicle weight) used more than 50% for business may qualify for §179 expensing up to a special SUV limit for 2024 of:
questions.rationale: For 2024, §179 expensing of a heavy SUV (over 6,000 lbs GVWR) is limited to $30,500.

questions.stem: A §501(c)(6) organization is generally a:
options: Social welfare organization
Charitable organization
Labor union
Business league, chamber of commerce, or trade association
questions.rationale: §501(c)(6) organizations are business leagues, chambers of commerce, real estate boards, and trade associations.

questions.stem: A taxpayer placed a $30,000 machine (5-year MACRS) in service. Using the 200% declining balance method with the half-year convention, first-year depreciation (before any §179 or bonus) is:
questions.rationale: For 5-year MACRS property, the first-year rate is 20% under 200% declining balance with the half-year convention: $30,000 × 20% = $6,000.

questions.stem: A corporation's accumulated adjustments account (AAA) is relevant:
options: For exempt organizations
For S corporations, to track undistributed previously taxed income for distribution ordering
For C corporations only
For partnerships only
questions.rationale: The AAA is an S corporation account tracking previously taxed undistributed income, important for ordering distributions when accumulated E&P exists.

questions.stem: An exempt organization that engages in an 'excess benefit transaction' with a disqualified person is subject to:
options: Loss of exemption only
No penalty
A 21% corporate tax
Intermediate sanctions (excise taxes) under §4958 on the disqualified person and possibly organization managers
questions.rationale: §4958 intermediate sanctions impose excise taxes on disqualified persons (and certain managers) for excess benefit transactions, instead of revoking exemption.

questions.stem: Two corporations are brother-sister corporations in a controlled group if five or fewer persons own at least 80% of each and more than 50% identically, considering the stock owned by each person only to the extent it is owned with respect to:
options: The smallest identical ownership across the corporations
The largest corporation
Each separate corporation
Voting stock only
questions.rationale: For brother-sister controlled groups, the identical ownership test counts only the smallest percentage each owner holds across the corporations.

questions.stem: A taxpayer may deduct business interest expense that was disallowed under §163(j) in a prior year by:
options: Carrying the disallowed interest forward indefinitely to future years
Carrying it back 2 years
Converting it to a credit
Never; it is permanently lost
questions.rationale: Disallowed business interest under §163(j) carries forward indefinitely, subject to the limitation in each future year.

questions.stem: A partnership terminates for tax purposes when:
options: It adds a new partner
A partner dies
No part of any business continues to be carried on by any partners in a partnership
It changes its name
questions.rationale: A partnership terminates when no part of its business continues to be carried on by any partners in a partnership.

questions.stem: A C corporation has taxable income before the dividends-received deduction. The DRD may be limited to a percentage of taxable income (the taxable income limitation), but this limitation does not apply if claiming the full DRD:
options: Increases taxable income
Triggers AMT
Creates or increases a net operating loss
Reduces estimated taxes
questions.rationale: The DRD taxable income limitation is waived when claiming the full DRD creates or increases an NOL.

questions.stem: For a partnership, syndication costs (costs of selling partnership interests) are:
options: Neither deductible nor amortizable; they are capitalized permanently
Amortized over 180 months
Currently deductible
Deducted up to $5,000
questions.rationale: Partnership syndication costs are permanently capitalized, unlike organizational costs which may be deducted and amortized under §709.

questions.stem: A trust makes a distribution within the first 65 days of the new tax year and elects to treat it as made in the prior year. This is known as the:
options: Tier system
Separate share rule
Throwback rule
65-day election (§663(b))
questions.rationale: The §663(b) 65-day election lets a trustee treat early-year distributions as made in the prior tax year for income allocation.

questions.stem: Dana contributes property with a $40,000 basis and $100,000 fair market value to a partnership in exchange for a 25% interest. The property is subject to a $60,000 nonrecourse liability that the partnership assumes. Assuming Dana's share of partnership liabilities is $15,000, what is the immediate effect on Dana under Section 752?
options: Dana is treated as receiving a $60,000 cash distribution equal to the full liability
Dana is treated as receiving a $45,000 cash distribution from the net relief of liabilities
Dana has no deemed distribution because Section 721 is fully nonrecognition
Dana recognizes $60,000 of gain on the contribution under Section 721
questions.rationale: Under Section 752, relief of liabilities is a deemed cash distribution, reduced by the contributing partner's reallocated share, so the net $45,000 shift is the distribution.

questions.stem: A partner contributes appreciated property and within two years receives a cash distribution that, under the facts and circumstances, was not dependent on partnership profits. Absent a qualifying exception, how does the IRS most likely characterize the transaction?
options: As a disguised sale under Section 707(a)(2)(B), with gain recognized to the contributing partner
As a guaranteed payment fully deductible by the partnership
As a tax-free Section 721 contribution followed by an unrelated Section 731 distribution
As a Section 736 retirement payment to a withdrawing partner
questions.rationale: The disguised sale rules of Section 707(a)(2)(B) recharacterize a contribution-plus-distribution within two years as a taxable sale of property to the partnership.

questions.stem: Under current law (post-2017), a partnership terminates for tax purposes under Section 708 in which of the following situations?
options: The partnership changes its tax year-end
A single partner buys out 30% of another partner's interest
No part of any business, financial operation, or venture continues to be carried on by any partner in a partnership
Fifty percent or more of the total interests in capital and profits is sold within a 12-month period
questions.rationale: Post-TCJA, Section 708 termination occurs only when the partnership's business ceases to be carried on by any of its partners; the technical termination rule was repealed.

questions.stem: A partnership has a Section 754 election in effect. A new partner buys an interest for $80,000 when the partner's share of the partnership's inside basis in assets is $50,000. What is the result under Section 743(b)?
options: The incoming partner recognizes $30,000 of immediate gain
A $30,000 positive basis adjustment is made to partnership assets allocable to the incoming partner
No adjustment is permitted because Section 743 applies only to distributions
The partnership's total inside basis is reduced by $30,000
questions.rationale: Section 743(b), available when a Section 754 election is in effect, adjusts the transferee partner's share of inside basis to match the price paid, eliminating the inside-outside basis disparity.

questions.stem: A partnership makes a distribution that results in a $25,000 downward adjustment under Section 734(b). For this adjustment to apply, what must be true?
options: The distribution must be to a corporate partner only
The partnership must be a publicly traded partnership
All partners must consent in writing each year
A Section 754 election is in effect, or a substantial basis reduction exceeding $250,000 exists
questions.rationale: Section 734(b) adjusts the basis of remaining partnership property after distributions when a 754 election is in effect or a substantial basis reduction over $250,000 mandates it.

questions.stem: In a disproportionate distribution involving Section 751(b) 'hot assets,' how are unrealized receivables and substantially appreciated inventory treated?
options: They convert to capital gain property in the distributee's hands
The disproportionate portion is treated as a taxable sale or exchange between the partner and the partnership, generating ordinary income
They are always distributed tax-free under Section 731
They are ignored unless the partnership has a Section 754 election
questions.rationale: Section 751(b) prevents partners from converting ordinary income into capital gain by treating disproportionate distributions of hot assets as taxable exchanges yielding ordinary income.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an 'unrealized receivable' constituting a hot asset under Section 751?
options: The right to payment for services already rendered by a cash-basis partnership but not yet collected
Marketable securities held for investment
Cash held in the partnership's operating account
Land held by the partnership for appreciation
questions.rationale: Unrealized receivables under Section 751 are amounts not yet included in income, like a cash-basis firm's uncollected receivables, carrying built-in ordinary income.

questions.stem: Partner B has an outside basis of $10,000 and receives a current (nonliquidating) cash distribution of $14,000. What is the tax consequence?
options: B recognizes no gain because current distributions are always tax-free
B recognizes $14,000 of ordinary income
B must reduce basis to negative $4,000 and carry it forward
B recognizes $4,000 of gain, generally capital, and basis is reduced to zero
questions.rationale: Under Section 731(a), a cash distribution exceeding the partner's outside basis produces gain (usually capital) equal to the excess, and basis cannot fall below zero.

questions.stem: An LLC with two members files Form 1065. One member wishes the LLC to be taxed as a corporation. What action accomplishes this?
options: Filing Form 8832 to elect classification as an association taxable as a corporation
Filing Form 1120 in any year the members choose
Amending the operating agreement, which automatically changes federal tax status
Filing Form 2553 directly without any prior election
questions.rationale: Under the check-the-box regulations, an eligible entity uses Form 8832 to elect association (corporate) status; default for a multi-member LLC is partnership.

questions.stem: An S corporation election terminates mid-year because a partnership becomes a shareholder, an impermissible shareholder. What is the consequence regarding the corporation's tax year?
options: The corporation must immediately liquidate
The entire year is treated as a C corporation year retroactively to January 1
The year splits into an S short year and a C short year, with income allocated between them
The entire year remains an S year and the termination is effective next year
questions.rationale: When S status terminates mid-year under Section 1362(d), the tax year divides into an S short year and a C short year with income allocated between them.

questions.stem: A former C corporation elected S status. During the recognition period it sells an asset that had a built-in gain at conversion. The built-in gain is $100,000 and the corporation's taxable income limitation is $70,000. What is the Section 1374 built-in gains tax base for the year?
options: $0, because S corporations never pay entity-level tax
$100,000, ignoring the taxable income limitation
$30,000, the difference between the two figures
$70,000, with the $30,000 excess carried over to a later recognition-period year
questions.rationale: Section 1374 limits the current built-in gains tax base to taxable income; the unused built-in gain carries over to later years within the five-year recognition period.

questions.stem: What is the current recognition period during which the Section 1374 built-in gains tax can apply after a C-to-S conversion?
options: 7 years
10 years
5 years
3 years
questions.rationale: The built-in gains tax recognition period is the 5 years beginning with the start of the first S corporation year.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a permissible shareholder of an S corporation?
options: A qualified subchapter S trust (QSST)
A C corporation
A partnership
A nonresident alien individual
questions.rationale: Permissible S shareholders include individuals (other than nonresident aliens), estates, and certain trusts such as QSSTs and ESBTs; corporations and partnerships are excluded.

questions.stem: An S corporation may have no more than how many shareholders, and how are family members treated for this count?
options: 75 shareholders, counting each family member separately
35 shareholders, with spouses treated as one
100 shareholders, counting each family member separately
100 shareholders, with members of a family treated as one shareholder
questions.rationale: An S corporation is limited to 100 shareholders, with family members treated as one shareholder under Section 1361.

questions.stem: A C corporation has a net operating loss carryforward and undergoes an ownership change as defined in Section 382. What does Section 382 limit?
options: Only capital loss carrybacks, not NOLs
The total lifetime NOLs to a fixed dollar cap of $100,000
The corporation's ability to file consolidated returns
The amount of pre-change NOLs that can offset post-change taxable income annually, generally to the value of the old loss corporation times the long-term tax-exempt rate
questions.rationale: Section 382 limits annual use of pre-change losses after an ownership change to the loss corporation's value times the long-term tax-exempt rate.

questions.stem: An individual sells qualified small business stock (QSBS) acquired in 2021 and held more than five years. The corporation was a qualifying C corporation. What is the general gain exclusion under Section 1202 for stock acquired in that period?
options: Up to 25% of the gain, capped at $1 million
0%, because only corporations may claim Section 1202
Up to 100% of the gain, subject to the greater of $10 million or 10 times basis cap per issuer
Exactly 50% of the gain, with no cap
questions.rationale: Section 1202 excludes up to 100% of QSBS gain for stock acquired after September 27, 2010, limited to the greater of $10 million or 10 times basis per issuer.

questions.stem: What is the minimum stock ownership requirement for a parent corporation to include a subsidiary in a consolidated federal return?
options: At least 60% of value only
More than 50% of voting power only
100% ownership of all subsidiaries
At least 80% of total voting power and 80% of total value
questions.rationale: Consolidated return eligibility requires the parent to own at least 80% of the vote and 80% of the value of each subsidiary.

questions.stem: Under Section 263A (UNICOP), a producer of inventory must capitalize which of the following into the cost of inventory?
options: A proper share of indirect costs such as purchasing, handling, and storage allocable to production
Interest on a loan unrelated to production property
Selling and advertising expenses
The owner's personal living expenses
questions.rationale: Section 263A requires capitalizing direct and an allocable share of indirect production costs into inventory; pure selling and general administrative period costs are excluded.

questions.stem: A small business with average annual gross receipts under the inflation-adjusted threshold (about $30 million for 2024) is exempt from which requirement?
options: Issuing Forms W-2 to employees
Filing any federal income tax return
Paying self-employment tax
The Section 263A UNICAP rules for inventory
questions.rationale: The small business taxpayer exemption (gross receipts under the inflation-adjusted threshold, ~$30 million for 2024) relieves a business of the Section 263A UNICAP requirements.

questions.stem: An accrual-basis taxpayer accrues a liability for services to be performed by another party. Under Section 461(h) economic performance, when is the liability generally deductible?
options: Only when cash is paid, regardless of the accrual method
When the taxpayer signs the contract
As the other party actually provides the services to the taxpayer
When the taxpayer first records the accrual on its books
questions.rationale: Under Section 461(h), economic performance for services provided to the taxpayer occurs as the services are rendered, fixing the timing of the deduction.

questions.stem: A cash-basis corporation accrues a year-end bonus to a more-than-50% shareholder-employee but pays it the following March. Under Section 267, when may the corporation deduct it?
options: In the year the board authorizes the bonus
In the year the related shareholder includes it in income
Never, because related-party payments are nondeductible
In the year of accrual, regardless of payment
questions.rationale: Section 267(a)(2) defers an accrual-basis payer's deduction on amounts owed to a related cash-basis payee until the payee includes the amount in income.

questions.stem: What is the maximum Section 179 expensing deduction for 2024, and at what total qualifying property amount does the phase-out begin?
options: $1,160,000 maximum, with phase-out beginning at $2,890,000
Unlimited expensing with no phase-out
$500,000 maximum, with phase-out beginning at $2,000,000
$1,220,000 maximum, with phase-out beginning at $3,050,000
questions.rationale: For 2024, Section 179 allows up to $1,220,000 of expensing, phasing out dollar-for-dollar above $3,050,000 of qualifying property.

questions.stem: A sole proprietor elects Section 179 of $50,000 but has only $30,000 of aggregate business taxable income before the deduction. What happens to the excess?
options: $30,000 is deducted currently and $20,000 carries forward due to the business income limitation
The excess $20,000 is permanently lost
The deduction is converted to bonus depreciation automatically
The entire $50,000 is allowed, creating a $20,000 loss
questions.rationale: The Section 179 deduction is limited to aggregate active business taxable income; amounts above that limit carry forward indefinitely.

questions.stem: What is the bonus depreciation percentage for most qualified property placed in service during 2024 under the TCJA phasedown?
questions.rationale: Under the TCJA phasedown, bonus depreciation is 80% for 2023, 60% for 2024, 40% for 2025, and 20% for 2026.

questions.stem: Unrecaptured Section 1250 gain attributable to depreciation on real property held by a noncorporate taxpayer is taxed at a maximum rate of what?
questions.rationale: Unrecaptured Section 1250 gain (prior depreciation on realty) is taxed at a maximum 25% rate for individuals.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sells Section 1245 equipment on the installment method for a $30,000 total gain, of which $18,000 is depreciation recapture. How is the recapture reported?
options: The recapture is deferred until the final payment
The $18,000 recapture is reported in full in the year of sale, even before cash is collected
The recapture is treated as capital gain
The recapture is spread ratably over the installment payments
questions.rationale: Under Section 453(i), depreciation recapture must be reported as ordinary income in the year of an installment sale, with only the remaining gain spread over collections.

questions.stem: In a like-kind exchange of real property under Section 1031, a taxpayer receives $12,000 of cash boot and has a realized gain of $20,000. How much gain is recognized?
options: $20,000, the full realized gain
$8,000, the difference between gain and boot
$12,000, the lesser of boot received or realized gain
$0, because Section 1031 is full nonrecognition
questions.rationale: In a Section 1031 exchange, recognized gain equals the lesser of boot received or realized gain; here $12,000.

questions.stem: A taxpayer uses the installment method to report gain on selling business land. The gross profit is $60,000 on a $200,000 contract price. What is the gross profit percentage applied to each payment?
questions.rationale: Under Section 453, the gross profit percentage (gross profit divided by contract price) applies to each installment payment to determine recognized gain.

questions.stem: Which method of accounting must generally be used for a C corporation (other than a qualified personal service corporation) with average annual gross receipts exceeding the inflation-adjusted threshold?
options: The cash method without restriction
The accrual method
The completed-contract method only
Any method the corporation prefers
questions.rationale: C corporations above the gross receipts threshold must use the accrual method; smaller businesses and qualified personal service corporations may use cash.

questions.stem: A business changes from an impermissible to a permissible accounting method, producing a negative Section 481(a) adjustment of $30,000 (a decrease in income). How is a negative adjustment generally taken into account?
options: Spread ratably over four years
Carried back three years
Fully in the year of change (the year of change deduction)
Spread over ten years
questions.rationale: Under Section 481(a), a negative adjustment is recognized fully in the year of change, while a positive adjustment is generally spread over four years.

questions.stem: A corporation contributes appreciated inventory (basis $4,000, FMV $10,000) to a qualified charity for the care of the ill, needy, or infants. What is the enhanced charitable deduction generally allowed under Section 170(e)(3)?
options: The $6,000 appreciation only
Basis plus half of the appreciation, not to exceed twice basis ($7,000 here)
Only the $4,000 basis
The full $10,000 fair market value
questions.rationale: Section 170(e)(3) allows corporations an enhanced deduction of basis plus half the appreciation (capped at twice basis) for qualifying inventory gifts.

questions.stem: A corporation owns 25% of another domestic corporation and receives a $40,000 dividend. What is the dividends-received deduction percentage?
questions.rationale: The dividends-received deduction is 50% for under-20% ownership, 65% for 20% to under 80%, and 100% for 80% or more.

questions.stem: For a net operating loss arising in a tax year beginning after 2020, what is the general carryover rule and the income offset limitation?
options: No carryforward, only a 3-year carryback
No carryback, indefinite carryforward, limited to 80% of taxable income
5-year carryback and unlimited carryforward
2-year carryback and 20-year carryforward with no percentage limit
questions.rationale: NOLs from years beginning after 2020 have no carryback, carry forward indefinitely, and are limited to offsetting 80% of taxable income.

questions.stem: For 2024, what is the Social Security (OASDI) wage base used to compute the employer and employee portion of FICA under Section 3121?
options: No limit
questions.rationale: For 2024, the Social Security wage base is $168,600; the Medicare portion has no wage ceiling.

questions.stem: What is the FUTA wage base per employee, and what is the standard net FUTA rate after the maximum state credit?
options: $10,000 wage base; 6.0% net rate
$15,000 wage base; 0.9% net rate
$7,000 wage base; 0.6% net rate after the 5.4% credit
$7,000 wage base; 6.0% net rate with no credit
questions.rationale: FUTA tax applies to the first $7,000 of each employee's wages at a 6.0% gross rate, reduced to 0.6% net after the 5.4% state unemployment credit.

questions.stem: An employer must begin withholding the additional 0.9% Medicare tax once an employee's wages exceed what threshold in a calendar year?
options: $200,000, regardless of the employee's filing status
$125,000 for single filers
$250,000 for all employees
$168,600 matching the Social Security base
questions.rationale: Employers must withhold the additional 0.9% Medicare tax on wages exceeding $200,000, regardless of the employee's actual filing status.

questions.stem: A shareholder transfers property to a controlled corporation in a Section 351 exchange. The property has a $30,000 basis and is subject to a $40,000 liability assumed by the corporation. What is the general consequence?
options: Gain of $40,000 is recognized for the full liability
Gain of $10,000 is recognized because liabilities assumed exceed the property's basis
No gain is recognized because Section 351 is fully tax-free
A $10,000 loss is recognized
questions.rationale: Section 357(c) requires gain recognition to the extent liabilities assumed by the corporation exceed the adjusted basis of the transferred property.

questions.stem: A complete liquidation of an 80%-owned subsidiary into its parent corporation is generally treated how under Section 332?
options: Taxable only to the subsidiary
Tax-free to the parent, which takes a carryover basis in the subsidiary's assets
Fully taxable to both the parent and subsidiary
Treated as a dividend to the parent
questions.rationale: Section 332 grants tax-free treatment when an 80%-owned subsidiary liquidates into its parent, with carryover basis under Section 334(b).

questions.stem: An S corporation shareholder has stock basis of $5,000 and a loan from the shareholder to the corporation (debt basis) of $3,000. The shareholder's share of the loss is $10,000. How much loss can the shareholder deduct currently?
options: $8,000, limited to combined stock and debt basis, with $2,000 suspended
$10,000, the full allocated loss
$5,000, limited to stock basis only
$3,000, limited to debt basis only
questions.rationale: An S shareholder may deduct losses up to the sum of stock basis and direct loan (debt) basis; excess losses are suspended and carried forward.

questions.stem: A partner's deductible share of partnership losses is limited by the order of three regimes. Which is the first hurdle applied?
options: The outside basis limitation under Section 704(d)
The passive activity loss rules under Section 469
The at-risk rules under Section 465
The excess business loss limit under Section 461(l)
questions.rationale: Partnership losses pass through the ordering of basis (704(d)), then at-risk (465), then passive (469), and finally the excess business loss limit (461(l)).

questions.stem: For 2024, the excess business loss limitation under Section 461(l) disallows net business losses exceeding what threshold for a married couple filing jointly (indexed amount)?
questions.rationale: Section 461(l) limits excess business losses to $305,000 (single) or $610,000 (MFJ) for 2024, with disallowed losses carried forward as an NOL.

questions.stem: Starting in 2022, the calculation of adjusted taxable income (ATI) for Section 163(j) changed. Which items are no longer added back in computing ATI?
options: Net operating loss deductions
Floor plan financing interest
Business interest income
Depreciation, amortization, and depletion
questions.rationale: From 2022 onward, depreciation, amortization, and depletion are no longer added back when computing ATI, tightening the Section 163(j) limitation.

questions.stem: Beginning in 2022, how must specified research and experimental (R&E) expenditures under Section 174 be treated?
options: Capitalized and never amortized
Deducted currently in full as before
Capitalized and amortized over 5 years (domestic) or 15 years (foreign)
Amortized over 3 years regardless of location
questions.rationale: Section 174 now requires capitalizing R&E expenditures, amortizing over 5 years (domestic) or 15 years (foreign) beginning mid-year of the year incurred.

questions.stem: A taxpayer may amortize qualifying business start-up costs by deducting up to what amount in the first year, with the rest amortized over 180 months?
options: $10,000 with no phase-out
$15,000 amortized over 60 months
$5,000 with phase-out beginning at $5,000
$5,000, reduced dollar-for-dollar when costs exceed $50,000
questions.rationale: Section 195 allows a $5,000 first-year start-up cost deduction (phased out above $50,000), with the balance amortized over 180 months.

questions.stem: A taxpayer places nonresidential real property in service in 2024 under MACRS. What is the recovery period and depreciation method?
options: 39 years, straight-line, mid-month convention
27.5 years, straight-line, mid-month convention
15 years, straight-line
39 years, 200% declining balance
questions.rationale: MACRS depreciates nonresidential real property over 39 years using straight-line and the mid-month convention.

questions.stem: Qualified improvement property (QIP) placed in service after 2017 is assigned what MACRS recovery period, making it eligible for bonus depreciation?
options: 15 years
39 years
20 years
7 years
questions.rationale: Qualified improvement property is 15-year MACRS property, restoring its eligibility for bonus depreciation after the CARES Act fix.

questions.stem: Distributable net income (DNI) under Section 643 generally serves what primary function in fiduciary income taxation?
options: It determines the trust's gross estate value
It sets the trustee's compensation
It limits the distribution deduction and the amount taxable to beneficiaries, and determines the character of distributions
It establishes the trust's basis in distributed property
questions.rationale: DNI under Section 643 ceilings the distribution deduction and beneficiary inclusion and carries through the character of trust income.

questions.stem: In computing distributable net income (DNI) for a typical trust, how are capital gains generally treated?
options: Generally excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust, unless allocated to income or distributed under the governing instrument or state law
Treated as tax-exempt interest
Always excluded and never taxable
Always included in DNI and taxed to beneficiaries
questions.rationale: Under Section 643, capital gains are generally allocated to corpus and excluded from DNI, being taxed to the trust unless allocated to income or distributed.

questions.stem: A complex trust may claim a personal exemption of what amount on Form 1041?
questions.rationale: On Form 1041, estates get a $600 exemption, simple trusts $300, and complex trusts $100.

questions.stem: Under the tier system for complex trust distributions, first-tier distributions consist of what?
options: Discretionary distributions of principal
Distributions of accumulated income from prior years
Amounts of income required to be distributed currently, taxed first up to DNI
Charitable contributions
questions.rationale: First-tier distributions (income required to be distributed currently) are taxed to beneficiaries up to DNI before second-tier discretionary distributions.

questions.stem: An exempt organization conducts a regularly carried-on trade or business not substantially related to its exempt purpose. The net income is subject to what?
options: Self-employment tax
No tax, because exempt organizations are never taxed
The accumulated earnings tax
Unrelated business income tax (UBIT), at corporate rates on Form 990-T
questions.rationale: Unrelated business taxable income is taxed under UBIT on Form 990-T to prevent exempt organizations from unfairly competing with taxable businesses.

questions.stem: What is the specific deduction allowed in computing unrelated business taxable income before applying the tax?
questions.rationale: Exempt organizations may take a $1,000 specific deduction in computing unrelated business taxable income.

questions.stem: Under the post-2017 'silo' rule for UBIT, how must an exempt organization with multiple unrelated trades or businesses compute UBTI?
options: Separately for each trade or business, so a loss from one cannot offset income from another
By electing whichever method yields the lowest tax
Only for the single largest activity
On a combined basis, netting all activities together
questions.rationale: Section 512(a)(6) silos each unrelated trade or business so losses from one cannot offset income from another.

questions.stem: Which income is generally excluded from unrelated business taxable income as passive income?
options: Dividends, interest, and royalties (absent debt-financing or controlled-entity rules)
Advertising income in the organization's periodical
Net income from an unrelated retail store operated daily
Income from a regularly operated unrelated parking garage
questions.rationale: Dividends, interest, and royalties are generally excluded from UBTI as passive income, subject to the debt-financed and controlled-entity exceptions.

questions.stem: At what gross receipts and total assets thresholds must an exempt organization file the full Form 990 rather than Form 990-EZ?
options: Gross receipts of $1,000,000 or more only
Gross receipts of $50,000 or more, or assets of $100,000 or more
Gross receipts of $200,000 or more, or total assets of $500,000 or more
Any organization with employees
questions.rationale: An exempt organization must file the full Form 990 when gross receipts reach $200,000 or total assets reach $500,000; otherwise Form 990-EZ may be allowed.

questions.stem: For 2024, what is the maximum elective deferral an employee may contribute to a 401(k) plan (excluding catch-up contributions)?
questions.rationale: For 2024, the 401(k) elective deferral limit is $23,000, with an additional $7,500 catch-up for those age 50 and over.

questions.stem: For 2024, a self-employed individual with a SEP-IRA may contribute up to what percentage of net self-employment earnings, subject to the overall dollar cap?
options: 50% of net earnings, capped at $30,000
Effectively 20% of net SE earnings (25% of net SE income after the SE tax and contribution adjustment), capped at $69,000
10% of gross receipts, capped at $50,000
100% of net earnings with no cap
questions.rationale: For 2024, a self-employed SEP contribution is limited to effectively 20% of adjusted net SE earnings, capped at $69,000.

questions.stem: Which retirement plan allows a small employer to make required matching or nonelective contributions and uses Form 5304-SIMPLE or 5305-SIMPLE to establish it?
options: A Roth IRA
A SIMPLE IRA plan
A traditional 401(k) with safe harbor
A defined benefit pension plan
questions.rationale: A SIMPLE IRA plan for small employers is established using Form 5304-SIMPLE or 5305-SIMPLE and requires employer contributions.

questions.stem: Income in respect of a decedent (IRD), such as a final paycheck, is taxed to whom?
options: The recipient (estate or beneficiary) who receives it, retaining its original character
Only the decedent on the final Form 1040
The employer who paid it
No one, because it is excluded from income
questions.rationale: Income in respect of a decedent is included in the income of the estate or beneficiary who receives it, retaining its character under Section 691.

questions.stem: A guaranteed payment to a partner for services is treated how by the partnership and the partner?
options: Deductible (or capitalized) by the partnership and ordinary income to the partner, regardless of partnership profits
A nondeductible distribution to the partner
Tax-free to the partner under Section 731
A dividend subject to the dividends-received deduction
questions.rationale: Guaranteed payments under Section 707(c) are fixed payments not dependent on profits, ordinary income to the partner and generally deductible by the partnership.

questions.stem: Under the centralized partnership audit regime (BBA), adjustments are generally assessed and collected at what level by default?
options: Only against the tax matters partner personally
At each partner's level automatically
At the partnership level, with the partnership paying an imputed underpayment unless it elects to push out
At the IRS national office without any partnership involvement
questions.rationale: The BBA centralized audit regime assesses adjustments at the partnership level via an imputed underpayment, unless the partnership elects to push out to partners.

questions.stem: What is the per-vehicle first-year depreciation cap (luxury auto limit) issue addressed by Section 280F for passenger automobiles, and how is it affected by bonus depreciation?
options: Section 280F caps annual depreciation on passenger autos, with an increased first-year cap when bonus depreciation applies
Section 280F allows unlimited first-year expensing of any auto
Section 280F applies only to vehicles over 14,000 pounds
Section 280F eliminates all depreciation on business autos
questions.rationale: Section 280F caps yearly depreciation on passenger autos, with a higher first-year ceiling when bonus depreciation is elected.

questions.stem: A taxpayer disposes of a passive activity in a fully taxable transaction to an unrelated party. What happens to the suspended passive losses from that activity?
options: They carry forward but remain passive indefinitely
They may only offset future passive income
They become fully deductible (against any income) in the year of the qualifying disposition
They are permanently forfeited
questions.rationale: Under Section 469(g), a fully taxable disposition of the entire passive interest to an unrelated party releases suspended passive losses against any income.

questions.stem: What is the deductible percentage of business meals (not entertainment) for 2024 when the meal is not lavish and the taxpayer is present?
questions.rationale: Business meals are generally 50% deductible in 2024; the temporary 100% restaurant deduction expired after 2022.

questions.stem: A taxpayer realizes $50,000 of gain on involuntary conversion of business property and timely reinvests $45,000 in qualifying replacement property under Section 1033. How much gain is recognized?
options: $50,000, the full gain
$0, because all gain is deferred
$45,000, the amount reinvested
$5,000, the amount of proceeds not reinvested
questions.rationale: Section 1033 defers involuntary conversion gain only to the extent proceeds are reinvested in qualifying property; the shortfall is recognized.

questions.stem: A net Section 1231 gain for the year is generally treated how, absent the lookback rule?
options: As ordinary income
As a short-term capital gain
As long-term capital gain
As tax-exempt income
questions.rationale: A net Section 1231 gain is treated as long-term capital gain, while a net 1231 loss is ordinary; the lookback rule can recharacterize gains as ordinary.

questions.stem: Under the Section 1231 5-year lookback rule, a current-year net 1231 gain is recharacterized as ordinary income to the extent of what?
options: All capital losses in the prior five years
The corporation's accumulated E&P
Nonrecaptured net Section 1231 losses deducted as ordinary in the five preceding years
Depreciation taken in the current year
questions.rationale: The Section 1231 lookback recharacterizes net 1231 gain as ordinary income to the extent of nonrecaptured net 1231 losses from the preceding five years.

questions.stem: A trust distributes property in kind to a beneficiary without electing to recognize gain. What is the general result regarding the trust's distribution deduction and the beneficiary's basis?
options: The beneficiary takes a stepped-up basis to FMV with no carryover
The trust recognizes gain and the beneficiary takes a fair market value basis
The distribution deduction and the amount taxed to the beneficiary are limited to the lesser of basis or FMV, and the beneficiary takes a carryover basis
The trust must always recognize gain on in-kind distributions
questions.rationale: Under Section 643(e), in-kind distributions generally pass at carryover basis with the deduction limited to the lesser of basis or FMV, unless the trust elects gain recognition.

questions.stem: A 501(c)(3) public charity must avoid private inurement. A transaction providing excess economic benefit to an insider may trigger what intermediate sanction?
options: Immediate loss of incorporation
The accumulated earnings tax
An excise tax on the disqualified person and possibly on organization managers under Section 4958
Self-employment tax on the charity
questions.rationale: Section 4958 intermediate sanctions impose excise taxes on excess benefit transactions, taxing the disqualified person and possibly the approving managers.

questions.stem: Marisol and Devon form an LLC and elect to be taxed as a partnership. Marisol contributes land with a fair market value of $80,000 and an adjusted basis of $30,000, subject to a $20,000 mortgage the partnership assumes. Assuming the partners share liabilities equally, what is Marisol's initial outside basis in her partnership interest immediately after contribution?
questions.rationale: Under Section 722, contributed property carries over at adjusted basis; a partner's basis is reduced by liability relief but increased by the share of partnership liabilities assumed under Section 752.

questions.stem: Which of the following business entities provides limited liability to all owners but is treated as a pass-through entity by default for federal income tax purposes when it has more than one member and makes no election?
options: A general partnership
A C corporation
A multi-member limited liability company (LLC)
A sole proprietorship
questions.rationale: A multi-member LLC is treated as a partnership by default under the check-the-box rules and combines pass-through taxation with limited liability for all members.

questions.stem: Trevor owns a 40% interest in the TLM Partnership with an outside basis of $25,000. The partnership distributes to him cash of $10,000 and inventory with a partnership basis of $22,000 in a current (non-liquidating) distribution. What is Trevor's basis in the inventory received?
questions.rationale: In a current distribution, cash reduces outside basis first; distributed property other than cash takes a basis limited to the partner's remaining outside basis under Section 732.

questions.stem: A partnership reports a guaranteed payment to a partner for services rendered. How is this guaranteed payment treated on the partnership return?
options: It is taxed as a capital gain to the receiving partner
It is a nondeductible distribution that reduces the partner's capital account only
It is a tax-free return of capital to the partner
It is deductible by the partnership (if it meets ordinary and necessary requirements) and is ordinary income to the receiving partner
