questions.stem: A partner sells her partnership interest for $120,000. Her outside basis is $70,000, and her share of the partnership's unrealized receivables (hot assets) accounts for $20,000 of the gain. How is the gain treated?
options: $50,000 of ordinary income, since the partnership holds receivables
$50,000 of capital gain, since an interest is a capital asset
$20,000 capital gain and $30,000 ordinary income
$20,000 ordinary income under §751; $30,000 capital gain
questions.rationale: The buyer's basis and the partnership's basis in assets may be adjusted if a §754 election is in effect.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a section 754 election by a partnership?
options: To adjust inside basis when an interest is sold or property is distributed
To change the partnership's tax year to a fiscal year
To elect S corporation status for the partnership
To elect out of the centralized partnership audit regime
questions.rationale: A mandatory adjustment applies when there is a substantial built-in loss, even without an election.

questions.stem: Several individuals transfer property to a newly formed corporation for 100% of its stock. One of them receives $10,000 cash in addition to stock. How does section 351 apply?
options: No gain on any part of the exchange, including the cash
No gain on the stock, but gain up to the $10,000 of boot
All gain is recognized, since cash was received
Gain is deferred until the corporation sells the property
questions.rationale: The corporation's basis in the property is the transferor's basis, increased by gain recognized.

questions.stem: A shareholder transfers property with a basis of $20,000 and subject to a $35,000 liability to a corporation in a section 351 exchange. What is the tax consequence of the liability?
options: $15,000 of gain, because liabilities exceed basis (§357(c))
$35,000 of gain, equal to the whole liability assumed
$20,000 of gain, equal to the basis of the property
No gain, since liabilities assumed are never treated as boot
questions.rationale: The shareholder's basis in the stock is zero in that case.

questions.stem: A C corporation receives a dividend from a 30%-owned domestic corporation. What dividends received deduction (DRD) applies?
options: 50%, because ownership is below 80%
No deduction is allowed on intercompany dividends
65%, because the ownership is 20% or more but less than 80%
100%, because the payor is a domestic corporation
questions.rationale: The deduction is limited to a percentage of taxable income unless the corporation has an NOL.

questions.stem: A C corporation has taxable income before charitable contributions and the DRD of $500,000, and makes $80,000 of cash contributions to qualified charities. What is the maximum charitable deduction for the year?
options: $50,000 (10% of taxable income); excess carries forward five years
$100,000 (20% of taxable income); the excess carries forward
$80,000, the full contribution, with no limit for corporations
$250,000 (50% of taxable income); the excess is lost
questions.rationale: The 2025 tax act adds a floor in 2026: contributions are deductible only to the extent they exceed 1% of taxable income.

questions.stem: A C corporation has capital losses of $15,000 and capital gains of $5,000 for the year. How are the capital losses treated?
options: Capital losses are disallowed
$3,000 is deducted against ordinary income, and the rest carries forward indefinitely
All $15,000 is deductible against ordinary income
$5,000 offsets the gains, and the $10,000 excess is carried back 3 years and forward 5 years
questions.rationale: Net capital gain of a corporation is taxed at the regular 21% rate.

questions.stem: A corporation distributes $50,000 to a shareholder. The corporation has current earnings and profits of $30,000 and accumulated E&P of $0. How much of the distribution is a dividend?
options: $30,000 is a dividend and $20,000 is a return of basis
$50,000 is a dividend
$0, because accumulated E&P is zero
$20,000 is a dividend and $30,000 is a return of basis
questions.rationale: Return of basis reduces the shareholder's stock basis, and any excess is capital gain.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to change the corporation's method of accounting for inventory from FIFO to LIFO. What form is generally required?
options: Form 8832, filed with the IRS to elect classification
Form 1128, filed within 30 days of the inventory change
Form 3115, filed with the IRS along with a user fee
Form 970, filed with the return for the first year of LIFO
questions.rationale: The LIFO conformity rule requires LIFO to be used in financial reports.

questions.stem: Which businesses may use the cash method of accounting under the small business gross receipts test?
options: Only businesses with fewer than five employees on payroll
One whose three-year average gross receipts are under the indexed limit
Any corporation that holds inventory during the year
Only sole proprietorships, whatever their size or receipts
questions.rationale: C corporations with receipts above the test generally must use accrual.

questions.stem: A newly formed LLC with two members files no election. How is it classified for federal tax purposes?
options: As a C corporation
As an S corporation
As a disregarded entity
As a partnership
questions.rationale: A multi-member LLC can elect to be an association taxable as a corporation.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is the sole member of an LLC that owns rental real estate. How is the LLC reported for income tax?
options: Schedule E of the owner's Form 1040
Form 1065, filed as a partnership return
Form 8832, which reports the LLC's income
Form 1120, filed as a corporate return
questions.rationale: The LLC may still need its own EIN for banking and employment taxes.

questions.stem: A sole shareholder of an S corporation also works full time for it but takes no salary, only distributions. What is the IRS's likely position?
options: Recharacterize part of the distributions as taxable wages
Treat the distributions as a gift from the corporation
Treat all of the distributions as taxable dividends
Disallow the S election automatically for the year
questions.rationale: Factors include duties, training, comparable pay, and time devoted to the business.
questions.source: Rev. Rul. 74-44; Watson v. United States

questions.stem: Which statement about family members and the 100-shareholder limit for an S corporation is correct?
options: Siblings count as separate shareholders, but cousins do not
Relatives in the same family can elect to count as one shareholder
All relatives count as a single shareholder with no election
A spouse is not permitted to hold stock in an S corporation
questions.rationale: A family aggregation is relevant only when the shareholder count approaches 100.

questions.stem: A C corporation merges into another corporation in a transaction that qualifies as a statutory merger under section 368(a)(1)(A). What is the general result for the target's shareholders?
options: All gain is recognized immediately on the exchange
The holding period restarts on the date of the merger
No gain or loss except boot received, and stock basis carries over
They recognize loss on the exchange, but never any gain
questions.rationale: Continuity of interest, continuity of business enterprise, and business purpose are required.

questions.stem: When a partnership distributes cash to a partner in a current (non-liquidating) distribution, when is gain recognized?
options: Only when the distribution is more than $10,000 in a year
When the cash exceeds the partner's outside basis in the interest
Whenever any cash is distributed to the partner
Never, since partnership distributions are always tax-free
questions.rationale: Marketable securities may be treated as money for this rule.

questions.stem: A partnership with two equal partners has a taxable year-end of June 30, while both partners are calendar-year taxpayers. Under the general rule, which tax year must the partnership adopt?
options: The year ending September 30, the middle of the range
A 52–53 week year ending near the end of November
A fiscal year of the partnership's own choosing
The calendar year of the partners who hold a majority interest
questions.rationale: A §444 election allows a limited deferral of up to three months with required payments (Form 8752).

questions.stem: What is the deadline to report a change in the responsible party for an entity with an EIN?
options: Within 30 days, using Form SS-4
No report is required
By the next return due date
Within 60 days, using Form 8822-B
questions.rationale: The responsible party is the person who controls or manages the entity.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to change a business's tax year from calendar year to a June 30 fiscal year. Which form generally begins the request?
options: Form 8832, Entity Classification Election
Form 2553, Election by a Small Business Corporation
Form 1128, Application To Adopt, Change, or Retain a Tax Year
Form 3115, Application for Change in Accounting Method
questions.rationale: A short period return is required for the transition period.

questions.stem: What is required for a corporation to be an affiliated group eligible to file a consolidated return?
options: Only foreign corporations may elect to file consolidated returns
Any two corporations that share common officers and directors
A parent that owns at least 51% of the subsidiary's stock
A parent owning at least 80% of vote and value of a subsidiary, plus an election
questions.rationale: Intercompany transactions are deferred and eliminated under the consolidated return regulations.

questions.stem: What is the effect of a corporation's liquidation under section 331 on a shareholder who receives property worth more than the stock basis?
options: Capital gain: value of property received less the stock basis
Ordinary income equal to the value of the property received
Dividend income up to the corporation's E&P
No gain is recognized by the shareholder on a liquidation
questions.rationale: A §332 liquidation of an 80% subsidiary into its parent is tax-free.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a requirement for a corporation to be a personal holding company (PHC)?
options: Ownership by a single partnership of all the stock
Five or fewer people own over 50%, and 60% of income is passive
At least 100 shareholders and all income from rents
Gross receipts of more than $50 million for the year
questions.rationale: PHC tax is in addition to regular corporate tax and can be avoided with dividends.

questions.stem: A new sole proprietor spends $12,000 on qualifying start-up costs before opening day. How much may she deduct in the first year the business begins?
options: The full $12,000 in the first year, with no limit
$12,000 amortized over 60 months, with no immediate deduction
Nothing now; all $12,000 is capitalized until the business is sold
$5,000 immediately, with the remaining $7,000 amortized over 180 months
questions.rationale: Start-up costs include investigation of the business, advertising before opening, and training employees. Organizational costs for a corporation or partnership follow a similar rule.

questions.stem: What percentage of the cost of business meals is generally deductible, and what is the treatment of entertainment expenses?
options: Meals are not deductible, and entertainment is 50% deductible
Meals and entertainment are both 100% deductible
Meals are generally 50% deductible, and entertainment is not deductible
Meals are 100% deductible, and entertainment is 50% deductible
questions.rationale: Substantiation requires the amount, time and place, business purpose, and business relationship.

questions.stem: A business owner gives a client a gift with a cost of $80 and a gift basket valued at $40 to another client. What is the maximum deduction for business gifts to each person?
options: $50 per recipient per year
$100 per recipient per year
The full cost, with no limit
$25 per recipient per year
questions.rationale: Gifts to employees may be excludable as de minimis fringe benefits if low-value.

questions.stem: A self-employed consultant drives 12,000 business miles. Which statement about the standard mileage rate is correct?
options: It already includes the cost of parking fees and tolls
It must be used in place of actual expenses every year after that
It may be used for any number of vehicles in a fleet of five or more
It may replace actual costs if chosen in the first year of business use
questions.rationale: Interest and taxes on the vehicle are included in the standard rate for the self-employed.

questions.stem: A business places depreciable equipment in service. More than 40% of the year's depreciable basis of personal property was placed in service in the last quarter. Which convention is required?
options: The half-year convention, applied to all property that year
The mid-quarter convention, applied to all personal property that year
The full-month convention, applied to real property only
The mid-month convention, applied to personal property only
questions.rationale: The mid-quarter convention treats property as placed in service in the middle of the quarter.

questions.stem: What is the MACRS recovery period for nonresidential real property placed in service, and which convention applies?
options: 15 years, using the mid-quarter convention
40 years, using the full-year convention
39 years, using the mid-month convention
27.5 years, using the half-year convention
questions.rationale: Land is not depreciable.

questions.stem: For property acquired after January 19, 2025, what is the bonus depreciation percentage under the 2025 tax act?
options: 100% for qualified property
questions.rationale: A taxpayer may elect out of bonus depreciation by class of property.

questions.stem: For property placed in service after 2024, what is the maximum section 179 deduction under the 2025 tax act, and when does the deduction begin to phase out?
options: $2,500,000, phasing out above $4,000,000 of property placed in service
$1,000,000, phasing out above $2,500,000 of property placed in service
$1,250,000, phasing out above $3,130,000 of property placed in service
$500,000, phasing out above $2,000,000 of property placed in service
questions.rationale: The deduction is limited to taxable income from the active conduct of the business.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has qualified improvement property (QIP) placed in service. What is its recovery period?
options: 15 years, straight line, and it is eligible for bonus depreciation
39 years, and it is not eligible for bonus depreciation
7 years, using 200% declining balance
27.5 years, using the mid-month convention
questions.rationale: Improvements for enlargement, elevators or escalators, and internal structural framework are excluded from QIP.

questions.stem: Section 197 intangibles such as goodwill acquired in a business purchase are amortized over what period?
options: They are not amortizable; they are deductible only on sale
15 years, ratably, beginning with the month of acquisition
5 years, ratably, beginning with the month of acquisition
10 years, declining balance, beginning with the month of acquisition
questions.rationale: Self-created goodwill is not amortizable.

questions.stem: Beginning in 2025, how are domestic research and experimental expenditures treated under the 2025 tax act?
options: They are not deductible by the business at all
Capitalize and amortize over 15 years, with no current deduction
Deduct currently, or capitalize and amortize over 60+ months by election
Amortize over 5 years, with no choice of any other method
questions.rationale: Small businesses may apply the change retroactively to 2022–2024 under transition rules.

questions.stem: A business has average annual gross receipts below the small business threshold. How does the §163(j) business interest expense limitation apply?
options: The limitation does not apply to the business
Interest is limited to 30% of adjusted taxable income
No interest is deductible
Interest is limited to 50% of gross receipts
questions.rationale: Beginning in 2025, ATI is computed without the deduction for depreciation, amortization, and depletion (EBITDA).

questions.stem: Under what circumstances does an employee reimbursement arrangement qualify as an accountable plan?
options: The employee reports the reimbursements as wages on Form 1040
Business connection, substantiation, and return of any excess advance
The employer reimburses only expenses that exceed $75 each
The employer pays a flat amount that the employee may simply keep
questions.rationale: Safe harbors: advances within 30 days, substantiate within 60 days, and return excess within 120 days.

questions.stem: What is the employer's share of Social Security and Medicare (FICA) tax rate on an employee's wages up to the Social Security wage base?
options: 7.65% on all wages, with no wage base
7.65%: 6.2% Social Security plus 1.45% Medicare
6.2% Social Security only
15.3%: 12.4% Social Security plus 2.9% Medicare
questions.rationale: FICA tax applies to wages, including tips and certain fringe benefits.

questions.stem: An employer's FUTA tax rate is 6.0% on the first $7,000 of wages per employee. What credit is available for timely state unemployment tax payments, and what is the resulting net rate?
options: A credit of 6.0%, producing a net rate of 0%
No credit is available
A credit of up to 5.4%, producing a net rate of 0.6%
A credit of up to 3.0%, producing a net rate of 3.0%
questions.rationale: FUTA is reported annually on Form 940 and paid by the employer only.

questions.stem: A new employer accumulates a $60,000 employment tax liability in a day during the deposit period. By when must the deposit be made?
options: Within 30 days after the end of the month of the payroll
Next business day if $100,000 accumulates; else on its normal schedule
At year end, along with the annual Form 944 filing
At the end of the quarter, along with filing Form 941
questions.rationale: The $100,000 next-day rule applies to the entire accumulated liability.

questions.stem: When are Forms W-2 and Form 1099-NEC (reporting nonemployee compensation) generally due to recipients and to the government?
options: January 31 after year end, for both recipients and the government
April 15 following the calendar year, for both forms
February 28 for recipients, and March 31 for the government
March 15 following the calendar year, for both forms
questions.rationale: Penalties depend on how late the filing is, and apply per form.
questions.source: IRC §6071(c); General Instructions for Certain Information Returns

questions.stem: For payments made after December 31, 2025, what is the minimum payment threshold for filing Form 1099-NEC or Form 1099-MISC?
questions.rationale: Backup withholding rules still apply to payees who do not furnish a TIN.

questions.stem: A service recipient treats a worker as an independent contractor. Which factor most strongly suggests the worker is an employee under the common-law test?
options: The worker is paid by the project and bears risk of loss
The worker provides her own tools and sets her own schedule
The worker offers services to the general public
The business controls how, when, and where the work is done
questions.rationale: Section 530 relief may protect a business that consistently treated workers as contractors with a reasonable basis.

questions.stem: Which form can employers with a very small annual employment tax liability (generally $1,000 or less) file instead of quarterly Form 941?
options: Form 945, Annual Return of Withheld Federal Income Tax
Form 940, Employer's Annual Federal Unemployment Tax Return
Form 944, Employer's Annual Federal Tax Return
Form 943, Employer's Annual Federal Tax Return for Agricultural Employees
questions.rationale: Employers may request to file Form 941 instead of Form 944.

questions.stem: A business with inventory uses the lower of cost or market method. In which situation can inventory be written down to a market value below cost?
options: Replacement cost is lower than the original cost of the goods
The owner estimates that prices will fall after year end
Goods are unsalable at normal prices and are offered at reduced prices within 30 days
The tax year is a 52-week year ending near year end
questions.rationale: A taxpayer using LIFO may not use the lower of cost or market.

questions.stem: An accrual-method business determines that a specific customer account of $4,000 is totally worthless. How does it deduct the bad debt?
options: As a nonbusiness short-term capital loss on Schedule D
As an addition to a reserve for bad debts at year end
As a business bad debt, deducted when wholly worthless, by specific charge-off
It is not deductible, since the income was already reported
questions.rationale: A cash-method taxpayer cannot deduct unpaid receivables since the income was never reported.

questions.stem: Which business credit requires the employer to submit Form 8850 to the state workforce agency within 28 days of the new employee's start date?
options: The work opportunity tax credit
The small employer pension plan startup credit
The research credit
The disabled access credit
questions.rationale: The credit is claimed on Form 5884 after certification is received.

questions.stem: A small employer with fewer than 25 full-time equivalent employees buys qualifying health coverage for its workers through the SHOP Marketplace. Which credit may be available?
options: The credit for employer-provided childcare on Form 8882
The small business health care tax credit on Form 8941
The work opportunity credit on Form 5884
The empowerment zone credit on Form 8844
questions.rationale: Coverage must be purchased through the SHOP Marketplace to claim the credit.

questions.stem: A company deducts a payment to a subcontractor but receives no Form W-9 and does not file Form 1099-NEC. What consequence may result?
options: Information return penalties, and backup withholding on later payments
A fine is imposed only on the subcontractor who got the payment
None, since the payment is deductible whether or not a 1099 is filed
The payment is disallowed in full for the entire year
questions.rationale: Collect Form W-9 before making the first payment to a contractor.

questions.stem: A partnership's Schedule K-1 reports $30,000 of ordinary business income, a $5,000 §179 deduction, and $2,000 of charitable contributions. How is each reported by an individual partner?
options: Income to Schedule E, §179 to Form 4562, and the gift as an itemized deduction
Only ordinary income is reported, and the other items are ignored
All three are reported together on the partner's Schedule C
All three items are netted into one amount reported on Schedule E
questions.rationale: Partner-level limitations include basis, at-risk, and passive activity rules.

questions.stem: A corporation's Schedule M-1 reconciles book income with taxable income. Which item is a reconciling difference?
options: Revenue treated identically for book and tax purposes
The number of employees working at the corporation
Cash on hand at the end of the corporation's tax year
Meals expense not deductible for tax but deducted in the books
questions.rationale: Corporations with total assets of $10 million or more file Schedule M-3 instead of M-1.

questions.stem: A business that discovers it overpaid employment taxes in a prior year should generally use which form to correct the Form 941?
options: Form 843, Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement
A second Form 941, marked 'amended' at the top of the form
Form 1040-X, Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return
Form 941-X, Adjusted Employer's Quarterly Federal Tax Return
questions.rationale: Use the adjustment process for underpayments or the claim process for overpayments.

questions.stem: A business pays a $1,500 penalty to the IRS for a late filing and a $400 parking ticket for an employee's delivery vehicle. How are these treated?
options: Both, as deductible taxes imposed on the business
Only the IRS penalty, since it relates to the business
Both, as ordinary and necessary business expenses
Neither; fines and penalties paid to a government are not deductible
questions.rationale: Parking tickets are fines for violating a law, even if incurred in business.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to deduct the business use of a car under the actual expense method. Which records are most important to preserve?
options: Only a signed statement from the taxpayer about use
A mileage log with date, place, purpose and miles, plus receipts
Only the year-end odometer reading for the vehicle
No records, since vehicles are exempt from substantiation
questions.rationale: Reconstructed logs are accepted only with corroborating evidence.

questions.stem: A rental real estate owner has $15,000 of net rental income and uses a safe harbor to treat a rental enterprise as a trade or business for the QBI deduction. What is one requirement of the safe harbor?
options: 250 or more hours of rental services per year, with separate records
A written lease of at least 30 years for each property
Ownership of the rental property through an S corporation
At least five separate rental properties held by the owner
questions.rationale: Triple net leases do not qualify under the safe harbor.

questions.stem: A taxpayer sells depreciable machinery used in the business for more than its adjusted basis. On which form is the sale reported?
options: Schedule C, Profit or Loss From Business
Form 4562, Depreciation and Amortization
Form 8949, Sales and Other Dispositions of Capital Assets
Form 4797, Sales of Business Property
questions.rationale: Section 1231 losses are ordinary, and §1231 gains are capital if there are no lookback losses.

questions.stem: What is the penalty that applies when a trust fund tax such as withheld income tax or employee FICA is not paid over to the IRS?
options: A flat $500 penalty imposed on the business entity only
The trust fund recovery penalty: 100% of the unpaid tax, on responsible persons
The 20% accuracy-related penalty imposed on the business
A 10% penalty imposed on the employees who were paid
questions.rationale: Responsible persons can include officers, owners, and signatories on bank accounts.

questions.stem: What is required for a taxpayer to elect out of the §263A uniform capitalization (UNICAP) rules?
options: Operate as a C corporation rather than a pass-through
File Form 8832 to classify the entity for tax purposes
Meet the small business gross receipts test
Own no inventory at any time during the tax year
questions.rationale: UNICAP generally requires capitalization of indirect costs of producing property.

questions.stem: A business changes its overall method of accounting from cash to accrual and has a $40,000 positive §481(a) adjustment. How is it generally taken into account?
options: Entirely in the year of change, taken as one amount
Ten years, in equal parts, starting in the year of change
Four years, one-fourth per year, starting in the year of change
It is not taken into account in computing income
questions.rationale: Form 3115 is filed to request the method change.

questions.stem: Which of the following qualifies as a deductible business expense for a sole proprietor?
options: Advertising costs to promote the business
Commuting costs between home and a regular workplace
The cost of a personal vacation
Fines for violating state safety laws
questions.rationale: Ordinary means common and accepted in the trade, and necessary means helpful and appropriate.

questions.stem: An S corporation's AAA is $50,000, and it has no C corporation E&P. It distributes $60,000 to its sole shareholder, whose stock basis is $80,000. What is the tax result for the shareholder?
options: $10,000 is a taxable dividend and $50,000 is tax-free
Tax-free; it reduces his stock basis from $80,000 to $20,000
$50,000 is tax-free and $10,000 is taxed as capital gain
The whole $60,000 is taxed as long-term capital gain
questions.rationale: Basis limits the tax-free portion of distributions, and AAA tracks previously taxed income.

questions.stem: A restaurant's employees report their customer tips to the employer each month. For which tips does the employer owe its share of FICA?
options: Only tips that the employer itself pays to employees
Only tips over $20 for the whole calendar year
None, since tips are never treated as wages for FICA
All tips that employees report to the employer
questions.rationale: Employers in food and beverage businesses may claim the FICA tip credit on Form 8846.

questions.stem: A business buys a heavy SUV (over 6,000 lbs. GVWR) for 100% business use. What limit applies to the §179 deduction for the vehicle?
options: The full price, with no limit on the amount
Only up to the annual §179 cap that applies to heavy SUVs
None; no §179 deduction is allowed for any vehicle
A fixed $10,000 limit that applies to all vehicles
questions.rationale: Bonus depreciation can apply in addition to the §179 limit.

questions.stem: A new charity expects annual gross receipts of $40,000 and total assets of $100,000. Which application for recognition of exemption may it use?
options: Form 1024, since it is a section 501(a) organization
Form 1023-EZ
Form 990-N, since receipts are under $50,000 a year
Form 8718, since assets are under $250,000
questions.rationale: Most other charities apply on the full Form 1023, filed electronically with a user fee.

questions.stem: An exempt organization earns $4,000 from a regularly carried-on business unrelated to its exempt purpose. What filing requirement applies?
options: Form 1120, since it is now treated as a corporation
No filing, since the income is small for the year
Form 990-N, to report the additional income
Form 990-T, since gross unrelated income reaches $1,000
questions.rationale: UBTI must come from a trade or business that is regularly carried on and not substantially related to exempt purposes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally excluded from unrelated business taxable income?
options: Profit from an unrelated bakery run every week
Dividends, interest, and royalties from passive investments
Rental income from property financed with debt
Income from selling advertising in a periodical
questions.rationale: Volunteer labor and donated merchandise are separate exceptions.

questions.stem: A private foundation has fair market value of noncharitable-use assets of $2,000,000. What is its approximate minimum distribution requirement under section 4942?
options: 1.39% of the assets, which is about $27,800
5% of the assets, which is about $100,000
2% of the assets, which is $40,000
10% of the assets, which is $200,000
questions.rationale: Qualifying distributions include grants and reasonable administrative expenses.

questions.stem: A substantial contributor sells property to a private foundation for more than fair market value. Which excise tax first applies?
options: A 10% tax on the amount involved, imposed on the self-dealer
A 5% tax on the foundation itself, imposed once
No tax at all, since the contributor is exempt
A flat 1.39% tax on the price the foundation paid
questions.rationale: Correction usually requires undoing the transaction and restoring the foundation to its prior position.

questions.stem: A public charity must show it receives broad public support. Under the general public support test, what percentage of support must come from the public?
options: At least 75%
At least 10%
At least 33⅓%
At least 50%
questions.rationale: The calculation uses a five-year period, and large donors' gifts are capped at 2% of total support.

questions.stem: A section 501(c)(3) organization wants to engage in some lobbying without risking its exempt status. Which election may it make?
options: A §501(h) expenditure test election on Form 5768
A §4947 election made on Form 4720
A §521 election made on Form 1028
A §527 election made on Form 8871
questions.rationale: Charities may not intervene in political campaigns for or against candidates at all.

questions.stem: A newly formed organization files Form 1023 within 27 months after the end of the month it was formed. What is the effect if it is approved?
options: The organization must refile each year
Recognition of exemption is retroactive to the date it was formed
Recognition is retroactive only for one year
Exemption begins only on the date the IRS approves it
questions.rationale: Donors may rely on retroactive recognition for deductions.

questions.stem: An exempt organization must make available its Form 990 for public inspection. How many years must the organization make its returns available?
options: The last three years
The last year only
Only for a year after filing
The last ten years
questions.rationale: Failure to comply can result in daily penalties.

questions.stem: A one-participant 401(k) plan has plan assets of $600,000 at the end of the year. Which annual filing generally applies?
options: Form 5500-SF, since the plan has over 100 participants
No filing, since the plan covers only the owner
Form 5330, since it is a defined contribution plan
Form 5500-EZ, since plan assets exceed $250,000
questions.rationale: Form 5500 is due the last day of the seventh month after the plan year ends, with a Form 5558 extension.

questions.stem: A participant in a qualified plan borrows from her vested account balance of $80,000. What is the maximum loan permitted without treating it as a distribution?
options: $80,000, the participant's entire vested balance
$10,000, the lowest of the statutory amounts
The lesser of $50,000 or 50% of the vested balance: $40,000
$50,000, whatever the size of the vested balance
questions.rationale: Level amortization is required, with payments at least quarterly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prohibited transaction under section 4975 for an IRA owner?
options: Borrowing money from the IRA
Naming a child as the IRA beneficiary
Taking a required minimum distribution
Rolling the IRA to another IRA
questions.rationale: Plan fiduciaries owe a 15% first-tier excise tax on prohibited transactions.

questions.stem: In a top-heavy plan, what is the general minimum contribution for non-key employees?
options: 3% of pay, or less if key employees receive a lower rate
10% of pay for every employee in the plan
No minimum, since top-heavy plans are exempt
A fixed $1,000 for every non-key employee
questions.rationale: Safe harbor 401(k) plans are generally exempt from top-heavy rules.

questions.stem: A U.S. person owns 12% of the stock of a foreign corporation. U.S. shareholders together own 60% of its stock by vote and value. Which statement is correct?
options: It is a PFIC by definition, so only Form 8621 applies
It is not a CFC, since the owner holds less than 50%
It is a CFC only if the 12% owner is a corporation
It is a CFC, and the 12% owner may need to file Form 5471
questions.rationale: Form 5471 has several filer categories and is filed with the income tax return.

questions.stem: A U.S. taxpayer owns shares of a passive foreign investment company (PFIC). Which form must generally be filed annually?
options: Form 3520, Annual Return To Report Transactions With Foreign Trusts
Form 8621, Information Return by a Shareholder of a PFIC
Form 8865, Return of U.S. Persons With Respect to Certain Foreign Partnerships
Form 5471, Information Return of U.S. Persons With Respect to Certain Foreign Corporations
questions.rationale: A PFIC meets an income test (75% passive) or an asset test (50% passive assets).

questions.stem: A foreign corporation operating a U.S. branch with effectively connected income must file which return?
options: Form 1042-S, the foreign person withholding statement
Form 1040-NR, the nonresident alien return
Form 1120, the same return a domestic corporation files
Form 1120-F, the foreign corporation income tax return
questions.rationale: Failure to file on time may forfeit deductions and credits.

questions.stem: A real estate investment trust (REIT) must meet which distribution requirement to be taxed as a REIT?
options: Distribute 100% of its income to avoid any tax
Distribute at least 50% of its gross income
Make no distribution, since REITs retain earnings
Distribute at least 90% of its REIT taxable income
questions.rationale: A REIT must have at least 100 shareholders and no more than 50% owned by five or fewer individuals.

questions.stem: When must an estate file Form 1041 for the estate's first tax year?
options: Gross income of $600 or more, or a nonresident alien beneficiary
The estate holds assets of more than $13 million
Always, even if the estate earned no income at all
The estate has at least $5,000 of income for the year
questions.rationale: An executor may choose a fiscal year, which can defer income to beneficiaries.

questions.stem: When is a federal estate tax return (Form 706) due for a decedent who died in 2025 with a gross estate above the filing threshold, and how may the due date be extended?
options: April 15 of the year after death, with a three-month extension
One year after death, with a two-year extension
Nine months after death, with an automatic six-month extension on Form 4768
Six months after death, with no extension
questions.rationale: Alternate valuation applies six months after death if elected and it reduces both gross estate and estate tax.

questions.stem: The surviving spouse of a decedent inherits the entire estate outright. What effect does this have on federal estate tax?
options: The transfer is taxed only if the spouse remarries
The transfer is taxed at the gift tax rate instead
The unlimited marital deduction removes estate tax on the transfer
Estate tax applies to the first $1,000,000 transferred
questions.rationale: A non-citizen spouse requires a qualified domestic trust (QDOT) to defer tax.

questions.stem: An individual in a chapter 7 bankruptcy case has assets that become part of the bankruptcy estate. Which statement is correct?
options: The debtor files Form 1120 for the estate
The estate files Form 1040 as part of the debtor's return
No return is ever required for the estate
The bankruptcy estate is a separate taxable entity that files Form 1041
questions.rationale: The estate uses the debtor's accounting method and may select a fiscal year.

questions.stem: A cash-method farmer prepays $60,000 for feed, and her other deductible farm expenses for the year are $90,000. What limit applies?
options: The full $60,000 in the year it is paid
None of it until the feed is actually used
Capped at 50% of other farm expenses, so $45,000 now
$30,000, one-third of the other farm expenses
questions.rationale: Farm syndicates face tighter limits on prepaid supplies.

questions.stem: A farmer sells part of her breeding herd because of a drought. How may she defer the gain?
options: Elect to treat the sale as a casualty loss deduction
Buy replacement property within 45 days under §1031
None; gain from livestock sold is always excludable
Buy replacement livestock within four years (longer if drought persists)
questions.rationale: The livestock must be held for draft, breeding, or dairy purposes, not for sale.

questions.stem: When must a taxpayer file Form 2290 for the heavy highway vehicle use tax, and for which vehicles?
options: By April 15 of the next year, for all trucks
By the end of the month after first use, for 55,000+ pounds
Each quarter, for vehicles weighing over 10,000 pounds
Never, since the heavy vehicle use tax was repealed
questions.rationale: Vehicles used less than 5,000 miles (7,500 for agricultural) are suspended from the tax but a return is still required.

questions.stem: A church that is a section 501(c)(3) organization elects to pay FICA for its non-minister employees by filing Form 8274. Under what condition may it make such an election?
options: The church is classified as a private foundation
The church wants to reduce its tax liability
Religious opposition to FICA, with the election filed before the first 941 is due
The church has more than 100 employees on payroll
questions.rationale: Church employees of electing churches pay SECA on their wages as self-employed.

questions.stem: For gift tax purposes, what is the effect of a married couple electing to split gifts on Form 709?
options: The donee reports the full gift as income on a return
The gift is tax-free whatever its size or number of donees
Each spouse is treated as making half, doubling the annual exclusion
The gift is taxed at the lower-income spouse's income tax rate
questions.rationale: Both spouses must be U.S. citizens or residents, and the election applies to all gifts in the year.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's investment in a qualified opportunity fund (QOF) is held for 10 years. What is the tax benefit?
options: Appreciation on the QOF investment is not taxed, via a basis step-up
The investment earns a credit of 20% against tax
The original deferred gain is permanently excluded
The amount invested is deductible from income
questions.rationale: Form 8997 reports QOF investments and Form 8949 reports the election.

questions.stem: A taxpayer owes tax on a cooperative patronage dividend. Which of the following is true about a cooperative's patronage dividends?
options: The co-op deducts qualified patronage dividends; patrons usually include them
Patronage dividends are always taxed as capital gains
Co-ops may not deduct any distributions to patrons
Patronage dividends are never taxable to patrons
questions.rationale: Patrons report them on the return as other income from Form 1099-PATR.

questions.stem: A business buys another business's assets for a lump sum. Under the residual method, which form reports the allocation among asset classes, and which class receives the residual amount?
options: Form 8594; the residual goes to Class III (receivables)
Form 8594; the residual goes to Class VII (goodwill)
Form 8832; the residual goes to Class I (cash)
Form 3115; the residual goes to Class V (inventory)
questions.rationale: Class I is cash, Class II is actively traded personal property, and Class VI is §197 intangibles other than goodwill.

questions.stem: A domestic LLC wants to elect to be taxed as an association (corporation) beginning on a date 40 days before it files the election. What does Form 8832 allow?
options: An effective date up to 30 days before the filing date
An effective date up to 75 days before the filing date
An effective date up to 12 months before the filing date
No retroactive effective date
questions.rationale: Late classification relief is available under Rev. Proc. 2009-41.

questions.stem: A partnership has nonrecourse debt on real estate that is secured by the property and owed to a qualified lender. How does the at-risk rule treat the partners' share of it?
options: At risk, as qualified nonrecourse financing on real property
Not at risk, since nonrecourse debt is never at risk
At risk only where each partner guarantees it personally
At risk for the general partners only, not limited partners
questions.rationale: Losses are limited to basis, then at-risk, then passive activity limits.

questions.stem: In what order are an S corporation shareholder's losses limited?
options: Basis, then at-risk, then passive activity, then excess business loss
Excess business loss, then passive, then basis, then at-risk
Passive activity, then at-risk, then basis, then excess business loss
At-risk, then excess business loss, then basis, then passive
questions.rationale: Disallowed losses carry forward indefinitely until basis is restored.

questions.stem: A foreign-owned U.S. disregarded entity (25% or more foreign owned) engages in reportable transactions with its foreign owner. Which form must it generally file?
options: Form 1120-F, the foreign corporation return
Form 8938, the foreign financial asset statement
Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120
Form 1042-S, the foreign person income statement
questions.rationale: The pro forma Form 1120 contains only the entity's identification information.

questions.stem: An S corporation makes a state-level pass-through entity (PTE) tax election and pays the tax at the entity level. How is the payment generally treated for federal purposes?
options: Treated as a distribution to shareholders, and not deductible
Deductible by the entity, which reduces income and avoids the SALT cap
Deductible only on the shareholders' individual returns
Nondeductible, and passed through to shareholders as a credit
questions.rationale: The 2025 tax act did not eliminate PTE taxes, though SALT cap treatment of SSTBs is restricted in some versions.

questions.stem: A business receives more than $10,000 in cash in a single transaction in its trade or business. Which form must it file, and by when?
options: Form 1099-K, due on the following January 31
Form 1099-B, due on the following February 28
Form 8938, filed with the income tax return
Form 8300, within 15 days of receiving the cash
questions.rationale: Cash includes currency and certain cashier's checks and money orders in some cases.

questions.stem: A small business wants to deduct, rather than capitalize, the cost of a $2,000 piece of equipment purchased from a single invoice. Which safe harbor may permit this?
options: The routine maintenance safe harbor for recurring repairs
The de minimis safe harbor election, up to $2,500 per item
The de minimis safe harbor election, up to $500 per item
The small taxpayer safe harbor for buildings, up to $10,000
questions.rationale: The election must be attached as a statement to the timely filed original return.

questions.stem: The 2025 tax act made the qualified business income deduction permanent. What additional benefit applies to taxpayers with at least $1,000 of qualified business income from active businesses?
options: A minimum deduction of $4,000
A minimum deduction of 5% of QBI
A minimum deduction of $400
A refundable credit of $400
questions.rationale: Taxpayers must materially participate to qualify for the minimum.

questions.stem: An employer pays an employee a bonus of $3,000 separately from regular wages and identifies it as supplemental wages. What flat withholding rate may the employer use for income tax on supplemental wages up to $1 million?
questions.rationale: Alternatively, the employer may aggregate the bonus with regular wages and use the regular withholding method.

questions.stem: A company reclassifies a worker as an employee after treating him as a contractor, and wants to pay the employment taxes at a reduced rate under a voluntary program. What is the program?
options: The Employee Retention Credit program
The Voluntary Classification Settlement Program (VCSP)
The Streamlined Filing Compliance Procedures
The Fresh Start initiative
questions.rationale: The employer files Form 8952 at least 60 days before the date it wants to treat workers as employees.

questions.stem: A business owner uses a vehicle for business 40% of the time. Which statement about depreciation on this listed property is correct?
options: Under 50% use, so only straight-line ADS, with no §179 or bonus
The owner may take 100% bonus depreciation on 40% of cost
The owner may use regular MACRS on 40% of the basis
The owner may take a §179 deduction on 40% of the cost
questions.rationale: Recapture applies if business use falls to 50% or less in a later year.

questions.stem: A partnership with an S corporation partner receives a Form 1099-NEC for services. How should the partnership report the income?
options: As partnership gross receipts, since the partnership is the payee
As income of the S corporation partner only
Not at all, since 1099-NEC income is never taxable
As the individual partners' wages from the partnership
questions.rationale: Nominee reporting may be used when income belongs to another person.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's corporation owns a rental property used by a shareholder personally at no charge. How is the benefit generally treated?
options: A return of capital to the shareholder in all cases
A charitable contribution deductible by the corporation
A constructive dividend to the shareholder, to the extent of E&P
A nontaxable business expense of the corporation
questions.rationale: Excess shareholder compensation or payments that are not at arm's length are often reclassified as dividends.

questions.stem: A small business wants a retirement plan that requires employer contributions of either a 3% matching contribution or a 2% nonelective contribution. Which plan has this feature?
options: A SIMPLE IRA plan
A defined benefit plan
A SEP-IRA
A profit-sharing plan with a vesting schedule
questions.rationale: SIMPLE IRA contributions are fully vested immediately.

questions.stem: Under the small taxpayer safe harbor for buildings, which building qualifies, and what is the annual limit on costs that may be deducted?
options: A building with a basis of $5 million or less; the lesser of $50,000 or 5% of basis
A building owned for over 10 years; 10% of basis
A building with an unadjusted basis of $1 million or less; the lesser of $10,000 or 2% of the basis
Any building; all repairs are deductible
questions.rationale: The election is made annually on the return.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to establish a solo 401(k) as a self-employed person with no employees. How are contributions structured?
options: Employee deferrals only, with no employer contribution allowed
Employee deferrals plus employer contributions of up to 20% of net SE earnings
A flat contribution of $5,000, whatever her earnings
Employer contributions only, limited to 5% of net earnings
questions.rationale: Plans with assets above $250,000 require annual Form 5500-EZ filings.

questions.stem: A one-owner S corporation provides health insurance to its 3% shareholder-employee. How is the premium reported?
options: Included in her W-2 wages, not FICA wages, with an above-the-line deduction
Treated as a nondeductible personal expense of hers
Reported to her as a dividend from the corporation
Excluded from wages as an employee health fringe benefit
questions.rationale: The premiums must be included in wages to qualify for the deduction.

questions.stem: Marcus is a newly enrolled agent who wants to understand which document governs his ethical conduct when practicing before the IRS. Which publication contains the regulations governing practice before the Internal Revenue Service?
options: The Internal Revenue Manual only
Treasury Department Circular No. 230
The Taxpayer Bill of Rights
IRS Publication 17
questions.rationale: Circular 230 is the foundational document setting forth the duties, restrictions, and sanctions applicable to those who practice before the IRS.

questions.stem: Which federal agency office is responsible for administering and enforcing the standards of conduct in Circular 230 for tax practitioners?
options: The Wage and Investment Division
The Criminal Investigation Division
The Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR)
The Taxpayer Advocate Service
questions.rationale: The Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR) is the IRS office charged with interpreting and enforcing Circular 230 standards and imposing discipline on practitioners.

questions.stem: A client asks enrolled agent Deborah to return all records the client provided so the client can file with another preparer, even though the client still owes Deborah's fee. Under Circular 230, what must Deborah do regarding the client's own records?
options: She must return only records she personally prepared, not those the client gave her.
She must promptly return any records of the client necessary for the client to comply with federal tax obligations, regardless of a fee dispute.
She may keep the records but must give the client copies for a charge.
She may keep all records until the fee is paid in full.
questions.rationale: Under Circular 230, a practitioner must promptly return a client's records needed to comply with federal tax obligations even when fees are in dispute, though state law may permit retention of work product the practitioner prepared.

questions.stem: Enrolled agent Tomas discovers that a return he is reviewing for a continuing client omitted $8,000 of interest income reported on a Form 1099-INT in a prior year already filed by another preparer. Under Circular 230, what is Tomas's duty upon learning of this error?
options: He must immediately notify the IRS of the omission.
He must refuse to do any further work for the client.
He must advise the client promptly of the error and the consequences of not correcting it.
He has no obligation because he did not prepare the original return.
questions.rationale: Circular 230 obligates a practitioner who learns of a client's error or omission to advise the client promptly of the error and its potential consequences; the decision to correct it rests with the client.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, which of the following types of fee arrangements is generally PROHIBITED for preparing an original tax return?
options: An hourly fee
A flat fee based on the complexity of the return
A fixed fee agreed to in advance
A contingent fee tied to the amount of the refund claimed on the original return
questions.rationale: Circular 230 generally bars contingent fees for preparing original returns, permitting them only in narrow situations like an IRS examination of a return, certain refund claims, or judicial proceedings.

questions.stem: Circular 230 imposes a duty of due diligence. When may a practitioner generally rely in good faith on information furnished by a client without independent verification?
options: When the information appears reasonable and the practitioner has no reason to believe it is incorrect or incomplete
Only for returns under $50,000 of income
Never; the practitioner must always verify every figure with third-party documents.
Only if the client signs an affidavit
questions.rationale: Under Circular 230, a practitioner may rely in good faith on information from the client but must make reasonable inquiries when the information appears incorrect, inconsistent with other facts, or incomplete.

questions.stem: The Office of Professional Responsibility can impose sanctions under Circular 230. Which of the following is NOT a sanction available to OPR against a practitioner?
options: Suspension from practice before the IRS
Imprisonment of the practitioner
Censure (a public reprimand)
A monetary penalty
questions.rationale: Circular 230 sanctions imposed by OPR include censure, suspension, disbarment, and monetary penalties; imprisonment is a criminal consequence handled by the courts, not OPR.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner who is disbarred from practice before the IRS is in what status?
options: Permanently allowed to practice with a warning on file
Temporarily barred but may reapply after 30 days
Required only to complete additional continuing education
Barred from practice and may petition for reinstatement only after at least five years
questions.rationale: Disbarment removes a practitioner from practice before the IRS, and reinstatement may be requested only after a minimum period (generally five years) and at OPR's discretion.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, when a practitioner gives written advice on a federal tax matter, the practitioner generally must do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Base the advice on reasonable factual and legal assumptions
Not rely on representations that the practitioner knows are unreasonable
Guarantee that the IRS will accept the position
Reasonably consider all relevant facts the practitioner knows or should know
questions.rationale: Circular 230 written advice standards require reasonable factual and legal assumptions, consideration of relevant facts, and no reliance on unreasonable representations, but they never require or permit a guarantee of the IRS result.

questions.stem: Circular 230 prohibits a practitioner from charging an 'unconscionable fee' for representation before the IRS. Which best describes an unconscionable fee?
options: Any fee above $500
A fee grossly excessive in relation to the services provided under the circumstances
Any contingent fee
Any fee charged before services are rendered
questions.rationale: Circular 230 bars unconscionable fees, which are evaluated by whether the fee is grossly excessive relative to the services provided rather than by any fixed dollar figure.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent is preparing a return that takes a position the agent believes is reasonable but the IRS would likely challenge. Under Circular 230, a practitioner generally may not advise a position on a return unless there is, at a minimum, what standard supporting it (absent disclosure)?
options: A reasonable basis with adequate disclosure, or substantial authority without disclosure
Absolute certainty the position will prevail
A more-likely-than-not standard in every case
A frivolous basis
questions.rationale: Under the return-position standards tied to Circular 230 and the Code, a practitioner generally needs substantial authority for an undisclosed position or at least a reasonable basis if the position is adequately disclosed; frivolous positions are prohibited.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, which of the following individuals is generally considered a 'practitioner' authorized to practice before the IRS?
options: A friend of the taxpayer with a financial power of attorney for banking only
A bookkeeper who only records transactions
An enrolled agent in active status
An unenrolled person with no credentials who prepared a return
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents, along with attorneys and CPAs, are practitioners under Circular 230 with unlimited rights to represent taxpayers before the IRS.

questions.stem: Circular 230 requires practitioners to exercise diligence about accuracy. Which behavior would most clearly violate the requirement to not engage in 'incompetence and disreputable conduct'?
options: Asking a client follow-up questions about inconsistent figures
Timely filing a client's return after gathering needed documents
Willfully assisting a client in evading taxes the client knows are owed
Declining to take a position the agent believes is frivolous
questions.rationale: Disreputable conduct under Circular 230 includes willfully assisting a client to evade taxes, and such conduct exposes the practitioner to censure, suspension, or disbarment.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a monetary penalty for a violation may be imposed not only on the individual practitioner but also on the practitioner's employer, firm, or other entity if the firm knew or should have known of the conduct. What is the maximum monetary penalty that may be imposed for such a violation?
options: A flat $5,000 per violation
Triple the tax owed
Up to the amount of gross income derived (or to be derived) from the conduct giving rise to the penalty
Up to $1,000 regardless of benefit
questions.rationale: Circular 230 authorizes a monetary penalty against a practitioner, and potentially the firm, up to the gross income derived or to be derived from the conduct subject to the penalty.

questions.stem: Which IRS form is used to authorize a representative to receive and inspect confidential tax information AND to represent a taxpayer before the IRS?
options: Form 4506, Request for Copy of Tax Return
Form 8821, Tax Information Authorization
Form W-9, Request for Taxpayer Identification Number
Form 2848, Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative
questions.rationale: Form 2848 (Power of Attorney) authorizes representation before the IRS, while Form 8821 only allows a designee to inspect or receive tax information without representing the taxpayer.

questions.stem: Which form authorizes a person only to inspect or receive a taxpayer's confidential tax information, but does NOT allow that person to advocate or represent the taxpayer before the IRS?
options: Form 2848
Form 1040-X
Form 9465
Form 8821, Tax Information Authorization
questions.rationale: Form 8821 authorizes only inspection or receipt of confidential tax information; it does not grant power to represent the taxpayer, which would require Form 2848.

questions.stem: On Form 2848, a representative must complete the Declaration of Representative section indicating the capacity in which they may practice. An enrolled agent should generally designate which capacity?
options: Attorney
Enrolled Agent
Certified Public Accountant
Unenrolled Return Preparer
questions.rationale: On Form 2848, each representative must accurately state their professional capacity; an enrolled agent selects the Enrolled Agent designation, which carries unlimited practice rights.

questions.stem: A taxpayer signs a Form 2848 appointing an enrolled agent for the 2023 Form 1040. Later the IRS begins examining the 2024 Form 1040. What is the effect of the existing power of attorney on the 2024 examination?
options: The Form 2848 covers any year as long as it is the same type of tax.
The Form 2848 covers 2024 because it is the next year.
The Form 2848 automatically covers all future years.
The Form 2848 does not cover the 2024 examination; a new authorization listing 2024 is generally required.
questions.rationale: Form 2848 only authorizes representation for the specific tax matters, forms, and periods listed; a new or amended authorization is needed to cover a year not originally specified.

questions.stem: Under the Taxpayer Bill of Rights, a taxpayer being interviewed by the IRS has the right to do what regarding representation?
options: Suspend an interview to consult with an authorized representative such as an enrolled agent
Require the IRS to conduct the interview only in writing
Refuse all contact with the IRS indefinitely
Demand that the IRS pay for an attorney
questions.rationale: The Taxpayer Bill of Rights includes the right to retain representation and to suspend an interview to consult an authorized representative who can practice before the IRS.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent holds a valid Form 2848 for a taxpayer. The IRS revenue agent insists the taxpayer must personally appear and answer questions even though the agent is fully representing the matter. Which statement is correct?
options: The representative's authorization is void if the taxpayer declines to appear.
The taxpayer must always appear in person for any examination.
The IRS generally cannot require a represented taxpayer to appear, but it may issue an administrative summons to compel the taxpayer's attendance when necessary.
A taxpayer can never be required to appear if represented.
questions.rationale: A valid power of attorney generally allows the representative to handle the matter so the taxpayer need not appear, but the IRS may issue a summons to compel the taxpayer's attendance or production of records when warranted.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent wants to be notified and receive copies of IRS notices for a client. On Form 2848, what must the representative do to receive copies of notices and communications?
options: Nothing; representatives automatically receive all notices.
File a separate Form 4506-T.
Submit a written letter to the IRS Commissioner.
Check the box authorizing the representative to receive copies of notices and communications.
questions.rationale: To receive copies of IRS notices, the representative must affirmatively check the box on Form 2848; otherwise notices may go only to the taxpayer.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the representation rights of an enrolled agent before the IRS?
options: Rights only for the returns the agent personally prepared
Rights only before the IRS Appeals office
Unlimited representation rights before any IRS office
Limited rights, similar to an unenrolled preparer
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents, like attorneys and CPAs, enjoy unlimited representation rights, allowing them to represent any taxpayer on any matter before any IRS office.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to revoke a previously filed Form 2848 without naming a new representative. Which method does NOT properly revoke the prior authorization?
options: Filing a new Form 2848 that revokes prior authorizations for the same matters
Writing 'REVOKE' across a copy of the prior Form 2848, signing it, and submitting it to the IRS
Sending the IRS a signed statement of revocation that identifies the representative and the matters
Simply telling the representative verbally without notifying the IRS
questions.rationale: To revoke a power of attorney, the taxpayer must notify the IRS in writing (or file a new Form 2848); a verbal statement to the representative alone does not update IRS records.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent represents both a husband and wife who filed a joint return but are now divorcing and have conflicting interests in the audit. Under Circular 230, what must the practitioner generally do regarding this conflict of interest?
options: Represent both only if the practitioner reasonably believes they can provide competent, diligent representation and each affected client gives informed written consent
Continue representing both with no disclosure necessary
Withdraw immediately in every case
Represent only the spouse who hired the agent first
questions.rationale: Under Circular 230 conflict-of-interest rules, a practitioner may represent clients with conflicting interests only with reasonable belief of competent representation, legality, and informed written consent from each affected client, retained for at least 36 months.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, when a practitioner obtains informed written consent to a conflict of interest, how long must the practitioner retain the written consents?
options: 12 months from the date of the consent
Only until the return is filed
Indefinitely with no end date
At least 36 months from the conclusion of the representation
questions.rationale: Circular 230 requires that informed written consents to conflicts be retained for at least 36 months after the representation ends and be made available to the IRS upon request.

questions.stem: The IRS centralized authorization system records third-party authorizations. What is this system commonly known as?
options: The IMF (Individual Master File)
The AUR (Automated Underreporter) system
The CAF (Centralized Authorization File)
The TIN matching system
questions.rationale: The Centralized Authorization File (CAF) is the IRS database that records Forms 2848 and 8821 so the IRS can confirm who is authorized to act for a taxpayer.

questions.stem: After an IRS examination concludes with proposed changes the taxpayer disagrees with, the taxpayer generally receives a letter offering the opportunity to appeal within the IRS. This letter is commonly called what?
options: A Final Notice of Intent to Levy
A CP2000 notice
A 90-day letter (Notice of Deficiency)
A 30-day letter
questions.rationale: The 30-day letter proposes examination changes and invites the taxpayer to appeal within the IRS by requesting an Appeals conference within 30 days.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wishes to appeal proposed examination changes by filing a formal written protest. A formal written protest is generally required when the total amount of proposed additional tax, penalties, and interest for any tax period exceeds what threshold?
questions.rationale: When the proposed amount for any tax period exceeds $25,000, a formal written protest is generally required to obtain an Appeals conference; smaller amounts may qualify for a small case request.

questions.stem: A taxpayer pays a disputed tax in full, files a claim for refund, and the IRS denies it. To pursue the matter in a court other than the U.S. Tax Court, where may the taxpayer file a refund suit?
options: In a state tax court
Only in the U.S. Tax Court
In the U.S. Court of Appeals as a court of first instance
In a U.S. District Court or the U.S. Court of Federal Claims after paying the tax and filing a refund claim
questions.rationale: Unlike the Tax Court, which hears cases before payment, refund litigation requires full payment and a denied (or aged) refund claim, after which suit may be filed in a U.S. District Court or the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.

questions.stem: A taxpayer owes back taxes and cannot full-pay but can pay over time. Which arrangement allows the taxpayer to pay the liability in monthly amounts?
options: Currently Not Collectible status
An Installment Agreement
A Notice of Federal Tax Lien
An Offer in Compromise
questions.rationale: An Installment Agreement permits a taxpayer to pay an outstanding tax liability through scheduled monthly payments rather than in a lump sum.

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer owes $40,000 in combined tax, penalties, and interest and wants a streamlined installment agreement without submitting detailed financial information. Generally, a streamlined installment agreement for an individual is available when the assessed balance is at or below what amount?
questions.rationale: Streamlined installment agreements for individuals are generally available for assessed balances of $50,000 or less, allowing approval without detailed financial statements when payable within the permitted timeframe.

questions.stem: The IRS may accept an Offer in Compromise on three grounds. Which of the following is NOT a recognized ground for an Offer in Compromise?
options: Effective tax administration
Doubt as to liability
Convenience of the taxpayer to avoid filing
Doubt as to collectibility
questions.rationale: The three statutory grounds for an Offer in Compromise are doubt as to liability, doubt as to collectibility, and effective tax administration; taxpayer convenience is not a basis.

questions.stem: A taxpayer is experiencing a serious financial hardship and cannot pay any amount toward an outstanding liability. The IRS may temporarily suspend active collection by placing the account in which status?
options: Trust Fund Recovery
Substitute for Return
Currently Not Collectible (CNC)
Innocent Spouse Relief
questions.rationale: When a taxpayer cannot pay due to financial hardship, the IRS may report the account Currently Not Collectible, suspending active collection while interest and penalties continue to accrue.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a federal tax lien and a federal tax levy?
options: A lien is a legal claim against property to secure a tax debt; a levy is the actual seizure of property to satisfy the debt.
A levy only applies to real estate; a lien only applies to wages.
A lien physically seizes property; a levy is just a public notice.
They are identical and interchangeable terms.
questions.rationale: A federal tax lien is the government's legal claim against a taxpayer's property securing a debt, whereas a levy is the actual seizure of property or rights to satisfy that debt.

questions.stem: The Trust Fund Recovery Penalty may be assessed against a 'responsible person' who willfully fails to collect or pay over certain taxes. To which taxes does this penalty primarily apply?
options: Federal estate taxes
The withheld income and employee FICA portions of employment taxes (the trust fund portion)
Self-employment taxes only
Federal excise taxes on fuel
questions.rationale: The Trust Fund Recovery Penalty targets the trust fund portion of employment taxes, withheld income tax and the employee share of FICA, and can be assessed personally against responsible persons who willfully fail to pay it over.

questions.stem: What number must a paid tax return preparer obtain and include on returns they prepare for compensation?
options: An EFIN only
A CAF number
A PTIN (Preparer Tax Identification Number)
The taxpayer's Social Security number as their own
questions.rationale: Paid return preparers must obtain a Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN) and sign returns they prepare for compensation using that PTIN.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A tax preparer who files returns electronically must obtain authorization from the IRS to participate in IRS e-file. What identifier does the IRS issue to an accepted e-file provider?
options: An EIN
An EFIN (Electronic Filing Identification Number)
A PTIN
An ITIN
questions.rationale: To participate in IRS e-file, a provider must apply and receive an Electronic Filing Identification Number (EFIN) after passing the IRS suitability check.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Which form is used by a taxpayer to authorize an Electronic Return Originator to electronically file the taxpayer's individual income tax return and to authorize a signature via PIN?
options: Form 2848
Form 8821
Form 4868
Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization
questions.rationale: Form 8879 is the IRS e-file Signature Authorization that lets the taxpayer authorize the ERO to e-file the return using a personal identification number as the signature.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A paid preparer completes a client's return for compensation but fails to sign it. Under the Internal Revenue Code, the preparer may be subject to which type of consequence?
options: Automatic disbarment
Criminal prosecution in all cases
No consequence because signing is optional
A preparer penalty for failure to sign the return
questions.rationale: The Code imposes a penalty on a paid preparer who fails to sign a return prepared for compensation, separate from any Circular 230 discipline.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A preparer claims the Earned Income Tax Credit on a client's return. Under the due diligence requirements, the preparer must complete and retain which form and supporting records?
options: Schedule EIC only
Form 8862
Form 8867, Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist
Form W-7
questions.rationale: Paid preparers must complete and retain Form 8867 and document the basis for credits like the EITC; failure to meet due diligence can result in a penalty per failure.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A preparer must keep records of due diligence for credits like the EITC. For how long must the preparer generally retain the Form 8867 and the records used to determine eligibility and the credit amount?
options: 1 year from the due date of the return
Indefinitely
3 years from the latest of the return due date, the date the return was filed, or the date it was presented to the taxpayer
7 years from filing
questions.rationale: Due diligence records, including Form 8867, must generally be retained for three years from the latest of the return due date, the date filed, or the date presented to the taxpayer for signature.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: If a taxpayer's electronically filed return is rejected and cannot be retransmitted electronically, what is the generally accepted procedure for the preparer to ensure the return is timely filed?
options: Wait until next year and combine the returns
File a paper return by the later of the due date or within the IRS-prescribed perfection period after rejection
Resubmit only after the IRS sends a paper notice
Do nothing because rejection cancels the filing obligation
questions.rationale: When an e-filed return is rejected and cannot be retransmitted, submitting a paper return within the IRS perfection period (or by the original due date if later) is the accepted way to maintain a timely filing.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: To maintain active enrollment, an enrolled agent must renew enrollment and meet continuing education requirements. How many total hours of continuing education are generally required during each three-year enrollment cycle?
options: 48 hours
72 hours
16 hours
120 hours
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents must complete 72 hours of CE per three-year cycle, with at least 16 hours each year and a minimum of 2 hours of ethics annually.

questions.stem: Among the annual continuing education hours an enrolled agent must complete, how many hours each year must be devoted to ethics or professional conduct?
options: 0 hours
8 hours
16 hours
2 hours
questions.rationale: Within the 72-hour, three-year CE requirement, enrolled agents must complete at least 2 hours of ethics or professional conduct CE each year.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent's renewal cycle is determined by the last digit of their Social Security number. If an enrolled agent fails to renew and complete CE, what is a likely consequence?
options: Immediate criminal charges
Placement in inactive status and loss of eligibility to practice until reinstated
Automatic conversion to attorney status
A permanent ban with no possibility of reinstatement
questions.rationale: Failing to renew or meet CE requirements generally results in inactive status, during which the enrolled agent may not practice until enrollment is properly renewed.

questions.stem: An individual who has passed the Special Enrollment Examination wants to become an enrolled agent. Beyond passing the exam and applying, what suitability requirement must the candidate satisfy?
options: Pass a tax compliance and background suitability check, including being current on personal tax filing and payment obligations
Have at least 10 years of prior IRS employment
Maintain a minimum net worth of $100,000
Hold a state CPA license
questions.rationale: Enrollment requires passing a suitability and tax compliance check; candidates must be current with their own federal tax obligations and free of disqualifying conduct.

questions.stem: What is the general statute of limitations period during which the IRS may assess additional tax after a return is filed, absent fraud, a substantial omission, or an unfiled return?
options: 6 years
10 years
3 years
1 year
questions.rationale: The general assessment statute of limitations is 3 years; a 6-year period applies to a substantial (over 25%) omission of gross income, and there is no limit for fraud or an unfiled return.

questions.stem: The IRS generally has how long to collect an assessed tax liability before the collection statute expires (absent events that suspend or extend it)?
options: There is no time limit on collection
6 years from assessment
3 years from assessment
10 years from the date of assessment
questions.rationale: The collection statute generally runs 10 years from the date of assessment; actions such as bankruptcy, offers in compromise, or CDP hearings can suspend or extend that period.

questions.stem: A taxpayer requests abatement of a penalty, asserting they relied on incorrect written advice from the IRS. This is an example of seeking penalty relief based on what?
options: Frivolous filing
An installment agreement
Reasonable cause / reliance grounds
An offer in compromise
questions.rationale: Penalties may be abated for reasonable cause, including reliance on erroneous IRS written advice, when the taxpayer acted in good faith and with ordinary business care.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: The First-Time Abate (FTA) administrative waiver may relieve certain penalties. Which condition is generally required to qualify for First-Time Abate?
options: The taxpayer must have a clean penalty history for the prior three years and be current on filing and payment requirements.
The taxpayer must be a corporation only.
The taxpayer must have an open Offer in Compromise.
