The taxpayer must have at least one prior penalty in the last year.
questions.rationale: First-Time Abate is an administrative waiver available when the taxpayer has a clean compliance history (no significant penalties in the prior three years) and is current on filing and payment obligations.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A preparer suspects a client is a victim of tax-related identity theft because the IRS rejected the e-filed return as a duplicate Social Security number filing. Which form does the affected taxpayer generally submit to report the identity theft to the IRS?
options: Form 56, Notice Concerning Fiduciary Relationship
Form 911, Request for Taxpayer Advocate Service Assistance
Form 8822, Change of Address
Form 14039, Identity Theft Affidavit
questions.rationale: Taxpayers report suspected tax-related identity theft to the IRS using Form 14039, the Identity Theft Affidavit, often after a rejected duplicate-SSN e-file.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: An IRS Identity Protection PIN (IP PIN) is a tool to combat identity theft. What is its primary function?
options: It is the preparer's signature code.
It is a six-digit number that helps verify the taxpayer's identity so that only they can file a return using their SSN.
It authorizes the IRS to issue refunds faster.
It replaces the taxpayer's Social Security number permanently.
questions.rationale: The IRS Identity Protection PIN is a six-digit number issued to eligible taxpayers to verify identity and block fraudulent returns filed under their Social Security number.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Circular 230 places limits on how practitioners may advertise and solicit clients. Which advertising practice is generally PROHIBITED?
options: Publishing accurate fee information for routine services
Advertising availability for consultations
Making false, fraudulent, or misleading claims about the practitioner's services or results
Listing the practitioner's enrolled agent designation truthfully
questions.rationale: Circular 230 permits truthful advertising but prohibits any false, fraudulent, misleading, or deceptive statements about the practitioner's services, qualifications, or results.

questions.stem: An unenrolled return preparer who participates in the IRS Annual Filing Season Program (AFSP) and holds a Record of Completion has what representation rights?
options: Unlimited representation rights identical to an enrolled agent
Rights to represent any taxpayer before Appeals and Counsel
Limited rights to represent clients whose returns they prepared and signed, before certain IRS personnel such as revenue agents and customer service representatives
No representation rights at all
questions.rationale: AFSP participants holding a Record of Completion have limited representation rights, covering only returns they prepared and signed and only before certain IRS employees such as examiners and customer service representatives, not Appeals or Collection.

questions.stem: During an IRS examination, the taxpayer's representative believes the revenue agent's proposed adjustment is unsupported. Before the case goes to Appeals, what is an appropriate step the representative can take with the examination function?
options: File an Offer in Compromise to end the audit
Request a meeting with the revenue agent's manager to discuss the disputed issue
Immediately file a petition in U.S. Tax Court
Refuse to provide any further documentation
questions.rationale: When disputes arise during an examination, requesting a managerial conference is a reasonable resolution step before pursuing the Independent Office of Appeals.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner must promptly submit records or information lawfully requested by the IRS. When may the practitioner properly decline or delay providing such requested records?
options: When the practitioner believes in good faith and on reasonable grounds that the records or information are privileged
Whenever the request comes from a revenue agent rather than Appeals
Whenever the client simply prefers not to share them
Any time a fee remains unpaid
questions.rationale: Circular 230 requires prompt submission of lawfully requested records, but a practitioner may withhold them when believing in good faith and on reasonable grounds that they are privileged.

questions.stem: A practitioner wants to assert the confidentiality privilege for tax advice under IRC section 7525 (the federally authorized tax practitioner privilege). Which statement about this privilege is correct?
options: It applies to all communications, including those promoting tax shelters and criminal matters.
It is identical to and as broad as the attorney-client privilege in all respects.
It applies only to communications with attorneys.

It generally applies to tax advice between a taxpayer and a federally authorized tax practitioner in noncriminal tax matters before the IRS or in federal court, but not to tax return preparation or criminal matters.
questions.rationale: The Section 7525 privilege extends limited confidentiality to tax advice from federally authorized practitioners in noncriminal federal tax matters, but excludes return preparation, criminal proceedings, and tax shelter promotion.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, what is a practitioner's obligation when the practitioner knows the client has NOT complied with the U.S. revenue laws or has made an error in a document submitted to the IRS?
options: Immediately resign from all engagements
Report the client to the Office of Professional Responsibility
Advise the client promptly of the noncompliance, error, or omission and the consequences
Correct the document without telling the client
questions.rationale: Circular 230 obligates a practitioner who becomes aware of a client's noncompliance or error to promptly inform the client of it and the potential consequences, leaving the correction decision to the client.

questions.stem: An Electronic Return Originator must keep certain records. After e-filing an individual return, how long must the ERO generally retain Form 8879 and supporting documents?
options: Until the return is accepted, then they may be destroyed
3 years from the return due date or the IRS received date, whichever is later
10 years from filing
1 year from filing
questions.rationale: EROs must retain Form 8879 and supporting documents generally for three years from the return due date or IRS received date, whichever is later, and make them available to the IRS upon request.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A taxpayer's representative wants the most efficient way to potentially remove a filed Notice of Federal Tax Lien after the underlying debt is satisfied. Which action reflects the proper outcome once the liability is fully paid?
options: The lien remains forever even after payment.
The taxpayer must sue in district court to remove any satisfied lien.
The IRS generally releases the lien within 30 days after the liability is fully satisfied or becomes legally unenforceable.
The lien automatically converts to a levy.
questions.rationale: Once the underlying tax liability is fully paid or becomes unenforceable, the IRS generally releases the federal tax lien within 30 days.

questions.stem: Who may sign a Form 2848 on behalf of a corporation to authorize representation in a tax matter?
options: Any shareholder regardless of ownership percentage
An officer of the corporation having authority to bind the corporation
Any employee of the corporation
Only the corporation's outside auditor
questions.rationale: A Form 2848 for a corporation must be signed by an officer who has the authority to bind the corporation, such as the president or another duly authorized officer.

questions.stem: A taxpayer disagrees with a CP2000 underreporter notice proposing additional tax from unreported income. What is the appropriate first response by the representative?
options: Pay the proposed amount without review
Ignore the notice since it is only a proposal
Respond by the deadline on the notice, explaining the disagreement and providing supporting documentation
Immediately file a Tax Court petition
questions.rationale: A CP2000 proposes changes from document matching; the proper response is to reply by the deadline, agreeing or disagreeing and providing documentation, before any notice of deficiency is issued.

questions.stem: A paid preparer must furnish a completed copy of a return to the taxpayer. When must this generally occur?
options: Not later than the time the return is presented to the taxpayer for signature
Within one year of filing
Only if the taxpayer specifically requests it in writing
Within 30 days after the IRS processes the return
questions.rationale: A paid preparer must give the taxpayer a completed copy of the return no later than the time the return is presented to the taxpayer for signature.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A taxpayer submits a lump-sum cash Offer in Compromise. Which statement about the required offer payment is correct?
options: The full offer amount must be paid before submission in all cases.
No payment is required until the OIC is accepted.
The taxpayer must generally submit an initial payment (a nonrefundable amount) with the offer along with the application fee, unless they qualify for a low-income waiver.
Only the application fee is ever required, never an offer payment.
questions.rationale: A lump-sum cash OIC generally requires an application fee and a nonrefundable initial payment with the offer, both of which may be waived for taxpayers who meet low-income certification criteria.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants a third party, such as a friend, to discuss a specific processing issue on a single filed return directly with the IRS but not represent them. Which authorization is the simplest fit?
options: A full Form 2848 power of attorney
A notarized durable power of attorney
A federal court order
The Third Party Designee checkbox on the return itself
questions.rationale: The Third Party Designee checkbox on a return allows a named person to discuss the processing of that specific return with the IRS without granting broader representation rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes 'practice before the IRS' as defined in Circular 230?
options: Only filing returns electronically
Only appearing in U.S. Tax Court
Only the act of preparing tax returns
Communications and representation relating to a taxpayer's rights, privileges, or liabilities, including preparing documents, corresponding, and representing at conferences and meetings
questions.rationale: Practice before the IRS encompasses all matters connected with presentations to the IRS regarding a taxpayer's rights, privileges, or liabilities, including correspondence, representation, and document preparation.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to challenge a tax in the U.S. Tax Court. Which characteristic distinguishes the Tax Court from refund forums?
options: The taxpayer can litigate in Tax Court without first paying the disputed deficiency.
The taxpayer must pay the full tax before filing in Tax Court.
The Tax Court only hears criminal tax cases.
Tax Court decisions cannot be appealed.
questions.rationale: The U.S. Tax Court is a prepayment forum, allowing taxpayers to dispute a deficiency without paying first, unlike refund suits that require full payment beforehand.

questions.stem: Under the preparer penalty rules, a preparer who takes an unreasonable position resulting in an understatement of a client's tax liability may be subject to a penalty. The position is generally 'unreasonable' unless there was at least what level of support (for a non-disclosed, non-tax-shelter position)?
options: A 10% chance of success
Substantial authority
Certainty of success
A frivolous basis
questions.rationale: A preparer generally avoids the unreasonable-position penalty for an undisclosed, non-shelter position when there is substantial authority for the position; disclosed positions generally need a reasonable basis.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: An enrolled agent learns that a current client intends to provide false documents to the IRS in an ongoing examination. Under Circular 230, what is the practitioner's best course of action?
options: Alter the documents to make them appear more credible
Advise the client that submitting false documents is improper and refuse to submit them, withdrawing if the client insists
Submit the false documents as instructed by the client
Quietly continue while ignoring the issue
questions.rationale: A practitioner may not knowingly submit false or misleading documents; the proper response is to counsel the client against it and withdraw if the client insists on the improper conduct.

questions.stem: Under the due diligence rules, the penalty for a preparer's failure to comply with the due diligence requirements applies on what basis for each return?
options: Once per return regardless of how many credits are involved
Per credit or head of household determination for which due diligence was not met, so a single return can incur multiple penalties
Only if the IRS audits the taxpayer
Only for returns claiming refunds over $10,000
questions.rationale: The due diligence penalty is assessed per credit or head of household determination for which requirements were not met, meaning a single return with multiple covered items can incur several penalties.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Which IRS function is primarily responsible for collecting taxes that have been assessed but remain unpaid?
options: The Return Preparer Office
The Office of Professional Responsibility
The Examination (Audit) function
The Collection function
questions.rationale: The IRS Collection function pursues payment of assessed but unpaid tax liabilities through arrangements and enforcement tools such as liens and levies.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent is asked to represent a taxpayer in an examination but the agent prepared the original return that is now being questioned. Under Circular 230, may the enrolled agent represent the taxpayer in this examination?
options: No, a preparer can never represent a client on a return they prepared.
Yes, an enrolled agent may represent a taxpayer in an examination of a return the agent prepared, subject to general ethics rules including conflicts of interest.
Only after the agent surrenders their enrollment.
Only if the taxpayer hires a second representative.
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents may represent taxpayers in examinations of returns they prepared given their unlimited representation rights, while observing Circular 230 ethics rules such as conflict-of-interest provisions.

questions.stem: An OPR proceeding alleges a practitioner violated Circular 230. Generally, what standard of proof must be met to sanction the practitioner for the alleged misconduct in most cases?
options: Probable cause
Preponderance of the evidence, except clear and convincing evidence is required when the sanction is suspension or disbarment for certain willful violations
No standard; OPR may sanction at will
Beyond a reasonable doubt
questions.rationale: Circular 230 disciplinary proceedings generally apply a preponderance-of-the-evidence standard, with a clear-and-convincing standard required where willful violations support suspension or disbarment.

questions.stem: A levy was served on a taxpayer's bank account. Generally, how long must the bank hold the funds before sending them to the IRS, giving the taxpayer time to resolve the matter?
options: The bank must send funds immediately with no holding period.
The bank may keep the funds permanently.
The bank must hold the funds for 21 days before remitting them to the IRS.
The bank must hold the funds for 90 days.
questions.rationale: When a levy reaches a bank account, the bank must hold the funds for 21 days before remitting them, giving the taxpayer time to address the levy.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who is deceased needs representation for a final return matter. Who is generally authorized to sign Form 2848 to appoint a representative for the decedent's tax matters?
options: Any relative of the decedent
The executor, administrator, or other duly appointed personal representative of the estate
Only the IRS
The decedent's former employer
questions.rationale: For a decedent, the duly appointed executor, administrator, or personal representative of the estate may sign Form 2848 to authorize representation for the decedent's tax matters.

questions.stem: A taxpayer needs more time to file an individual income tax return. Which form provides an automatic extension of time to file (but not to pay)?
options: Form 1040-X
Form 2848
Form 9465
Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time To File
questions.rationale: Form 4868 gives an automatic extension of time to file an individual return, but it does not extend the time to pay; the tax remains due by the original deadline.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner generally must not unreasonably delay the prompt disposition of any matter before the IRS. Which of the following would most likely violate this duty?
options: Repeatedly failing to respond to IRS requests in order to stall the examination without legitimate reason
Asking clarifying questions about an IRS request
Submitting requested documents on time
Requesting a reasonable extension to gather needed documents
questions.rationale: Circular 230 prohibits practitioners from unreasonably delaying the prompt disposition of IRS matters; tactically stalling without legitimate cause violates this duty.

questions.stem: A taxpayer requests innocent spouse relief. Which form is used to request relief from joint and several liability on a jointly filed return?
options: Form 8857, Request for Innocent Spouse Relief
Form 2848
Form 8332
Form 8379, Injured Spouse Allocation
questions.rationale: Form 8857 requests innocent spouse relief from joint and several liability, distinct from Form 8379 (injured spouse), which allocates a refund away from a spouse's separate debts.

questions.stem: A preparer must exercise due diligence in determining a client's eligibility for the head of household filing status. Which documentation approach best satisfies due diligence?
options: Accepting the client's word with no inquiry
Choosing the status that yields the lowest tax regardless of facts
Asking sufficient questions, documenting the answers, and verifying that the client meets the cost-of-keeping-up-a-home and qualifying-person requirements
Assuming head of household whenever there are children
questions.rationale: Head of household due diligence requires the preparer to ask sufficient questions, document the answers, and confirm the client meets the requirements, including paying more than half the cost of keeping up a home for a qualifying person.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, which conduct relating to a practitioner's own taxes can be a basis for discipline?
options: Hiring another preparer for one's own return
Requesting an extension to file one's own return
Willfully failing to file one's own federal tax returns or willfully evading one's own taxes
Timely filing and paying all of one's own taxes
questions.rationale: A practitioner's own willful failure to file returns or willful tax evasion constitutes disreputable conduct subject to Circular 230 sanctions, reflecting that practitioners must be compliant taxpayers.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's representative wants to know how the period of limitations on assessment is affected when the taxpayer omits a substantial amount of gross income. If gross income omitted exceeds 25% of the gross income stated on the return, what is the assessment period?
options: Reduced to 2 years
Extended to 6 years
Still 3 years
Unlimited in this circumstance
questions.rationale: A substantial omission of gross income (over 25% of the gross income stated) extends the assessment statute of limitations from 3 years to 6 years.

questions.stem: Which collection alternative results in the IRS settling a tax debt for less than the full amount owed when the taxpayer cannot pay the full liability?
options: Installment Agreement
Penalty abatement
Offer in Compromise
Currently Not Collectible status
questions.rationale: An Offer in Compromise lets a qualifying taxpayer settle a tax liability for less than the full amount owed, unlike an installment agreement, which pays the full balance over time.

questions.stem: An individual who passes all three parts of the Special Enrollment Examination must apply for enrollment within a certain time after passing. Within how long after passing the last part must the candidate apply for enrollment?
options: 2 years
1 year
5 years
30 days
questions.rationale: After passing all three parts of the SEE, a candidate must apply for enrollment (Form 23) within two years of passing the final part; individual exam parts remain valid for carryover for two years (commonly described as a two-year window).

questions.stem: Which form does an individual file to apply to become an enrolled agent after passing the Special Enrollment Examination?
options: Form SS-4, Application for Employer Identification Number
Form W-12, IRS Paid Preparer Tax Identification Number Application
Form 23, Application for Enrollment to Practice Before the IRS
Form 8554, Application for Renewal of Enrollment
questions.rationale: Form 23 is the application used to become an enrolled agent after passing the SEE, and it triggers a suitability and tax-compliance background check.

questions.stem: A former IRS employee wishes to become an enrolled agent without taking the Special Enrollment Examination. Generally, what is required for the former employee to qualify for enrollment based on IRS experience?
options: A current CPA license combined with IRS employment
A specified period (generally five years) of past service and technical experience in applying and interpreting the tax laws and regulations
Twenty years of any government service
Any one year of IRS clerical employment
questions.rationale: An applicant can become an enrolled agent based on former IRS employment if they have the required period (generally five years) of technical experience interpreting and applying the Internal Revenue Code and regulations.

questions.stem: Circular 230 addresses the standards for covered opinions and written advice. A practitioner who provides written tax advice generally must NOT do which of the following?
options: Use reasonable factual and legal assumptions
Take into account the possibility that the return will not be audited when evaluating a tax position
Relate applicable law to the relevant facts
Consider all relevant facts that the practitioner knows or reasonably should know
questions.rationale: Under the written advice standards, a practitioner may not base advice on the audit lottery, meaning the chance that the IRS will not examine the return; advice must rest on the merits, relevant facts, and the law.

questions.stem: After OPR institutes a disciplinary proceeding under Circular 230, the case is generally heard and decided in the first instance by whom?
options: The U.S. Tax Court
A federal grand jury
An Administrative Law Judge
The IRS Commissioner personally
questions.rationale: Circular 230 disciplinary proceedings begin with a complaint and are decided initially by an Administrative Law Judge, whose decision may be appealed to the Treasury Appellate Authority.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent receives a notice that OPR intends to seek a sanction. The practitioner wants to contest the allegations. What document does OPR file to formally begin the disciplinary proceeding?
options: A statutory notice of deficiency
A summons
A Notice of Federal Tax Lien
A complaint
questions.rationale: A Circular 230 disciplinary proceeding formally begins when OPR files a complaint; the practitioner must answer, and the matter proceeds before an Administrative Law Judge.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner may be sanctioned for giving false or misleading information to the Treasury Department or any officer or employee thereof. The practitioner is sanctionable for such conduct only if it is done in what manner?
options: Knowingly, or through gross incompetence or reckless conduct
Negligently, even without any knowledge
Only if the IRS suffers actual monetary loss
Only if a court first finds the practitioner liable
questions.rationale: Circular 230 makes it disreputable conduct to knowingly give false or misleading information, or to do so through gross incompetence or reckless conduct, in connection with matters before the Treasury Department.

questions.stem: A PTIN must be renewed on what basis to remain valid for a paid preparer?
options: Once every three years
Annually, for each calendar year
Only when the preparer changes employers
Only one time, with lifetime validity
questions.rationale: Paid preparers must renew their PTIN every calendar year (generally beginning in the fall for the upcoming year) to continue preparing returns for compensation.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, when may a practitioner generally charge a contingent fee in connection with an IRS matter?
options: Never, under any circumstance
For any service the practitioner wishes
For preparing an original income tax return
For services rendered in connection with an IRS examination of, or challenge to, an original return or an amended return or refund claim filed within 120 days of receiving notice of the examination
questions.rationale: Circular 230 allows contingent fees only in limited circumstances, including representation in an IRS examination or judicial proceeding, and certain refund claims filed within 120 days of an examination notice or relating to statutory interest and penalties.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner who is suspended or disbarred from practice before the IRS is also prohibited from doing which of the following during the period of sanction?
options: Filing their own personal tax return
Accepting assistance from, or assisting, another person who is under suspension or disbarment if the assistance constitutes practice before the IRS
Owning a personal residence
Holding a bank account
questions.rationale: Circular 230 bars a suspended or disbarred practitioner from practice before the IRS and from knowingly assisting, or being assisted by, another sanctioned individual in such practice during the sanction period.

questions.stem: Circular 230 includes a provision on the negotiation of taxpayer checks. The prohibition on a practitioner negotiating a refund check applies to refunds issued in connection with what?
options: Any federal tax return prepared by the practitioner
Only refunds for business returns
Only checks over $5,000
Only state tax refunds
questions.rationale: Circular 230 prohibits a practitioner from endorsing or otherwise negotiating any government refund check issued to a taxpayer for a return the practitioner prepared, with no dollar threshold and regardless of return type.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent in active status changes their business mailing address. Under the enrollment rules, the enrolled agent should notify the IRS of the address change within what general timeframe?
options: Within 60 days of the change
Only at the next renewal
Notification is never required
Within 30 days of the change
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents are expected to keep their contact information current with the IRS, generally notifying the IRS of an address change within 30 days.

questions.stem: Among the best practices in Circular 230 for tax advisors, which of the following is encouraged?
options: Communicating clearly with the client about the terms of the engagement and the form and scope of the advice
Avoiding any discussion of risks to keep the client confident
Guaranteeing favorable IRS results
Minimizing documentation to reduce file size
questions.rationale: Circular 230 best practices include communicating clearly about the engagement, establishing the facts, relating law to facts, advising on conclusions, and acting fairly and with integrity.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent who is the recognized representative wants the IRS to send refund checks or notices to the representative's address. Which statement is correct regarding having a refund check sent to a representative under Form 2848?
options: A Form 2848 automatically directs refund checks to the representative.
The representative must request the refund check in cash.
A representative can never affect where notices are sent.
The taxpayer's refund check itself cannot be sent to the representative; the power of attorney does not authorize the representative to receive or negotiate refund checks.
questions.rationale: A Form 2848 may authorize a representative to receive copies of notices and communications, but it does not authorize the representative to receive or negotiate the taxpayer's refund check, which is issued to the taxpayer.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to authorize a family member who is not a credentialed practitioner to represent them before the IRS in a limited situation. Under the rules for limited practice, an individual may represent a family member before the IRS in which circumstance?
options: Only if the family member is also an enrolled agent
Family members can never represent one another
In any examination, appeal, or collection matter without restriction
Only if the family relationship is disclosed and the representation is limited to matters where a family member may appear, generally without compensation, before IRS personnel handling the matter
questions.rationale: Circular 230 permits limited practice by an individual representing a member of their immediate family, generally without compensation, even though that individual is not a credentialed practitioner.

questions.stem: How many representatives may a taxpayer name on a single Form 2848 to receive copies of notices and communications?
options: No representative may receive copies
Unlimited representatives may receive copies
Up to two named representatives may be designated to receive copies of notices and communications
Only one representative total may be listed on the form
questions.rationale: A Form 2848 may list multiple representatives, but the IRS will send copies of notices and communications to no more than two of the named representatives who request them.

questions.stem: A representative wants to substitute or add another representative to an existing matter, but the original Form 2848 did not authorize the representative to delegate authority. What is required for the new representative to act?
options: The IRS automatically adds any requested representative.
Nothing; any representative may freely add others.
The representative may delegate only if the taxpayer authorized substitution or delegation on the Form 2848; otherwise a new authorization from the taxpayer is generally needed.
The new representative may act based solely on a verbal agreement.
questions.rationale: Substitution or delegation of representative authority is permitted only if the taxpayer authorized it on Form 2848; absent that authorization, a new Form 2848 from the taxpayer is required for an additional or substitute representative.

questions.stem: A representative previously withdrew from a matter by submitting a signed statement to the IRS. What is the effect of a representative's properly submitted withdrawal on the power of attorney?
options: It automatically appoints the IRS as the taxpayer's representative.
It withdraws the representative from the matter so the representative is no longer authorized to act, while the taxpayer remains free to appoint another representative.
It revokes the taxpayer's filing obligations.
It has no effect; only the taxpayer can end the authorization.
questions.rationale: Just as a taxpayer can revoke a power of attorney, a representative can withdraw by submitting a signed statement (or a copy of the Form 2848 marked withdraw) to the IRS, ending the representative's authority for the matter.

questions.stem: A taxpayer submits a Form 8821 naming a designee. Which of the following can the designee do under that authorization?
options: Sign a closing agreement on the taxpayer's behalf
Advocate the taxpayer's position in an Appeals conference
Negotiate an installment agreement on the taxpayer's behalf
Inspect and receive confidential tax information for the matters and years listed
questions.rationale: Form 8821 grants only the ability to inspect or receive confidential tax information; any advocacy, negotiation, or signing on the taxpayer's behalf requires a Form 2848 power of attorney.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, after a practitioner's relationship with a client ends, what duty continues with respect to the former client's information?
options: The practitioner may freely disclose the former client's information to anyone.
Confidentiality obligations end immediately when the engagement concludes.
The practitioner must continue to protect the confidentiality of the client's tax return information consistent with the law, including IRC section 7216 restrictions on disclosure and use.
The practitioner must publish the client's return data to the IRS.
questions.rationale: A preparer's obligation to protect a client's tax return information, including the IRC section 7216 restrictions against unauthorized disclosure or use, continues even after the engagement ends.

questions.stem: A preparer wants to disclose a client's tax return information to a third party for a purpose other than preparing the return. Under IRC section 7216, what is generally required before doing so?
options: The taxpayer's prior written consent that meets the specific requirements, unless an exception applies.
Only verbal consent from the taxpayer.
Approval from the IRS Commissioner.
Nothing; preparers may disclose freely.
questions.rationale: IRC section 7216 imposes penalties for unauthorized disclosure or use of a taxpayer's return information; absent an exception, a preparer must obtain the taxpayer's specific prior written consent before disclosing or using that information for other purposes.

questions.stem: A representative needs a number to be associated with their authorizations so the IRS can track powers of attorney filed for various taxpayers. What is this representative-specific number called?
options: An IP PIN
An EFIN
A routing number
A CAF number
questions.rationale: A representative is assigned a CAF number, which the IRS uses to link the representative to the authorizations (Forms 2848 and 8821) filed for their clients.

questions.stem: A partnership needs to authorize a representative for a partnership-level tax matter. Who is generally authorized to sign Form 2848 on behalf of a partnership?
options: Only an outside attorney for the firm
Any employee of the partnership
A partner duly authorized to act for the partnership in the matter, such as a general partner or partnership representative
Any limited partner regardless of authority
questions.rationale: For a partnership, the Form 2848 must be signed by a partner (or the partnership representative) who has authority to act for the partnership in the tax matter at issue.

questions.stem: An IRS examination can be conducted in different formats. Which type of examination is generally conducted entirely by mail, with the taxpayer asked to mail in documentation for specific items?
options: A field examination
A Tax Court trial
A correspondence examination
An office examination
questions.rationale: The IRS conducts correspondence examinations by mail for limited, specific issues, while office and field examinations involve in-person interviews and broader review.

questions.stem: A taxpayer files a timely petition with the U.S. Tax Court in response to a notice of deficiency. What is the effect on assessment and collection while the case is pending?
options: The taxpayer must pay the deficiency before the case can be heard.
Interest stops accruing on the deficiency.
Assessment and collection of the disputed deficiency are generally suspended (barred) until the Tax Court decision becomes final.
The IRS may immediately assess and collect the disputed amount.
questions.rationale: A timely Tax Court petition suspends assessment and collection of the contested deficiency until the decision is final, which is a key advantage of the prepayment forum, though interest continues to accrue.

questions.stem: The U.S. Tax Court has a procedure for disputes that do not exceed a certain dollar amount per year, offering a simplified process from which decisions cannot be appealed. This small tax case ('S case') procedure is generally available when the amount in dispute for any year does not exceed how much?
questions.rationale: The Tax Court's small tax case procedure applies when the disputed amount is $50,000 or less per period; it is informal and the decisions are final and not appealable.

questions.stem: A taxpayer seeks help when facing a significant hardship that the IRS's normal channels have not resolved. Which IRS organization is designed to assist taxpayers experiencing such hardships or systemic problems?
options: The Independent Office of Appeals
Criminal Investigation
The Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS)
The Office of Professional Responsibility
questions.rationale: The Taxpayer Advocate Service is an independent organization within the IRS that assists taxpayers facing economic hardship, delays, or systemic issues, often via Form 911.

questions.stem: Which form does a taxpayer or representative file to request assistance from the Taxpayer Advocate Service?
options: Form 656, Offer in Compromise
Form 12153, Request for a Collection Due Process or Equivalent Hearing
Form 911, Request for Taxpayer Advocate Service Assistance
Form 433-A, Collection Information Statement
questions.rationale: Form 911 is used to request help from the Taxpayer Advocate Service, typically when a taxpayer faces significant hardship or unresolved problems with the IRS.

questions.stem: When the IRS evaluates an Offer in Compromise based on doubt as to collectibility, it generally calculates a minimum acceptable offer amount based on the taxpayer's reasonable collection potential (RCP). RCP generally includes which of the following?
options: Only the value of the taxpayer's home
The total of the taxpayer's gross receipts for the year
Only the taxpayer's annual income
The net realizable equity in the taxpayer's assets plus a calculation of future remaining income
questions.rationale: Reasonable collection potential equals the net realizable equity in the taxpayer's assets plus the taxpayer's future remaining income, which the IRS uses to determine the minimum acceptable offer under doubt as to collectibility.

questions.stem: While an Offer in Compromise is pending with the IRS, what is the general effect on the ten-year collection statute of limitations?
options: The collection statute is reduced to five years.
The collection statute is unaffected and continues to run normally.
The collection statute is permanently terminated.
The collection statute is generally suspended while the offer is pending plus an additional 30 days after rejection.
questions.rationale: Submitting an offer in compromise generally suspends the collection statute while the offer is pending, for 30 days after a rejection, and during any timely appeal, effectively extending the time the IRS has to collect.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants the IRS to withdraw a filed Notice of Federal Tax Lien (as opposed to merely releasing it). Which circumstance can support a lien withdrawal?
options: The taxpayer simply asks and offers no basis.
The taxpayer disagrees with the amount but has not paid.
The taxpayer has filed for an extension of time to file.
Withdrawal will facilitate collection of the tax, or the taxpayer has entered a qualifying direct debit installment agreement and meets the conditions, among other allowed grounds.
questions.rationale: Lien withdrawal (removing the public Notice of Federal Tax Lien) is allowed in specific situations, such as premature or improper filing, entering a qualifying direct debit installment agreement, facilitating collection, or where withdrawal benefits both the taxpayer and the government.

questions.stem: A taxpayer missed the 30-day deadline to request a Collection Due Process hearing after a Final Notice of Intent to Levy. What option may still be available, and what is its key limitation?
options: An immediate Offer in Compromise that stops the levy permanently.
An Equivalent Hearing, which provides Appeals review but does not preserve the right to judicial review in the Tax Court.
No options remain; the taxpayer has waived all rights.
An automatic Tax Court petition with full rights.
questions.rationale: If a taxpayer misses the 30-day CDP window, an Equivalent Hearing may still be requested (generally within one year), providing Appeals review but without the right to petition the Tax Court for judicial review of the determination.

questions.stem: Which form does a taxpayer use to request a Collection Due Process or Equivalent Hearing with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals?
options: Form 843, Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement
Form 1040-X, Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return
Form 12153, Request for a Collection Due Process or Equivalent Hearing
Form 9465, Installment Agreement Request
questions.rationale: Form 12153 is the form a taxpayer submits to request a Collection Due Process or Equivalent Hearing after receiving a lien filing notice or a Final Notice of Intent to Levy.

questions.stem: When proposing a Trust Fund Recovery Penalty against a responsible person, the IRS must establish two elements. What are they?
options: The person was responsible for collecting or paying over the trust fund taxes, and the person willfully failed to do so.
The person filed late and the business had employees.
The person was an owner and the business was profitable.
The person had a CPA license and signed the return.
questions.rationale: The Trust Fund Recovery Penalty applies when a person is both a responsible person, with the duty to collect and pay over the trust fund taxes, and that person willfully failed to do so.

questions.stem: Under the innocent spouse rules, what is the general deadline to request relief under the separation of liability and traditional innocent spouse provisions?
options: Within 10 years after the return was filed.
Within 30 days of the original return due date.
No deadline applies.
Generally within 2 years after the date the IRS first began collection activity against the requesting spouse.
questions.rationale: Traditional innocent spouse relief and separation of liability relief generally must be requested within 2 years of the first IRS collection activity against the requesting spouse; equitable relief has a more flexible timeframe.

questions.stem: An IRS examination concludes and the taxpayer agrees to the proposed changes. Which form is commonly signed to consent to the immediate assessment and collection of the agreed deficiency, waiving the right to a notice of deficiency?
options: Form 12153
Form 870, Waiver of Restrictions on Assessment and Collection
Form 8821
Form 656
questions.rationale: By signing Form 870, a taxpayer agrees to the examination changes and waives the restriction requiring a notice of deficiency, allowing the IRS to assess and collect the agreed amount immediately, though it does not finally settle the issue.

questions.stem: A taxpayer and the IRS want to permanently and conclusively close a tax matter for a specific year so neither party can reopen it absent fraud, malfeasance, or misrepresentation of material fact. Which document accomplishes this?
options: A Form 870 waiver
A CP2000 notice
A closing agreement under IRC section 7121 (Form 866 or 906)
A Form 4868 extension
questions.rationale: A closing agreement under IRC section 7121 conclusively settles a tax matter and cannot be reopened by either party except in cases of fraud, malfeasance, or misrepresentation of a material fact.

questions.stem: Which financial statement form does an individual wage earner or self-employed taxpayer generally submit to support a collection alternative such as a non-streamlined installment agreement or an offer in compromise?
options: Form 1099-MISC
Form 433-A (or 433-A (OIC)), Collection Information Statement for Wage Earners and Self-Employed Individuals
Form 8867
Form 940, Employer's Annual Federal Unemployment Tax Return
questions.rationale: Form 433-A (and the 433-A (OIC) variant) is the Collection Information Statement individuals provide so the IRS can evaluate ability to pay for installment agreements, currently not collectible status, or offers in compromise.

questions.stem: Which IRS document number is the formal application for an Offer in Compromise that a taxpayer submits?
options: Form 9465
Form 4506-T
Form 2848
Form 656, Offer in Compromise
questions.rationale: Form 656 is the Offer in Compromise application, typically accompanied by a Collection Information Statement (Form 433-A (OIC) or 433-B (OIC)) and required fees and payments.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's offer in compromise is accepted. Which condition must the taxpayer generally meet after acceptance to keep the offer in effect?
options: The taxpayer must remain compliant by timely filing and paying all required taxes for a period (generally five years) after acceptance, or the offer may default.
The taxpayer must hire the same representative for five years.
The taxpayer must immediately repay all previously refunded amounts.
The taxpayer is permanently exempt from filing returns.
questions.rationale: An accepted offer in compromise requires the taxpayer to remain compliant with filing and payment obligations, generally for five years; failure to do so can cause the offer to default and revive the full original liability.

questions.stem: A taxpayer disagrees with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals' determination in a Collection Due Process hearing concerning a levy. Where may the taxpayer seek judicial review of that determination?
options: In a state court
In a U.S. District Court after paying the tax
In the U.S. Tax Court
Judicial review is never available for CDP determinations
questions.rationale: Following a timely CDP hearing, a taxpayer who disagrees with the Appeals determination may seek judicial review by petitioning the U.S. Tax Court, which is why preserving CDP rights matters.

questions.stem: A representative wants to know how a taxpayer's bankruptcy filing generally affects IRS collection activity. What is the immediate effect of a bankruptcy filing?
options: An automatic stay generally goes into effect, halting most IRS collection actions while the bankruptcy is pending.
It has no effect on IRS collection.
It immediately discharges all tax debts.
It accelerates IRS levies.
questions.rationale: A bankruptcy filing triggers an automatic stay that stops most IRS collection activity while the case is pending; the stay period also generally suspends the collection statute of limitations.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to claim a refund of overpaid income tax for a prior year that was already filed. Which form does an individual generally use to claim the refund by amending the return?
options: Form 1040-X, Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return
Form 9465
Form 12153
Form 656
questions.rationale: Individuals claim a refund on a previously filed return by filing Form 1040-X, subject to the refund statute of limitations.

questions.stem: Under the accuracy-related penalty rules, a substantial understatement of income tax by an individual generally exists when the understatement exceeds the greater of 10% of the tax required to be shown or what dollar amount?
questions.rationale: The substantial understatement component of the accuracy-related penalty applies to an individual when the understatement exceeds the greater of 10% of the correct tax or $5,000.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: What is the general rate of the accuracy-related penalty for negligence or a substantial understatement of income tax?
options: 50% of the underpayment
75% of the underpayment
5% of the underpayment
20% of the portion of the underpayment attributable to the misconduct
questions.rationale: The accuracy-related penalty under IRC section 6662 is generally 20% of the underpayment attributable to negligence, disregard of rules, or a substantial understatement (and is doubled to 40% in certain undisclosed transaction cases).
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Which form does a taxpayer generally use to claim a refund of certain assessed penalties or to request abatement of penalties and certain interest?
options: Form 9465
Form 843, Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement
Form 2848
Form 8867
questions.rationale: Form 843 is the Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement, commonly used to request abatement of penalties (for example, for reasonable cause) and certain interest, though income tax refunds use Form 1040-X.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Generally, a taxpayer who files an individual income tax return more than 60 days after the due date (including extensions) is subject to a minimum failure-to-file penalty. This minimum penalty is the lesser of a statutory dollar amount (indexed for inflation) or what?
options: 10% of the refund
The taxpayer's total income
100% of the tax required to be shown on the return
50% of any balance due
questions.rationale: For returns filed more than 60 days late, the failure-to-file penalty is at least the lesser of an inflation-adjusted statutory minimum or 100% of the tax required to be shown on the return.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Under IRC section 6695, the penalty imposed on a preparer for failure to furnish a required copy of the return to the taxpayer, failure to sign, or failure to furnish their identifying number is generally assessed in what manner?
options: A percentage of the refund
Only after criminal conviction
A per-failure dollar penalty (indexed for inflation) for each return, subject to an annual maximum
A single flat $50,000 per firm
questions.rationale: Section 6695 imposes specific per-failure dollar penalties (indexed for inflation) for preparer compliance failures such as not signing, not furnishing a copy, or not including the PTIN, each subject to an annual maximum.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Which IRS program automatically matches information returns (such as Forms W-2 and 1099) against amounts reported on a filed return and proposes adjustments for discrepancies?
options: The Centralized Authorization File
The Offer in Compromise program
The Automated Underreporter (AUR) program
The Annual Filing Season Program
questions.rationale: The Automated Underreporter program compares income reported on third-party information returns with the taxpayer's return and proposes changes, often through a CP2000 notice, when amounts do not match.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: An ERO transmits a return to the IRS. Which of the following is the ERO generally NOT permitted to do?
options: Verify the taxpayer's identity before e-filing
Provide the taxpayer a copy of the return
Alter the taxpayer's data on a return after the taxpayer has signed Form 8879 without the taxpayer's knowledge and a new signature when changes are substantive
Submit the return after obtaining the taxpayer's signature authorization
questions.rationale: If the return data changes substantively after the taxpayer signs the Form 8879, the ERO must have the taxpayer review and re-sign a new authorization; the ERO cannot silently alter the signed return for material items.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A return preparer must retain a completed copy of each prepared return or a list of taxpayers for whom returns were prepared. For how long must the preparer generally retain this record?
options: 30 days
Indefinitely
10 years
3 years (generally for the period ending after the close of the return period)
questions.rationale: Under the preparer recordkeeping rules, a preparer must keep a copy of each prepared return, or a list of the taxpayers and their identification numbers, generally for three years after the close of the return period.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Under IRC section 6701, a penalty applies to a person who aids or assists in the preparation of a document knowing it will be used in connection with a material tax matter and that it will result in an understatement of another person's tax liability. This is best described as a penalty for what?
options: Failure to make estimated tax payments
Failure to keep adequate records
Aiding and abetting an understatement of tax liability
A late-filed return
questions.rationale: IRC section 6701 imposes a penalty for aiding and abetting an understatement of tax liability when a person knowingly assists in preparing a document that they know will be used in a material tax matter and will understate another's tax.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: The due diligence requirements that require completing Form 8867 apply to which set of items?
options: The Earned Income Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit/Additional Child Tax Credit/Credit for Other Dependents, the American Opportunity Tax Credit, and head of household filing status
Only the Earned Income Tax Credit
Only itemized deductions
Only the standard deduction
questions.rationale: Paid preparer due diligence under Form 8867 applies to the EITC, the Child Tax Credit (and ACTC and Credit for Other Dependents), the American Opportunity Tax Credit, and the head of household filing status.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A taxpayer who already received an IP PIN must do what when e-filing or paper-filing their return?
options: Enter the current-year IP PIN on the return so the IRS will accept and process it
Ignore the IP PIN since it is optional once issued
Share the IP PIN publicly to verify identity
Use the prior-year IP PIN every year
questions.rationale: Once the IRS assigns an IP PIN, the taxpayer must enter the correct current-year number on the return; otherwise the IRS rejects the e-filed return or delays processing of a paper return.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a tax credit from a tax deduction when completing a return?
options: They have identical effects on the final tax.
A credit only applies to corporations.
A credit reduces the tax owed dollar-for-dollar, while a deduction reduces the amount of income subject to tax.
A deduction reduces tax dollar-for-dollar, while a credit reduces taxable income.
questions.rationale: A tax credit reduces the tax owed dollar-for-dollar, whereas a deduction reduces taxable income, so a credit generally provides greater tax savings per dollar than a deduction.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: A preparer learns after filing that a client's e-filed return claimed a credit based on documents the preparer now knows were fabricated. Considering preparer penalties, which exposure is most directly implicated by knowingly using fabricated documents to claim a credit?
options: No exposure because the return was already accepted
The willful or reckless conduct preparer penalty for understatements, which carries a higher penalty than the ordinary unreasonable-position penalty
Only an estimated tax penalty
Only a late-filing penalty
questions.rationale: Under the preparer understatement penalty rules, willful or reckless conduct (such as knowingly using false documents) triggers the higher-tier penalty, which exceeds the penalty for a mere unreasonable position.
questions.source: Part 3 – Completion of the Filing Process

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.20, when the IRS makes a proper and lawful request for records or information, a practitioner must promptly submit them unless the practitioner believes in good faith and on reasonable grounds that the records or information are what?
options: Owned by a third party
Privileged
Located outside the United States
Older than three years
questions.rationale: Circular 230 §10.20 requires prompt furnishing of lawfully requested records and information unless the practitioner reasonably and in good faith believes they are privileged.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.22, a practitioner exercising due diligence may generally rely on the work product of another person if the practitioner does what?
options: Uses reasonable care in engaging, supervising, training, and evaluating that person
Reviews each item personally before signing
Verifies that the person holds a valid PTIN
Obtains a written indemnification agreement from that person
questions.rationale: Section 10.22(b) allows a practitioner to rely on another person's work product when the practitioner uses reasonable care in engaging, supervising, training, and evaluating that person.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.23, a practitioner may not unreasonably delay what?
options: The renewal of the practitioner's enrollment
The payment of the practitioner's own estimated taxes
The prompt disposition of any matter before the IRS
The transmission of a client's refund check
questions.rationale: Section 10.23 forbids a practitioner from unreasonably delaying the prompt disposition of any matter before the IRS.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.24, a practitioner generally may not knowingly accept assistance from, or assist, a person who is under disbarment or suspension from practice before the IRS if the assistance relates to what?
options: Preparation of state income tax returns only
Bookkeeping services performed offshore
A matter or matters constituting practice before the IRS
Any personal financial planning service
questions.rationale: Section 10.24 prohibits a practitioner from assisting, or accepting assistance from, a disbarred or suspended individual in any matter constituting practice before the IRS.

questions.stem: Circular 230 §10.27 prohibits a practitioner from charging which type of fee for preparing an original tax return?
options: An hourly fee
A contingent fee
A flat fee
A retainer fee
questions.rationale: Under §10.27, contingent fees are generally prohibited, including for preparing an original return; flat, hourly, and retainer arrangements are not restricted.

questions.stem: Under the §10.27 exceptions, a practitioner MAY charge a contingent fee in connection with which of the following?
options: Advising a client on the deductibility of routine business expenses
Preparing an original income tax return claiming the earned income credit
An IRS examination of, or challenge to, an original return, provided the fee is charged for services in connection with that examination
Preparing a first-time amended return before any IRS contact
questions.rationale: Section 10.27 allows contingent fees in narrow situations, such as services connected to an IRS examination of an original return, or certain refund claims tied to interest/penalty determinations.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.28, when a client requests the return of the client's records that are necessary to comply with federal tax obligations, the practitioner must do what, even if there is a fee dispute?
options: Promptly return the client's records to the client
Forward the records directly to the IRS
Retain all records until the fee is paid in full
Destroy the records after 30 days
questions.rationale: Section 10.28 requires a practitioner to promptly return a client's records necessary for the client's federal tax obligations, even amid a fee dispute, though state law may let the practitioner retain its own work product.

questions.stem: Under §10.28, which item is generally considered the practitioner's own work product that may be withheld pending a fee dispute if permitted by applicable state law?
options: The client's original Forms W-2 and 1099
Receipts the client provided for deductions
A tax return the practitioner prepared but for which fees remain unpaid, where state law allows retention
The client's prior-year returns the client delivered to the practitioner
questions.rationale: Under §10.28, originals and client-furnished documents must be returned, but a practitioner may withhold its own work product (such as an unpaid-for prepared return) where state law allows.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.29, a practitioner may represent a client despite a conflict of interest only if the practitioner reasonably believes representation will be competent and diligent, the representation is not prohibited by law, AND what additional condition is met?
options: Each affected client provides oral consent at the first meeting
The practitioner discloses the conflict only to the primary client
Each affected client waives the conflict in writing within a reasonable time after informed consent, and the practitioner retains the consents for at least 36 months after the representation ends
The IRS approves the joint representation in advance
questions.rationale: Under §10.29, conflicted representation is permitted only with informed, written consent from each affected client (confirmed within 30 days), retained for 36 months after the representation concludes.

questions.stem: Circular 230 §10.30 governs solicitation. Which practice does §10.30 generally PROHIBIT?
options: Publishing a fee schedule for routine services
Advertising the practitioner's enrolled agent designation
Listing the practitioner in a telephone directory
Making, in connection with practice, a false, fraudulent, or coercive solicitation
questions.rationale: Section 10.30 bars false, fraudulent, coercive, or misleading solicitations and regulates advertising, fee information, and the retention of communications.

questions.stem: Under §10.30, a practitioner who publishes a fee schedule for routine services must honor those published fees for at least how long after the last date the schedule was published?
options: 1 year
14 days
30 days
7 days
questions.rationale: Section 10.30 requires a practitioner to honor a published fee schedule for at least 30 days after its last date of publication.

questions.stem: Circular 230 §10.33 sets forth aspirational standards. These best practices for tax advisors are described as what?
options: Mandatory rules whose violation results in automatic disbarment
Aspirational standards that practitioners should observe to provide the highest quality representation
Rules applicable only to attorneys
Penalty provisions enforced by the RPO
questions.rationale: Section 10.33 lists aspirational best practices (clear engagement scope, reliance on facts and law, clear advice, and acting fairly) to encourage high-quality representation.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.34(a), a practitioner may not willfully, recklessly, or through gross incompetence sign a tax return or advise a position on a return that the practitioner knows or reasonably should know does what?
options: Results in a refund of more than $10,000
Lacks a reasonable basis, is an unreasonable position under §6694(a)(2), or is a willful or reckless understatement under §6694(b)
Requires attachment of more than three schedules
Was prepared using commercial tax software
questions.rationale: Section 10.34(a) ties the standard for signing or advising return positions to the §6694 preparer-penalty standards (reasonable basis, unreasonable position, and willful/reckless understatements).

questions.stem: Under §10.34(b), a practitioner advising a client to take a position on a document or submission may not advise a position that the practitioner knows or reasonably should know contains or omits information in a manner that demonstrates what?
options: A clerical typographical error
Use of an outdated form version
An intentional disregard of a rule or regulation, unless the position represents a good-faith challenge to the rule's validity
A rounding difference under $1
questions.rationale: Section 10.34(b) bars advising positions that intentionally disregard a rule or regulation, except as a good-faith challenge to the rule's validity, with full disclosure when required.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.35, a practitioner must possess the necessary competence to engage in practice before the IRS. Competence requires what?
options: An advanced degree in taxation
Membership in a national professional association
The appropriate level of knowledge, skill, thoroughness, and preparation necessary for the matter
A minimum of five years of experience in every matter
questions.rationale: Section 10.35 requires competent practice—appropriate knowledge, skill, thoroughness, and preparation—which a practitioner may achieve through study or by associating with a competent person.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.37, when giving written advice, a practitioner must base the advice on reasonable factual and legal assumptions and may NOT do which of the following?
options: Relate applicable law to the relevant facts
Consider the possibility that the return will not be audited
Take into account the possibility that a tax return will not be audited, that an issue will not be raised on audit, or that a matter will be settled
Rely on the client's representations after exercising reasonable diligence
questions.rationale: Section 10.37 requires written advice to rest on reasonable assumptions and prohibits considering the audit lottery—the chance a return won't be audited or an issue won't be raised.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.50, the Secretary may sanction a practitioner who is incompetent or disreputable, who violates the regulations, or who acts willfully and misleadingly. The available sanctions include censure, suspension, disbarment, and what other sanction?
options: Forfeiture of the practitioner's personal assets
Permanent revocation of the practitioner's PTIN by OPR
A monetary penalty
Criminal imprisonment imposed by OPR
questions.rationale: Section 10.50 authorizes the sanctions of censure, suspension, disbarment, and monetary penalties for violations of Circular 230.

questions.stem: Under §10.50, when a practitioner acts in violation of Circular 230 while engaged by an employer or firm, a monetary penalty may be imposed against whom?
options: Only the OPR
Only the individual practitioner
Only the client who benefited
The individual practitioner, the employer/firm, or both, and the penalty may equal the gross income derived from the conduct
questions.rationale: Under §10.50, a monetary penalty (up to gross income derived from the conduct) may be assessed against the practitioner, the employer or firm, or both.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.51, which of the following is an example of disreputable conduct for which a practitioner can be sanctioned?
options: Conviction of any criminal offense involving dishonesty or breach of trust
Charging a reasonable flat fee for preparing a return
Advising a client to claim a properly substantiated deduction
Requesting a filing extension for a client
questions.rationale: Section 10.51 enumerates disreputable conduct, including convictions for crimes involving dishonesty or breach of trust, giving false information, and willfully failing to file returns.

questions.stem: Under §10.51, willfully failing to make a federal tax return in violation of the revenue laws, or evading or attempting to evade any federal tax, is classified as what?
options: Conduct outside OPR's authority
Disreputable conduct subject to sanction
Permissible if later corrected
A minor administrative oversight
questions.rationale: Section 10.51 includes willful failure to file returns and willful evasion of taxes among examples of disreputable conduct.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.52, a practitioner may be sanctioned for willfully violating any provision of the regulations or for recklessly or through gross incompetence violating which sections?
options: §§10.1 through 10.5
Only §10.27
questions.rationale: Section 10.52 allows sanctions for willful violations of any rule, and for reckless or grossly incompetent violations of §§10.34, 10.35, 10.36, and 10.37.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.53, when an IRS officer or employee believes a practitioner has violated a provision of the regulations, that person must do what?
options: File a lawsuit against the practitioner in federal court
Notify the practitioner's clients directly
Suspend the practitioner immediately
Promptly make a written report of the suspected violation to the OPR
questions.rationale: Section 10.53 directs IRS officers and employees who suspect a Circular 230 violation to make a prompt written report to the OPR.

questions.stem: Which IRS office is responsible for administering and enforcing Circular 230, including investigating practitioner misconduct and pursuing sanctions?
options: The IRS Independent Office of Appeals
The Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS)
The Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR)
The Return Preparer Office (RPO)
questions.rationale: The Office of Professional Responsibility enforces Circular 230 and oversees practitioner conduct and discipline; the RPO handles PTINs and the preparer program.

questions.stem: Which IRS office issues and manages PTINs and oversees the annual filing season program for return preparers?
options: The Return Preparer Office (RPO)
The Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR)
The Criminal Investigation Division (CI)
The Office of Chief Counsel
questions.rationale: The RPO administers PTIN issuance and the Annual Filing Season Program, distinct from OPR's role enforcing Circular 230.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent must renew enrollment every three years. The renewal cycle is determined by what?
options: The last digit of the agent's Social Security number
The first letter of the agent's last name
The agent's date of birth
The state in which the agent resides
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents renew every three years on a staggered schedule keyed to the last digit of their SSN.

questions.stem: Under §6713, an unauthorized disclosure or use of tax return information by a return preparer is subject to a civil penalty of what amount per disclosure or use?
options: $50 per disclosure or use, capped at $27,000 per year (adjusted)
$5,000 per disclosure or use with no cap
$1,000 per disclosure or use with no cap
$250 per disclosure or use, capped at $10,000 per year (adjusted)
questions.rationale: Section 6713 imposes a $250 civil penalty per unauthorized disclosure or use of return information, capped at $10,000 per calendar year; willful or knowing violations may trigger the §7216 criminal penalty.

questions.stem: Section 7216 makes a knowing or reckless unauthorized disclosure or use of tax return information by a preparer what kind of offense?
options: An offense handled exclusively by OPR
A civil-only infraction with no criminal exposure
A criminal misdemeanor punishable by fine up to $1,000 and/or imprisonment up to one year
A felony with mandatory disbarment
questions.rationale: Section 7216 is a criminal misdemeanor (up to $1,000 fine and/or one year imprisonment) for knowing or reckless unauthorized disclosure or use of return information; §6713 is the parallel civil penalty.

questions.stem: A preparer who consents to electronically disclose a client's return information to a third party (for example, for a financial product) generally must obtain the taxpayer's consent in what form and when?
options: From the third party, not the taxpayer
Orally, at any time during the engagement
In writing (or electronically per IRS rules), signed and dated by the taxpayer before the disclosure or use
Only after the disclosure has occurred
questions.rationale: The §7216 regulations require a signed, dated, informed consent from the taxpayer obtained before any disclosure or use of return information not otherwise permitted.

questions.stem: Under §6700, a person who organizes or sells an abusive tax shelter and makes a false or fraudulent statement about the tax benefits is subject to a penalty. For a false statement about the tax benefits, the penalty is generally what?
options: 50% of the gross income the person derived (or to be derived) from the activity
$500 flat
$1,000 per activity
10% of the investor's loss
questions.rationale: Section 6700 penalizes abusive tax shelter promoters; a false/fraudulent statement about benefits (or a gross valuation overstatement) is penalized at 50% of the gross income derived from the activity.

questions.stem: Under §6701, the penalty for aiding and abetting the understatement of another person's tax liability is what amount?
options: $50,000 regardless of taxpayer type
25% of the understated tax
$1,000 ($10,000 if the understatement relates to a corporation's tax), limited to one penalty per person per period
$100 per occurrence
questions.rationale: Section 6701 penalizes aiding and abetting an understatement at $1,000 per document ($10,000 for corporate matters), with one penalty per person per period.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants a third party to receive copies of IRS notices and account information but does NOT want that person to advocate or represent them. Which form is appropriate?
options: Form 8821
Form 2848
Form 56
Form 4868
questions.rationale: Form 8821 authorizes a designee to receive and inspect confidential tax information but, unlike Form 2848, does not authorize representation or advocacy.

questions.stem: Authorizations from Forms 2848 and 8821 are recorded in which IRS system that assigns a number identifying the representative or designee?
options: The Information Returns Master File (IRMF)
The Integrated Data Retrieval System (IDRS) only
The Automated Collection System (ACS)
The Centralized Authorization File (CAF) system
questions.rationale: Powers of attorney and tax information authorizations are recorded in the Centralized Authorization File (CAF), and representatives receive a CAF number.

questions.stem: A CAF number is best described as what?
options: The IRS office code where a return is filed
The representative's PTIN used on prepared returns
A unique identifier the IRS assigns to a representative to track third-party authorizations
A taxpayer's account number for installment agreements
questions.rationale: A CAF number uniquely identifies a representative or designee so the IRS can associate them with the authorizations they hold.

questions.stem: A new Form 2848 is filed for the same taxpayer and the same matters and periods as a prior Form 2848, but the taxpayer does NOT check the box to retain the prior power of attorney. What is the effect on the earlier authorization?
options: Both powers of attorney remain fully in effect
The earlier power of attorney is automatically revoked to the extent of the overlapping matters and periods
The IRS contacts the taxpayer to choose one
The new power of attorney is rejected as a duplicate
questions.rationale: A later Form 2848 revokes prior authorizations for the same matters/periods unless the retention box is checked and a copy of the prior POA is attached.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.3 and the Form 2848 instructions, which of the following individuals may NOT generally represent a taxpayer before the IRS as an unlimited representative?
options: An attorney in good standing
An enrolled agent
A certified public accountant in good standing
An unenrolled return preparer who did not participate in the Annual Filing Season Program
questions.rationale: Attorneys, CPAs, and enrolled agents have unlimited representation rights; unenrolled preparers generally cannot represent, and AFSP participants have only limited rights tied to returns they prepared.

questions.stem: An Annual Filing Season Program participant who prepared and signed a 2024 return may represent that taxpayer before which IRS personnel regarding that return?
options: Appeals officers and Counsel attorneys
Any IRS employee for any tax year
Revenue agents, customer service representatives, and similar IRS employees in the examination of that return
Revenue officers in the Collection function
questions.rationale: AFSP participants have limited representation rights—only before examination function personnel and only for returns they prepared and signed; they cannot represent before Appeals, Counsel, or Collection.

questions.stem: Which IRS office provides an independent forum for resolving tax disputes without litigation and is meant to be impartial?
options: The Return Preparer Office
The Office of Professional Responsibility
The Criminal Investigation Division
The IRS Independent Office of Appeals
questions.rationale: The IRS Independent Office of Appeals offers a fair, impartial, and independent forum to resolve tax controversies short of litigation.

questions.stem: A revenue agent proposes adjustments after an examination and issues a 30-day letter. What does the 30-day letter generally offer the taxpayer?
options: 30 days to request a conference with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals
An automatic abatement of all penalties
A jeopardy assessment notice
The right to petition the U.S. Tax Court
questions.rationale: A 30-day letter proposes examination changes and gives the taxpayer 30 days to agree or to request a conference with Appeals before a statutory notice of deficiency is issued.

questions.stem: After receiving a statutory notice of deficiency (90-day letter), a taxpayer who wants to dispute the deficiency without first paying it must do what, and within what period?
options: File a claim for refund within two years
Request audit reconsideration within 30 days
File a CDP request within 45 days
Petition the United States Tax Court within 90 days (150 days if the notice is addressed to a person outside the United States)
questions.rationale: The statutory notice of deficiency (90-day letter) gives the taxpayer 90 days (150 if outside the U.S.) to petition the Tax Court to contest the deficiency without prepaying it.

questions.stem: Which document must a representative who is an enrolled agent complete and sign in Part II of Form 2848 to declare eligibility to represent the taxpayer?
options: The taxpayer's signature line in Part I
A separate Form 8867
The Declaration of Representative
A Power of Attorney rider
questions.rationale: On Form 2848, the representative completes Part II, the Declaration of Representative, indicating their eligibility (e.g., enrolled agent) and signing under penalties.

questions.stem: A taxpayer disputes only the IRS's denial of a refund. Which forum allows the taxpayer to sue, given that the tax has already been paid?
