No notice is required for third-party summonses
The taxpayer must generally receive advance notice of a third-party summons and has the right to intervene and move to quash the summons within 20 days
questions.rationale: Under section 7609, when the IRS summons records from a third party, the taxpayer is generally entitled to notice and may file a petition to quash the summons within 20 days of the notice, with certain exceptions (such as summonses in aid of collection).

questions.stem: The section 6662 accuracy-related penalty applies to taxpayers. Which of the following is a basis for the 20 percent accuracy-related penalty?
options: Filing a return one day late
A substantial understatement of income tax or negligence or disregard of rules and regulations
Claiming a standard deduction
Requesting an extension
questions.rationale: The section 6662 accuracy-related penalty of 20 percent applies to underpayments attributable to negligence or disregard of rules or regulations, substantial understatement of income tax, substantial valuation misstatements, and certain other items.

questions.stem: A taxpayer relied in good faith on a competent tax professional's advice and still incurred an understatement. What defense may apply to the section 6662 accuracy-related penalty?
options: The contingent fee exception
The reasonable cause and good faith exception under section 6664(c), which can apply when the taxpayer reasonably relied in good faith on professional advice
No defense exists for the taxpayer
The first-time abatement only
questions.rationale: Section 6664(c) provides that no accuracy-related penalty applies to any portion of an underpayment for which the taxpayer shows reasonable cause and good faith, which can include reasonable, good-faith reliance on the advice of a competent tax adviser who had all the relevant facts.

questions.stem: A taxpayer with a clean compliance history incurred a failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalty for one year. What administrative relief may the IRS grant even without reasonable cause?
options: First-Time Abatement (FTA) of certain penalties if the taxpayer has no penalties for the prior three years and is otherwise compliant
Automatic full refund
An offer in compromise
Innocent spouse relief
questions.rationale: First-Time Abatement is an administrative waiver allowing relief from failure-to-file, failure-to-pay, and failure-to-deposit penalties when the taxpayer has filed required returns, paid or arranged to pay, and had no penalties (other than estimated tax) for the prior three years.

questions.stem: What is the standard combined behavior of the failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalties when both apply for the same month?
options: The failure-to-file penalty (5 percent per month) is reduced by the failure-to-pay penalty (0.5 percent per month) for any month both apply
They both apply at full rate with no interaction
Neither applies if a return is eventually filed
Only the failure-to-pay penalty applies ever
questions.rationale: When both penalties apply in the same month, the failure-to-file penalty of 5 percent per month is reduced by the failure-to-pay penalty of 0.5 percent per month, so the combined maximum is 5 percent for that month; the failure-to-file penalty maxes at 25 percent.

questions.stem: An EA wishes to charge a flat 'engagement fee' plus a bonus equal to 30 percent of any additional refund obtained from amending a prior return that is NOT under examination and was filed more than 120 days ago. Is the bonus permissible under section 10.27?
options: Yes, if the client agrees in writing
Yes, all amended return fees may be contingent

No, a contingent fee for preparing an amended return or refund claim is generally prohibited unless it falls within an exception (such as an exam, a claim filed within 120 days of a written notice, judicial proceedings, or interest/penalty determinations)
No, all fees must be hourly
questions.rationale: Circular 230 section 10.27 generally bars contingent fees, with exceptions for IRS examinations, amended returns or refund claims filed within 120 days of a written notice of examination or challenge, judicial proceedings, and claims for refund involving interest or penalties; a contingent fee outside these is prohibited.

questions.stem: An EA is asked by a client's spouse to share details of the client's tax matters. The EA has a Form 2848 only for the client, not the spouse. What should the EA do?
options: Share the information because they are married
Decline to disclose the client's confidential tax information to the spouse without proper authorization, consistent with confidentiality and disclosure rules
Share only verbally
Share if the spouse signs a Form W-9
questions.rationale: A practitioner must safeguard client confidential information and not disclose it to third parties, including a spouse, without proper authorization; if the matter is a joint return, the authorization and the parties' roles determine what may be shared.

questions.stem: Under section 7525, a limited confidentiality privilege exists between a taxpayer and a federally authorized tax practitioner (such as an EA). To what does this privilege NOT apply?
options: Noncriminal tax matters before the IRS
Tax advice given in a civil examination
Noncriminal tax proceedings in federal court brought by or against the United States
Criminal tax matters and written communications promoting tax shelters
questions.rationale: Section 7525 extends a limited privilege, similar to the attorney-client privilege for tax advice, to federally authorized tax practitioners, but only for noncriminal tax matters before the IRS or in noncriminal federal tax proceedings; it does not cover criminal matters, return preparation, or tax shelter promotion communications.

questions.stem: Does the section 7525 tax practitioner privilege protect the actual preparation of a tax return?
options: Yes, all preparer work is privileged
No, the privilege protects tax advice, not the act of preparing a return or the underlying documents
Yes, for criminal matters only
Yes, but only for corporations
questions.rationale: The section 7525 privilege protects confidential communications of tax advice between a taxpayer and a federally authorized tax practitioner, but it does not extend to the mechanical preparation of a return, the return itself, or the underlying business records.

questions.stem: An EA prepares a return claiming the Earned Income Tax Credit. The taxpayer's stated income seems implausibly precise to maximize the credit, and self-employment records are missing. What does due diligence require?
options: Accept the figures to keep the client happy
Refer the client to another preparer without explanation
Round the numbers down slightly
Make reasonable inquiries to verify the self-employment income and expenses, document the inquiries and responses, and not prepare the return if the information cannot be reconciled
questions.rationale: Under section 6695(g) and the due diligence regulations, when income or expenses for a credit appear incorrect, inconsistent, or incomplete, the preparer must make and document reasonable inquiries; absent reconciliation, claiming the credit is improper.

questions.stem: A return preparer is enjoined by a federal court under section 7407 from acting as a preparer. What conduct can lead to such an injunction?
options: Filing returns on time
Charging reasonable fees

Engaging in conduct subject to penalty under sections 6694 or 6695, misrepresenting eligibility to practice, guaranteeing refunds, or other fraudulent or deceptive conduct that substantially interferes with tax administration
Using tax software
questions.rationale: Under section 7407, the government may seek a court injunction against a return preparer who repeatedly engages in conduct subject to sections 6694 or 6695 penalties, misrepresents qualifications, guarantees refunds, or engages in fraudulent or deceptive conduct; if narrower relief is insufficient, the court may bar the person from acting as a preparer.

questions.stem: A taxpayer disagrees with an examiner's findings but does not want to go to Appeals or court yet. The examiner offers a 'fast track settlement.' What is fast track settlement?
options: A guaranteed reduction of tax owed
A way to immediately litigate in Tax Court
A criminal referral process
A mediation process while the case is still in Examination, using an Appeals mediator to help resolve the dispute quickly without a formal protest
questions.rationale: Fast Track Settlement is an alternative dispute resolution program that brings an Appeals mediator into the case while it is still in the Examination function, helping the taxpayer and IRS reach resolution more quickly while preserving traditional appeal rights if it fails.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants a private letter ruling (PLR) on the tax treatment of a proposed transaction. What is a key characteristic of a PLR?
options: It is a written determination issued to a specific taxpayer in response to a request, generally binding the IRS for that taxpayer on the stated facts, and a user fee applies
It is free and binding on all taxpayers
It applies retroactively to all prior years automatically
It is published as binding law
questions.rationale: A private letter ruling is a written statement issued to a taxpayer that interprets and applies tax law to the taxpayer's specific facts; it is generally binding on the IRS for that taxpayer if the facts are as represented, requires a user fee, and may not be used as precedent by others.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's offer in compromise is returned (not rejected) because the taxpayer failed to file a required return while the offer was pending. What is the difference between a returned and a rejected offer?
options: A returned offer is not considered on its merits and carries no appeal rights, while a rejected offer is decided on the merits and may be appealed to Appeals
There is no difference
A rejected offer can never be appealed
A returned offer must be appealed within 30 days
questions.rationale: When the IRS returns an offer in compromise (for reasons such as failure to stay in filing or payment compliance, or failure to provide information), it is not considered on the merits and there is no right to appeal; a rejected offer is a merits determination that the taxpayer may appeal to the Office of Appeals.

questions.stem: When computing the minimum amount the IRS will generally accept for a doubt-as-to-collectibility OIC paid as a lump sum, what is the reasonable collection potential (RCP) generally based on?
options: Only the taxpayer's wages
The total tax owed regardless of assets
The taxpayer's gross income for one year
The net realizable equity in assets plus a multiple of monthly disposable income (future income) over a defined number of months
questions.rationale: Reasonable collection potential combines the net realizable equity in the taxpayer's assets with future income (monthly disposable income multiplied by a set number of months, such as 12 for lump-sum and 24 for periodic payment offers); this generally sets the minimum acceptable offer for doubt as to collectibility.

questions.stem: A federal tax lien arises automatically. When does the federal tax lien generally come into existence under section 6321?
options: When the tax is assessed, demand for payment is made, and the taxpayer fails to pay (the lien relates back to the assessment date)
Only after a levy
When the IRS files a Notice of Federal Tax Lien
When the taxpayer files the return
questions.rationale: Under section 6321, a federal tax lien arises automatically when tax is assessed, the IRS makes notice and demand, and the taxpayer neglects or refuses to pay; the lien attaches to all property and rights to property and relates back to the assessment date, while filing the Notice of Federal Tax Lien establishes priority against certain creditors.

questions.stem: A purchaser buys a car from a taxpayer who has an unrecorded federal tax lien. Under section 6323, is the buyer's interest protected against the lien?
options: Yes, certain purchasers (such as a purchaser of personal property in a casual sale, or a bona fide purchaser before the Notice of Federal Tax Lien is filed) can take free of the unfiled lien under the superpriority and notice rules
No, the lien always wins
Only if the buyer is a relative
Only commercial buyers are protected
questions.rationale: Section 6323 provides that the federal tax lien is not valid against certain parties (purchasers, holders of security interests, mechanic's lienors, judgment lien creditors) until the Notice of Federal Tax Lien is properly filed, and it grants superpriorities to specified interests even after filing.

questions.stem: Which IRS office assists taxpayers experiencing significant hardship or unresolved problems with the IRS and can issue a Taxpayer Assistance Order?
options: The Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS)
The Office of Professional Responsibility
Criminal Investigation
The Office of Appeals
questions.rationale: The Taxpayer Advocate Service is an independent organization within the IRS that helps taxpayers who are experiencing financial difficulty or whose problems are not resolved through normal channels, and the National Taxpayer Advocate can issue a Taxpayer Assistance Order under section 7811.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who suffered significant hardship from an impending levy asks TAS for help. What can a Taxpayer Assistance Order (TAO) direct the IRS to do?
options: Fire the revenue officer
Forgive all tax permanently
Take or refrain from taking certain actions, such as releasing a levy or expediting a refund, to relieve the significant hardship
Override the tax law
questions.rationale: Under section 7811, the National Taxpayer Advocate may issue a Taxpayer Assistance Order requiring the IRS to release property from levy or to take or refrain from taking certain actions when a taxpayer is suffering or about to suffer a significant hardship as a result of IRS action.

questions.stem: An EA's firm employs an unenrolled assistant who interacts with clients. Under Circular 230, what responsibility does the EA have regarding the assistant's conduct?
options: The practitioner with principal authority must take reasonable steps to ensure the firm has adequate procedures for compliance, and a practitioner may be responsible for a subordinate's actions in certain circumstances
The EA must fire any unenrolled staff
The EA must personally do all client work
None; only the assistant is responsible
questions.rationale: Circular 230 section 10.36 requires individuals with principal authority over a firm's practice to ensure adequate compliance procedures, and section 10.51 can attribute responsibility to a practitioner who, through willfulness or recklessness, allows subordinates to engage in improper conduct.

questions.stem: An EA gave oral advice to a client about a transaction and now learns the IRS may scrutinize it. Under the current section 10.37 standard, does the standard for written advice also inform reliance on advice?
options: A practitioner may not give written (or oral) advice that fails to consider relevant facts or relies on unreasonable assumptions; reliance on another person's advice is reasonable only if the practitioner reasonably believes that person is competent and the advice meets the standard
Reliance is always reasonable
Oral advice can never be relied upon
Section 10.37 applies only to opinions over a fee threshold
questions.rationale: Circular 230 section 10.37 governs written advice and addresses reliance: a practitioner may rely on the advice of another person only if the reliance is reasonable and made in good faith, considering the competence of that person and whether the advice meets the section's requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a 'practitioner' as opposed to an 'unenrolled return preparer' under Circular 230?
options: A practitioner is any taxpayer
A practitioner is anyone who files a tax return
A practitioner is someone authorized to practice before the IRS, such as an attorney, CPA, enrolled agent, enrolled actuary, or enrolled retirement plan agent
A practitioner is only an IRS employee
questions.rationale: Circular 230 defines practitioners as those authorized to practice before the IRS, principally attorneys, CPAs, enrolled agents, enrolled actuaries, and enrolled retirement plan agents, who are subject to its duties and restrictions.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, which credential allows a person to practice before the IRS without limitation as to the type of taxpayer or tax matter?
options: A registered tax return preparer with a current PTIN
An enrolled agent in active status
A reporting agent authorized to make federal tax deposits
An unenrolled preparer who participates in the Annual Filing Season Program
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents, attorneys, and CPAs in good standing have unlimited practice rights before the IRS.

questions.stem: How frequently must an enrolled agent renew enrollment with the IRS?
options: Every two years
Every three years
Annually
Every five years
questions.rationale: Enrolled agents must renew enrollment every three years according to the assigned renewal cycle.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent's Social Security number ends in 4. Under the staggered renewal system, during which renewal period must this EA renew?
options: Any period the EA chooses within the three-year cycle
The period for SSNs ending in 4, 5, or 6
The period for SSNs ending in 0, 1, 2, or 3
The period for SSNs ending in 7, 8, or 9
questions.rationale: Enrollment renewal is staggered by the last digit of the SSN, with 4-6 falling in the second group.

questions.stem: A practitioner learns that a client has not complied with a federal tax filing requirement. Under Circular 230 due diligence and the duty to advise, what must the practitioner do?
options: Promptly advise the client of the noncompliance, error, or omission and the consequences
Refuse all further representation until the client files
Immediately notify the IRS of the client's noncompliance
Prepare and file the missing return without the client's consent
questions.rationale: Section 10.21 requires the practitioner to advise the client of any noncompliance, error, or omission and its consequences.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 section 10.27, a contingent fee is permitted in which of the following situations?
options: Services rendered in connection with the IRS examination of an original return, if charged within 120 days of the examination notice
Preparing an original income tax return
Advising a client on a position taken on an original return before filing
Preparing a claim for refund of income tax with no examination pending
questions.rationale: Section 10.27 allows contingent fees only in specific situations, including examinations of original returns under the 120-day rule.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN)?
options: To identify a paid preparer on returns and claims for refund they prepare
To grant unlimited practice rights before the IRS
To authorize the preparer to receive a taxpayer's refund
To serve as the firm's employer identification number
questions.rationale: All paid preparers must obtain and use a PTIN on returns and refund claims they prepare for compensation.

questions.stem: How often must a paid tax return preparer renew a PTIN?
options: Once, with no renewal required
Every five years
Every three years
Annually
questions.rationale: PTINs must be renewed annually, typically during the renewal season in the fall.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner who is suspended or disbarred from practice before the IRS is prohibited from:
options: Representing taxpayers before the IRS during the period of suspension or disbarment
Preparing returns under any circumstances for the rest of their life
Filing their own personal tax returns
Holding any state professional license
questions.rationale: Suspension and disbarment remove the privilege to practice (represent taxpayers) before the IRS for the stated period.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sanction the IRS may impose under Circular 230 for incompetence or disreputable conduct?
options: Automatic revocation of the practitioner's state license
Censure, suspension, disbarment, or a monetary penalty
Criminal imprisonment imposed directly by the Office of Professional Responsibility
Garnishment of the practitioner's wages by OPR
questions.rationale: Section 10.50 authorizes censure, suspension, disbarment, and monetary penalties for violations.

questions.stem: A practitioner may rely on information furnished by a client without verification, but Circular 230 requires the practitioner to:
options: Report any doubtful information directly to the IRS
Independently audit all of the client's books
Make reasonable inquiries if the information appears incorrect, inconsistent, or incomplete
Refuse to prepare the return unless documentation is provided for every item
questions.rationale: Under section 10.34(d), a practitioner may rely in good faith on client information but must make reasonable inquiries when it appears questionable.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner who knows a client has not filed a required return and continues to represent the client must:
options: Advise the client of the noncompliance and the consequences, and may not assist in any willful evasion
Withdraw from representation in all cases
File the delinquent return on behalf of the client immediately
Notify the client's other advisors of the issue
questions.rationale: Sections 10.21 and 10.51 require advising the client and prohibit assisting in willful evasion of tax.

questions.stem: Best practices under Circular 230 section 10.33 include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Communicating clearly with the client about the terms of the engagement
Establishing the facts and arriving at a conclusion supported by the law
Acting fairly and with integrity in practice before the IRS
Guaranteeing the client a specific outcome in every IRS matter
questions.rationale: Best practices include clear communication, sound factual and legal analysis, advising on conclusions, and acting with integrity - not guaranteeing results.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent's enrollment that has lapsed because of failure to renew is placed in what status?
options: Terminated immediately
Active
Disbarred
Inactive
questions.rationale: An EA who fails to renew is placed in inactive status and cannot practice until reinstated.

questions.stem: Which of the following individuals is NOT eligible to become an enrolled agent based on prior IRS experience?
options: A former IRS employee with qualifying technical experience applying and interpreting tax law
An individual who passes all three parts of the Special Enrollment Examination
A person whose only IRS experience was clerical mail sorting
A former IRS revenue agent with five years of qualifying experience
questions.rationale: Enrollment via former IRS experience requires qualifying technical experience interpreting and applying tax law, not clerical work.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 section 10.35, a practitioner who provides written advice must:
options: Base the advice on reasonable factual and legal assumptions and not rely on unreasonable representations
Disclaim all responsibility for the advice in writing
Always issue a formal opinion meeting covered-opinion standards
Limit the advice to issues the IRS has already audited
questions.rationale: Section 10.37 requires written advice to reflect competence, reasonable factual and legal assumptions, and consideration of relevant facts.

questions.stem: A practitioner may NOT charge an unconscionable fee for representation before the IRS. This rule is found in which area of Circular 230?
options: Rules on conflicts of interest
Rules on diligence as to accuracy
Rules on solicitation and advertising
Rules on fees
questions.rationale: Section 10.27 prohibits charging an unconscionable fee for representation.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a conflict of interest exists when:
options: A practitioner charges different fees to different clients
A practitioner advertises services to the public
The representation of one client is directly adverse to another, or there is a significant risk the representation will be materially limited
A practitioner represents two clients in unrelated matters
questions.rationale: Section 10.29 defines conflicts of interest based on direct adversity or material limitation of representation.

questions.stem: When a conflict of interest exists under Circular 230, the practitioner may still represent the clients if all of the following are met EXCEPT:
options: Each affected client waives the conflict in writing within a reasonable time, generally no later than 30 days
The practitioner reasonably believes competent and diligent representation can be provided to each client
The IRS pre-approves the representation in writing
The representation is not prohibited by law
questions.rationale: Section 10.29 permits conflicted representation with informed written consent, not IRS pre-approval.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, how long must a practitioner retain written consents to conflicts of interest?
options: 12 months
36 months
Indefinitely
24 months
questions.rationale: Section 10.29 requires retaining conflict-of-interest waivers for 36 months after representation concludes.

questions.stem: A practitioner who is an officer or employee of the IRS is, under Circular 230:
options: Permitted to represent taxpayers for a fee in their off hours
Required to obtain a PTIN to do their job
Automatically an enrolled agent
Prohibited from practicing before the IRS in their personal capacity for clients
questions.rationale: Circular 230 and federal ethics rules prohibit IRS employees from representing taxpayers before the agency.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 section 10.51, which of the following is considered disreputable conduct that can lead to sanctions?
options: Declining to represent a client
Willfully failing to file the practitioner's own federal tax return
Advising a client to file an extension
Charging a reasonable hourly fee
questions.rationale: Section 10.51 lists willful failure to file one's own returns and other misconduct as disreputable conduct.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, who has the burden of proof in a disciplinary proceeding alleging a violation?
options: The taxpayer who was represented
The IRS (through OPR) must establish the violation by the applicable standard
There is no burden of proof in administrative proceedings
The practitioner must prove innocence
questions.rationale: In Circular 230 disciplinary proceedings, the government bears the burden of proving the violation.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent may use which of the following designations?
options: Enrolled to practice before the IRS or enrolled agent
Federally authorized attorney
IRS-licensed CPA
Certified by the IRS
questions.rationale: Circular 230 limits how EAs describe their status; they may say they are enrolled to practice before the IRS but not imply IRS endorsement.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 section 10.30, in advertising and solicitation a practitioner may NOT:
options: State a fixed fee for specific routine services
Use false, fraudulent, or misleading representations
List their areas of practice
Publish a fee schedule
questions.rationale: Section 10.30 prohibits false or misleading advertising while permitting truthful fee and service information.

questions.stem: Form 8821, Tax Information Authorization, allows the designee to:
options: Sign a return on the taxpayer's behalf
Represent the taxpayer in an examination
Negotiate an installment agreement
Receive and inspect confidential tax information only
questions.rationale: Form 8821 only allows a designee to receive and inspect tax information; it confers no representation rights.

questions.stem: On Form 2848, an enrolled agent must enter which designation code in the Declaration of Representative section?
options: Attorney (a)
Enrolled Agent (c)
Officer (d)
Certified Public Accountant (b)
questions.rationale: On Form 2848, enrolled agents enter designation code (c).

questions.stem: A power of attorney filed on Form 2848 generally remains in effect until:
options: It is revoked by the taxpayer or withdrawn by the representative, or otherwise terminated
Exactly three years after filing in all cases
The end of the calendar year in which it is filed
The taxpayer files the next year's return
questions.rationale: A Form 2848 stays in effect until revoked, withdrawn, or otherwise terminated by operation of the form's terms.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent representing a taxpayer in an examination has the authority to:
options: Waive the taxpayer's right to appeal without authorization
Endorse and cash the taxpayer's refund check
Change the taxpayer's filing status without consent
Receive and inspect confidential tax information and advocate the taxpayer's position
questions.rationale: A POA authorizes representation and information access but not endorsing refund checks or unauthorized waivers.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who is overseas wants an enrolled agent to substitute a new representative for one already named on Form 2848. The original POA did not authorize substitution. What is required?
options: The taxpayer must authorize the substitution, generally by a new Form 2848
No authorization is needed because the EA is the new representative
The IRS must appoint the substitute representative
The named representative may substitute anyone at will
questions.rationale: Substitution or delegation requires authorization; absent that, the taxpayer must file a new POA naming the new representative.

questions.stem: When a Form 2848 is submitted, the representative's signature in the Declaration of Representative section certifies that:
options: The representative is a relative of the taxpayer
The representative guarantees the accuracy of all prior returns
The representative will pay any tax the taxpayer owes
The representative is authorized and subject to Circular 230 and not disbarred or suspended
questions.rationale: The Declaration of Representative certifies the representative is authorized, subject to Circular 230, and in good standing.

questions.stem: Which of the following matters can be handled by an unenrolled return preparer who participates in the Annual Filing Season Program?
options: Limited representation before revenue agents and customer service for returns the preparer prepared and signed
Representation in U.S. Tax Court
Representation before IRS Appeals for any return
Representation in collection matters before Revenue Officers for any taxpayer
questions.rationale: AFSP participants have limited representation rights confined to returns they prepared and signed, before certain IRS functions.

questions.stem: A taxpayer may authorize disclosure of tax return information to a third party such as a mortgage lender using:
options: Form 8821
Form 1040-X
Form 941
Form 2848
questions.rationale: Form 8821 is the appropriate authorization for third-party information disclosure.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent receives a summons from the IRS for testimony about a client. Under the limited confidentiality privilege of IRC section 7525, the privilege:
options: Applies to all communications including those about tax shelters
Is identical to attorney-client privilege in all respects

Applies to tax advice between a federally authorized practitioner and client to the same extent as attorney-client privilege in noncriminal matters, but not to criminal matters or many tax shelter communications
Does not exist for enrolled agents
questions.rationale: Section 7525 provides a limited confidentiality privilege for tax advice in noncriminal federal tax matters, not criminal cases or many shelter communications.

questions.stem: The IRC section 7525 privilege does NOT apply to:
options: Civil tax advice to a partnership
Communications regarding the preparation of a tax return
Civil tax advice given to an individual client
Civil tax advice in a noncriminal IRS matter
questions.rationale: The section 7525 privilege covers tax advice in noncriminal matters but not return preparation or criminal matters.

questions.stem: If a taxpayer wants the IRS to send copies of notices to an enrolled agent representative, the taxpayer should:
options: Check the box on Form 2848 designating the representative to receive copies
File Form 4506-T
Do nothing; the IRS automatically copies all representatives
Call the IRS each time a notice is issued
questions.rationale: The taxpayer designates up to two representatives to receive notice copies on Form 2848.

questions.stem: When two Forms 2848 are filed for the same tax matters and periods, the IRS will:
options: Reject both forms
Honor both equally
Treat the most recent as revoking the prior unless the new one states otherwise
Contact the taxpayer to choose
questions.rationale: A new Form 2848 revokes a prior one for the same matters unless the retention box is checked.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent wants to withdraw from representing a client mid-examination. Under Circular 230 and POA rules, the EA should:
options: Simply stop responding to the IRS
Continue indefinitely because withdrawal is prohibited
Withdraw from representation and may notify the IRS by submitting a signed statement of withdrawal
Transfer the POA to another EA without notice
questions.rationale: A representative withdraws by submitting a signed withdrawal statement or a copy of the POA marked WITHDRAW.

questions.stem: A corporate officer signing Form 2848 to appoint a representative for the corporation must:
options: Have authority to legally bind the corporation
Be a shareholder of any size
Hold a personal PTIN
Be the company's outside auditor
questions.rationale: The Form 2848 for an entity must be signed by a person with authority to bind that entity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about a centralized authorization file (CAF) number?
options: It is the same as a Social Security number
It is required to file a personal tax return
It replaces the representative's PTIN on returns
It is a unique number the IRS assigns to identify a representative on third-party authorizations
questions.rationale: The CAF number is assigned by the IRS to track representatives on Forms 2848 and 8821.

questions.stem: A taxpayer grants an enrolled agent a POA covering Form 1040 for tax years 2022, 2023, and 2024. The IRS later begins examining the taxpayer's 2025 Form 1040. The existing POA:
options: Covers all future years indefinitely
Is void because more than one year was listed
Automatically covers 2025 because it is a Form 1040 matter
Does not cover 2025 because that year was not listed; a new authorization is needed
questions.rationale: Form 2848 covers only the specific tax matters and periods listed; a new authorization is needed for unlisted years.

questions.stem: On Form 2848 the taxpayer may list future tax periods, but the IRS will not accept periods that end more than how many years after the date the form is received?
options: 5 years
1 year
3 years
2 years
questions.rationale: The IRS limits future-period authorizations on Form 2848 to periods ending no more than 3 years after receipt.

questions.stem: Which IRS document proposes adjustments after an examination and gives the taxpayer 30 days to request an appeal?
options: A Final Notice of Intent to Levy
A CP2000 underreporter notice
A 90-day letter (Notice of Deficiency)
A 30-day letter with the examination report
questions.rationale: The 30-day letter accompanies the exam report and allows the taxpayer 30 days to request an Appeals conference.

questions.stem: A statutory Notice of Deficiency gives the taxpayer how many days to petition the U.S. Tax Court?
options: 30 days
90 days (150 days if addressed to a person outside the U.S.)
60 days
1 year
questions.rationale: The Notice of Deficiency (90-day letter) allows 90 days, or 150 if addressed outside the U.S., to petition the Tax Court.

questions.stem: To petition the U.S. Tax Court in response to a Notice of Deficiency, the taxpayer must generally:
options: First pay the disputed tax in full
Request an installment agreement first
File the petition within the 90-day (or 150-day) period without prepaying the tax
Wait until the IRS files a lien
questions.rationale: Tax Court is the prepayment forum: the taxpayer petitions within the deadline without paying the deficiency first.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who has fully paid a disputed tax and wants a refund denied by the IRS may pursue litigation in which courts?
options: U.S. District Court or the U.S. Court of Federal Claims after a refund claim is disallowed
U.S. Tax Court only
The Supreme Court only
U.S. Court of Appeals directly
questions.rationale: After paying and having a refund claim disallowed, taxpayers sue in U.S. District Court or the Court of Federal Claims.

questions.stem: The IRS Independent Office of Appeals is best described as:
options: A criminal investigation unit
Part of the examination function that issues audit reports
An independent function that seeks to resolve tax controversies without litigation, impartially
A collection function that files liens
questions.rationale: The Independent Office of Appeals resolves controversies impartially, on a basis fair to both the government and the taxpayer.

questions.stem: Under the doctrine considered by Appeals, the hazards of litigation refers to:
options: The risk of criminal prosecution
The probability that the IRS or the taxpayer would not prevail if the case went to court, used to settle
The chance the statute of limitations will expire
The cost of hiring an attorney
questions.rationale: Appeals settles based on the hazards of litigation - the likelihood each party would prevail in court.

questions.stem: Which form requests a Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing after a Final Notice of Intent to Levy?
options: Form 656
Form 12153
Form 843
Form 9465
questions.rationale: Form 12153 is used to request a Collection Due Process hearing.

questions.stem: If a taxpayer misses the 30-day CDP deadline, the taxpayer may still request what type of hearing, though without the right to judicial review?
options: A grand jury hearing
An equivalent hearing
A statutory deficiency hearing
A Tax Court hearing
questions.rationale: After missing the CDP deadline, the taxpayer can request an equivalent hearing, but it does not preserve Tax Court rights.

questions.stem: Which form is used to request an installment agreement to pay tax over time?
options: Form 12153
Form 8857
Form 9465
Form 2848
questions.rationale: Form 9465 requests a monthly installment payment plan.

questions.stem: An offer in compromise based on doubt as to collectibility is appropriate when:
options: The taxpayer cannot pay the full liability and the amount offered reflects reasonable collection potential
The taxpayer disputes that the tax is owed
The taxpayer simply wants to pay less
The IRS made a computational error
questions.rationale: Doubt as to collectibility OICs apply when the taxpayer cannot pay in full; the offer must reflect reasonable collection potential.

questions.stem: When the IRS receives a processable offer in compromise, the collection statute of limitations is generally:
options: Unaffected
Reduced by half
Eliminated entirely
Suspended while the offer is pending plus 30 days after rejection
questions.rationale: Filing a processable OIC suspends the collection statute while pending plus 30 days after any rejection and during appeals.

questions.stem: A federal tax lien arises automatically when:
options: The IRS files a Notice of Federal Tax Lien
Tax is assessed, demand for payment is made, and the taxpayer fails to pay
The IRS issues a 30-day letter
The taxpayer files a return
questions.rationale: The statutory federal tax lien arises on assessment, notice and demand, and failure to pay; the NFTL is a public filing of that lien.

questions.stem: An installment agreement that allows individuals owing $50,000 or less to pay over up to 72 months with streamlined approval is called a:
options: Currently not collectible status
Streamlined (guaranteed-type) installment agreement
Offer in compromise
Partial payment installment agreement
questions.rationale: Streamlined installment agreements provide simplified approval for qualifying balances paid over up to 72 months.

questions.stem: A taxpayer can request a Collection Appeals Program (CAP) hearing to challenge:
options: Certain collection actions such as a lien filing, levy, or seizure, with no Tax Court review
Eligibility for the earned income credit
A proposed examination adjustment
The amount of the underlying tax liability
questions.rationale: CAP provides a faster appeal of specific collection actions but does not allow challenges to the underlying liability or Tax Court review.

questions.stem: The Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) primarily helps taxpayers who:
options: Are experiencing significant hardship or whose problems are not resolved through normal IRS channels
Want to file their returns electronically
Need to pay their balance in full immediately
Are under criminal investigation
questions.rationale: TAS helps taxpayers with significant hardship or problems unresolved through normal IRS processes.

questions.stem: A Taxpayer Assistance Order (TAO) issued by the National Taxpayer Advocate can:
options: Permanently cancel a taxpayer's debt
Impose penalties on IRS employees
Require the IRS to take or cease certain actions to relieve significant hardship
Overrule a Tax Court decision
questions.rationale: A TAO directs the IRS to take or refrain from specified actions to relieve significant taxpayer hardship.

questions.stem: During an audit reconsideration, the IRS will reexamine an assessment when:
options: The statute of limitations on assessment has already expired with no exceptions
The taxpayer simply disagrees with the result and pays nothing new
The taxpayer provides new information not previously considered or shows a computational or processing error
The taxpayer has already litigated and lost in Tax Court on the merits
questions.rationale: Audit reconsideration is available when the taxpayer presents new information or shows an IRS error, and the matter was not finally adjudicated.

questions.stem: When the IRS files a substitute for return (SFR) because a taxpayer failed to file, the SFR generally:
options: Is prepared using available information and typically does not include many deductions, often resulting in a higher liability
Cannot be challenged by the taxpayer
Eliminates the need for the taxpayer to ever file
Includes all deductions and credits the taxpayer is entitled to
questions.rationale: An SFR is based on third-party data and generally omits deductions; the taxpayer can file an original return to reduce the liability.

questions.stem: There is NO statute of limitations on assessment when:
options: The taxpayer files a fraudulent return or fails to file a return at all
The return is filed one day late
The taxpayer underpays estimated tax
The taxpayer claims a refund
questions.rationale: For a false or fraudulent return, or no return, the tax may be assessed at any time.

questions.stem: The general statute of limitations for the IRS to collect an assessed tax is:
options: 6 years from assessment
3 years from assessment
No limit
10 years from the date of assessment
questions.rationale: The collection statute of limitations is generally 10 years from the date of assessment, subject to suspensions.

questions.stem: The failure-to-pay penalty is generally:
options: 5% per month, up to 25%
20% of the underpayment
100% of the unpaid trust fund taxes
0.5% of the unpaid tax per month or part of a month, up to 25%
questions.rationale: The failure-to-pay penalty is 0.5% per month of unpaid tax, capped at 25%.

questions.stem: A taxpayer may avoid the accuracy-related penalty by showing:
options: The amount was small
The IRS took too long to audit
The taxpayer was unaware of the tax laws
Reasonable cause and that the taxpayer acted in good faith
questions.rationale: The accuracy-related penalty does not apply where the taxpayer shows reasonable cause and good faith.

questions.stem: To qualify for First-Time Abatement, a taxpayer generally must have:
options: Never owed any tax
No penalties for the prior three years and be current with filing and payment requirements
An income below a fixed threshold
A pending offer in compromise
questions.rationale: FTA requires a clean compliance history (no significant penalties in the prior three years) and current filing and payment compliance.

questions.stem: The penalty for a paid preparer who understates a taxpayer's liability due to an unreasonable position (IRC section 6694(a)) is generally the greater of $1,000 or:
options: 100% of the refund
20% of the tax
50% of the income derived by the preparer for the return
10% of the understatement
questions.rationale: Section 6694(a) imposes a penalty of the greater of $1,000 or 50% of the preparer's income from the return for unreasonable positions.

questions.stem: Under IRC section 6695, a preparer who fails to sign a return they prepared is subject to:
options: No penalty
A per-return penalty (indexed) for failure to sign
A 75% penalty
Disbarment automatically
questions.rationale: Section 6695 imposes per-return penalties for failures including failure to sign, failure to furnish a copy, and failure to provide a PTIN.

questions.stem: Under IRC section 6695(g), a preparer who fails to comply with due diligence requirements for the earned income credit, child tax credit, or American Opportunity credit faces:
options: A penalty per credit per return for each failure
No penalty if the client signed the return
Loss of PTIN immediately
Only a warning letter
questions.rationale: Section 6695(g) imposes a per-failure penalty for each applicable credit (and head of household) when due diligence is not met, documented on Form 8867.

questions.stem: Which form documents a preparer's due diligence for refundable credits and head of household status?
options: Form 8821
Form 8867
Form 2848
Form 8862
questions.rationale: Form 8867 is the preparer's due diligence checklist for EIC, CTC/ACTC/ODC, AOTC, and head of household.

questions.stem: An authorized IRS e-file provider must apply to participate and receive what identifier?
options: An EIN
A PTIN
An Electronic Filing Identification Number (EFIN)
A CAF number
questions.rationale: Authorized e-file providers must obtain an EFIN to electronically file returns.

questions.stem: Which form does a taxpayer use to authorize a return to be e-filed and to provide an electronic signature for an individual return?
options: Form 8453
Form 8879
Form 9465
Form W-4
questions.rationale: Form 8879 authorizes the ERO to enter the taxpayer's self-selected PIN for e-filing.

questions.stem: A preparer who prepares 11 or more covered individual income tax returns in a calendar year is generally:
options: Required to obtain an attorney's license
Required to mail all returns
Exempt from e-filing
Required to e-file the returns under the e-file mandate, absent an exception or taxpayer opt-out
questions.rationale: Specified tax return preparers filing 11 or more covered returns must e-file unless an exception or taxpayer opt-out applies.

questions.stem: The penalty for a preparer who endorses or otherwise negotiates a taxpayer's refund check is:
options: No penalty
A per-check penalty under IRC section 6695(f)
Disbarment only
A 75% penalty
questions.rationale: Section 6695(f) penalizes a preparer who endorses or negotiates a client's refund check.

questions.stem: Interest on an underpayment of tax generally accrues from:
options: The date the IRS issues a notice
The original due date of the return (without regard to extensions) until paid
The date the taxpayer files
The date of assessment only
questions.rationale: Underpayment interest accrues from the return's original (unextended) due date until the tax is paid in full.

questions.stem: An extension of time to file (Form 4868) provides:
options: Additional time to both file and pay the tax
Additional time to file the return but not to pay the tax owed
An automatic installment agreement
A waiver of all penalties
questions.rationale: A filing extension postpones the filing deadline, not the payment due date; failure-to-pay penalties and interest can still accrue.

questions.stem: The estimated tax penalty for individuals is generally avoided if withholding and estimated payments equal at least:
options: 25% of the prior year tax
50% of the current year tax
90% of the current year tax or 100% of the prior year tax (110% for higher-income taxpayers)
The full balance by April 1
questions.rationale: Individuals avoid the estimated tax penalty by meeting the 90%/100% (or 110%) safe harbor.

questions.stem: The penalty under IRC section 6700 targets:
options: Promoters of abusive tax shelters
Late filing of returns
Failure to pay estimated tax
Errors in arithmetic
questions.rationale: Section 6700 imposes penalties on promoters of abusive tax shelters.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who disagrees with a math-error adjustment notice from the IRS generally has how long to request that the assessment be abated and handled through deficiency procedures?
options: 90 days
30 days
10 days
60 days
questions.rationale: A taxpayer has 60 days to request abatement of a math-error adjustment, after which deficiency procedures apply.

questions.stem: When the IRS issues a math-error notice and the taxpayer requests abatement within the required period, the IRS must:
options: Ignore the request
Immediately levy
Refer the case for criminal prosecution
Abate the assessment and, to reassess, follow normal deficiency procedures
questions.rationale: A timely math-error abatement request forces the IRS to abate and pursue any reassessment through standard deficiency procedures.

questions.stem: The penalty for failure to furnish a copy of the return to the taxpayer is imposed under:
options: IRC section 6695(a)
IRC section 6700
IRC section 6651
IRC section 6694
questions.rationale: Section 6695(a) imposes a penalty when a preparer fails to provide the taxpayer a copy of the return.

questions.stem: If a taxpayer files a return reporting a tax of $0 that is later determined to be fraudulent, the IRS may assess additional tax:
options: At any time, because of fraud
Only within 6 years
Never, once the return is filed
Only within 3 years
questions.rationale: A fraudulent return has no assessment statute of limitations; tax may be assessed at any time.

questions.stem: A taxpayer signs a Form 872 to extend the assessment statute of limitations. This agreement:
options: Is invalid because the statute cannot be extended
Shortens the collection period
Extends the assessment period to a specified date by mutual agreement
Automatically waives all penalties
questions.rationale: Form 872 is a consent that extends the assessment statute of limitations to an agreed-upon date.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, a practitioner who becomes aware that a client's submission to the IRS contains an error must:
options: Advise the client promptly of the error and its consequences
Ignore it if the IRS has not noticed
Correct it directly with the IRS without telling the client
Resign immediately in every case
questions.rationale: Section 10.21 requires prompt notice to the client of any error or omission and its potential consequences.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's representative wishes to obtain account transcripts electronically. The representative may use Tax Pro Account or the e-Services Transcript Delivery System after establishing authorization through:
options: A signed Form W-2
A Form 1099 from the taxpayer
An accepted Form 2848 or Form 8821 on file
A verbal phone request only
questions.rationale: Transcript delivery to a representative requires an accepted Form 2848 or 8821 establishing the authorization.

questions.stem: If a taxpayer defaults on an installment agreement, the IRS generally must:
options: Convert it to an offer in compromise
Provide notice of the proposed termination and an opportunity to appeal before terminating
Immediately seize property without notice
Forgive the remaining balance
questions.rationale: The IRS must notify the taxpayer before terminating an installment agreement and offer an appeal opportunity.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who substantially understates income tax has a substantial understatement when the understatement exceeds the greater of 10% of the tax required to be shown or:
questions.rationale: For individuals, a substantial understatement exists when it exceeds the greater of 10% of the correct tax or $5,000.

questions.stem: The penalty under IRC section 6713 for unauthorized disclosure or use of taxpayer return information by a preparer is a civil penalty, while the related criminal provision is found in:
options: IRC section 7216
IRC section 7212
IRC section 7206
IRC section 7201
questions.rationale: Section 6713 is the civil penalty and section 7216 the criminal penalty for unauthorized disclosure or use of taxpayer information by preparers.

questions.stem: A practitioner negotiates a settlement with the IRS but realizes a conflict of interest arose mid-engagement. Under Circular 230, the practitioner must:
options: Obtain informed written consent from each affected client within a reasonable time, or withdraw
Charge a higher fee to offset the conflict
Continue regardless of the conflict
Report the conflict to the state bar
questions.rationale: When a conflict arises, section 10.29 requires informed written consent from each affected client or withdrawal.

questions.stem: An enrolled agent representing a deceased taxpayer's estate before the IRS must have a Form 2848 signed by:
options: The decedent before death only
Any heir of the estate
The executor, administrator, or other fiduciary authorized to act for the estate
The IRS examiner
questions.rationale: For an estate, the Form 2848 must be signed by the authorized fiduciary, and Form 56 may be needed to establish fiduciary status.

questions.stem: Form 56, Notice Concerning Fiduciary Relationship, is filed to:
options: Request an installment agreement
Notify the IRS of the creation or termination of a fiduciary relationship
Authorize representation
Request a refund
questions.rationale: Form 56 informs the IRS that a fiduciary has assumed or ended responsibility for a taxpayer or estate.

questions.stem: The penalty for failure to deposit employment taxes timely (IRC section 6656) varies by how late the deposit is and can reach:
options: 25% maximum
10% maximum
15% for deposits more than 10 days after an IRS notice/demand
5% maximum
questions.rationale: Section 6656 imposes tiered penalties (2%, 5%, 10%, and 15%) based on how late the employment tax deposit is.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230, negotiating a taxpayer's refund check is:
options: Required for direct deposit
Prohibited for a practitioner who is the income tax return preparer
Only allowed for enrolled agents
Permitted with client consent
questions.rationale: Circular 230 and IRC section 6695(f) prohibit a preparer from endorsing or negotiating a client's refund check.

questions.stem: A taxpayer living in the United States receives a statutory notice of deficiency (90-day letter) dated June 1. By when must the petition to the U.S. Tax Court be filed to preserve prepayment review?
options: Within 30 days from the date the notice was mailed
Within 180 days from the date the notice was mailed
Within 90 days from the date the notice was mailed
Within 60 days from the date the notice was received
questions.rationale: The date stated on the notice as the last day to petition is the deadline to use.

questions.stem: What is the dollar limit for a Tax Court 'small tax case' (S case) procedure?
options: $25,000 for all years combined
$50,000 for each tax year, including penalties
$100,000 for each tax year, excluding penalties
$10,000 for each tax year, including interest
questions.rationale: The S case procedures are informal, and the court may allow evidence that is not otherwise admissible.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to challenge a deficiency in a forum other than the Tax Court and does not want to petition within 90 days. What must she generally do first to sue in U.S. District Court or the Court of Federal Claims?
options: Request a CDP hearing first, and then sue before paying the tax
Pay only the disputed penalty and then file suit in district court
Pay the full tax, file a refund claim, then wait for denial or six months
File a protest within 30 days of the notice, without paying anything
questions.rationale: Divisible taxes such as employment tax penalties have narrower rules.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a 30-day letter proposing a deficiency of $18,000 and disagrees. Which request allows a streamlined Appeals conference without a formal written protest?
options: A Taxpayer Advocate request for assistance on Form 911
A Collection Due Process request on Form 12153 within 30 days
A small case request on Form 12203, since the amount is $25,000 or less
A claim for abatement of the proposed tax on Form 843
questions.rationale: Appeals considers the hazards of litigation in settlement discussions.

questions.stem: A taxpayer signs Form 870, Waiver of Restrictions on Assessment. What is one effect of the waiver?
options: The IRS may assess the agreed amount at once, and a refund claim is still allowed
The taxpayer gives up any right to claim a refund of the amount
The assessment statute of limitations is extended by one year
The waiver stops the IRS from charging interest on the amount
questions.rationale: A Form 870-AD used by Appeals is different and ordinarily precludes reopening the case.

questions.stem: Which form does a taxpayer sign to extend the assessment statute of limitations (ASED) for a specific period?
options: Form 870, Waiver of Restrictions on Assessment
Form 872, Consent to Extend the Time to Assess Tax
Form 4549, Report of Income Tax Examination Changes
Form 2848, Power of Attorney
questions.rationale: Restricted consents limit the extension to particular issues.

questions.stem: An IRS summons is served on a third-party record keeper, such as a bank, requesting a taxpayer's records. How long does the taxpayer generally have to begin a proceeding to quash the summons?
options: 60 days from the date the records are produced
20 days from the date notice of the summons is given
There is no right to quash a third-party summons
90 days from the date of the summons
questions.rationale: The court may enforce the summons if the IRS meets the Powell requirements.

questions.stem: The IRS assessed a tax on March 1, 2020. Assuming no suspending events, when does the collection statute expiration date (CSED) generally occur?
options: Six years after the assessment date
Twenty years after the assessment date
Ten years after the assessment date
Three years after the assessment date
questions.rationale: Timely written waivers may extend the collection period in installment agreement situations.

questions.stem: Which event suspends the running of the 10-year collection statute?
options: A pending offer in compromise, plus 30 days after rejection and any appeal
A request by the taxpayer for a copy of a transcript
The IRS issuing a CP14 balance-due notice to the taxpayer
A change of the taxpayer's address on file with the IRS
questions.rationale: Currently not collectible status does not suspend the statute.

questions.stem: When does the federal tax lien arise?
options: Assessment, then notice and demand, then the taxpayer fails to pay
The date the Notice of Federal Tax Lien is filed in the county
The date the taxpayer files a return that contains an error
The date the taxpayer receives a CP504 notice of intent to levy
questions.rationale: The lien continues until paid or expiring after the CSED.

questions.stem: After the IRS files a Notice of Federal Tax Lien, how long does the taxpayer have to request a Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing?
options: 10 days after the date the Notice of Federal Tax Lien is filed
Any time before the collection statute expiration date
90 days after the date the Notice of Federal Tax Lien is filed
30 days, starting the day after the fifth business day after NFTL filing
questions.rationale: Timely CDP requests suspend collection and the CSED during the hearing.

questions.stem: Within what time must the IRS release a federal tax lien after the liability is fully satisfied?
options: Within 10 days after the date of satisfaction
Within one year after the date of satisfaction
Within 90 days after the date of satisfaction
Within 30 days after the date of satisfaction
questions.rationale: A lien withdrawal (Form 12277) removes the public notice and is separate from release.

questions.stem: What is the general notice requirement before the IRS may levy on a taxpayer's property (other than in jeopardy)?
options: A phone call to the taxpayer, followed by a levy the next day
A court order from a federal judge approving each levy
A CP14 balance-due notice, followed by a levy 10 days later
A Final Notice of Intent to Levy, sent at least 30 days before
questions.rationale: A levy on a principal residence requires judicial approval.

questions.stem: Which kind of IRS action allows immediate assessment and collection without the usual notice and waiting periods when collection is in danger?
options: An installment agreement
A jeopardy assessment or jeopardy levy
A Collection Due Process hearing
A notice of deficiency
questions.rationale: Administrative review is available and judicial review in Tax Court.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's return understates tax by $30,000, which is more than 10% of the correct tax of $200,000. Which accuracy-related penalty and rate may apply?
options: 75% of the underpayment for civil fraud
20% of the underpayment for a substantial understatement of income tax
10% of the underpayment under the substantial understatement rule
40% of the underpayment for negligence
questions.rationale: The penalty can be avoided by showing reasonable cause and good faith.

questions.stem: What is the time limit to request innocent spouse relief under section 6015(b) or (c)?
options: Within 10 years after the return was filed with the IRS
Within 30 days after the date of the final divorce decree
Within two years after the IRS's first collection activity against her
Within 90 days after the return containing the item was filed
questions.rationale: Form 8857 is used to request relief.

questions.stem: What is the minimum payment required with a lump-sum offer in compromise?
options: No payment is required
50% of the offer amount submitted with the application
20% of the offer amount submitted with the application
100% of the offer amount in advance
questions.rationale: Periodic payment offers require monthly payments while the offer is being considered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a ground for an offer in compromise?
options: Doubt that the preparer computed the tax correctly
Doubt as to collectibility of the full amount
Doubt as to liability for the assessed tax
Effective tax administration based on hardship or equity
questions.rationale: The taxpayer must be in filing and payment compliance for an offer to be processed.

questions.stem: What does 'currently not collectible' (CNC) status mean for a taxpayer's account?
options: The liability is forgiven and removed from the taxpayer's account
The IRS releases every lien it has filed against the taxpayer
The collection statute stops running for as long as CNC applies
Active collection pauses for hardship; interest and penalties keep accruing
questions.rationale: The IRS reviews CNC accounts periodically to see if the taxpayer's income has changed.

questions.stem: In which circumstance is an income tax debt generally dischargeable in a chapter 7 bankruptcy?
options: Taxes owed for years in which the debtor filed no return
Return due 3+ years, filed 2+ years, assessed 240+ days before, no fraud
Trust fund taxes owed by a person who was responsible
Any income tax debt can be discharged, whatever its age
questions.rationale: The automatic stay stops most collection while the bankruptcy is pending.

questions.stem: What is the effect of a taxpayer's burden of proof shifting to the IRS under section 7491(a)?
options: The burden always shifts once the taxpayer files a petition
The burden of proof never shifts in any tax case
The taxpayer offers credible evidence, keeps records, and cooperates
The burden shifts whenever the taxpayer has no records at all
questions.rationale: The burden on penalties of production is on the IRS for individuals under §7491(c).

questions.stem: Which authority carries the greatest weight in the hierarchy of tax authorities?
options: IRS publications written for the general public
Private letter rulings issued to individual taxpayers
Revenue rulings issued by the Internal Revenue Service
The Internal Revenue Code, as enacted by Congress
questions.rationale: After Loper Bright (2024), courts apply independent judgment and do not defer to agency interpretations under Chevron.
questions.source: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369 (2024)

questions.stem: Under the Golsen rule, which court's precedent does the Tax Court follow in a regular case?
options: The U.S. Supreme Court, and no other court at all
The Court of Federal Claims in Washington, D.C.
The circuit court of appeals where an appeal would lie, by residence
Whichever circuit court the particular judge prefers
questions.rationale: Appeals from Tax Court regular cases go to the appropriate U.S. Court of Appeals.

questions.stem: Which IRS examination type generally requires the taxpayer to visit an IRS office with records?
options: Field examination
Office examination
Correspondence examination
Math error adjustment
questions.rationale: Taxpayers may request a transfer of the exam to another IRS office if more convenient.

questions.stem: What right does a taxpayer have if the IRS proposes an adjustment through a math error notice under section 6213(b)?
options: Appeal only to the Tax Court, with no other recourse
No right to challenge a math error notice exists
A right to file a Tax Court petition within 30 days
Request abatement within 60 days; the IRS must then abate
questions.rationale: The notice must describe the error and explain the right to abatement.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Cohan rule is correct?
options: Courts may estimate a proven expense, except under strict substantiation
The IRS must disregard missing records and allow no estimate
Estimates are prohibited in every case, whatever the evidence
Estimates are allowed for all expenses, including travel and gifts
questions.rationale: Credible testimony and corroborating evidence improve the outcome.
questions.source: Cohan v. Commissioner, 39 F.2d 540 (2d Cir. 1930); IRC §274(d)

questions.stem: A taxpayer requests a transcript showing the information that third parties reported to the IRS, such as Forms W-2 and 1099. Which transcript is it?
options: Return Transcript
Account Transcript
Wage and Income Transcript
Record of Account
questions.rationale: Practitioners can request transcripts through e-Services (TDS) with a valid CAF authorization.

questions.stem: Which of the following may represent taxpayers before the IRS without limitation as to the tax matters involved?
options: Attorneys, certified public accountants, and enrolled agents
Anyone who prepared and signed the return in question
Any family member of the taxpayer, for any matter
Any enrolled retirement plan agent, for any matter
questions.rationale: Annual Filing Season Program participants have limited representation rights.

questions.stem: How may an enrolled agent satisfy the continuing education requirements for renewal?
options: 72 hours per three years, 16+ per year, with 2 ethics hours yearly
36 hours per three years, with no annual minimum at all
24 hours every year, with no ethics requirement
72 hours every year, with 2 ethics hours in total
questions.rationale: CE must be from IRS-approved providers and reported by the provider or the EA.

questions.stem: An IRS agent requests records from a practitioner that the practitioner has in his possession on behalf of a client, and that are not privileged. What does Circular 230 require?
options: Destroy the records to protect the client's position
Refuse the request until the IRS serves a formal summons
Submit the records promptly, unless a good-faith privilege claim exists
Provide them only after the client signs a written consent
questions.rationale: A practitioner must also not interfere with the lawful efforts of the IRS to obtain information.

questions.stem: A practitioner charges a fee for preparing an original individual income tax return that is contingent on the amount of the refund. Under Circular 230, is this permitted?
options: Yes; contingent fees are allowed for every kind of service
No; contingent fees are generally barred for original returns
Yes, if the fee is disclosed to the client in writing
Yes, but only when the refund exceeds $5,000
questions.rationale: Charging an unconscionable fee is also prohibited.

questions.stem: A client disputes a fee and asks the practitioner to return the client's records. What does Circular 230 require?
options: Return only copies of the records after the dispute is resolved
Return the records only after 90 days
Withhold the records until the fee is paid
Return the client's records promptly on request, even if a fee dispute exists
questions.rationale: Work product that the practitioner prepared but the client has not paid for is not necessarily included if state law allows retention.

questions.stem: A practitioner is asked to represent two clients whose interests are directly adverse. Under what condition can the practitioner proceed?
options: Verbal consent from whichever client is more important
Only after the IRS approves the arrangement in advance
Never; the practitioner must always decline both clients
Written informed consent from each client, and a belief of competent service
questions.rationale: Written confirmation is required within 30 days of the oral consent.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.30, how long must a practitioner who advertises keep copies of advertisements and solicitations?
options: At least 7 years after the last publication
At least 12 months after the last publication
At least 36 months after the last publication
No retention of advertisements is required
questions.rationale: Advertising must not be false, fraudulent, deceptive, or coercive.

questions.stem: A practitioner may not sign a tax return that contains a position unless certain standards are met. Which standard applies under Circular 230 §10.34(a)?
options: No standard applies to returns of individual taxpayers
The position must have at least a 95% chance of success
The position must be more likely than not to prevail
Not signing a position that lacks a reasonable basis, or is unreasonable
questions.rationale: Disclosure on Form 8275 can protect positions with a reasonable basis.

questions.stem: A practitioner relies on information supplied by a client. Under Circular 230 §10.34(d), when may the practitioner rely on it in good faith?
options: Rely only if the client signs a sworn statement first
Always rely on it, with no duty to ask any questions
Never rely on it without full independent verification
Rely in good faith, but inquire if it looks inconsistent or incomplete
questions.rationale: Document the inquiries and the client's answers in the work paper.

questions.stem: What requirements apply to written advice under Circular 230 §10.37?
options: Use reasonable assumptions, consider all facts, and avoid unreasonable reliance
Obtain an IRS private letter ruling before giving any written advice
Add a legend stating the advice cannot be used to avoid penalties
Never give written advice to an individual client
questions.rationale: A practitioner must not take into account the possibility that a return won't be audited.

questions.stem: A firm's principal knows that the firm's procedures for complying with Circular 230 are inadequate and that a pattern of noncompliance has occurred. Which section addresses the responsibility of the individual with principal authority?
options: §10.36, reasonable procedures to ensure compliance
§10.29, conflicts of interest between clients
§10.25, practice by former government employees
§10.26, notaries who are also practitioners
questions.rationale: Section 10.38 provides for firm sanctions where the firm participated in or knew of the conduct.

questions.stem: Which of the following sanctions may the Office of Professional Responsibility impose on a practitioner under Circular 230?
options: Censure, suspension, disbarment, or a monetary penalty
A monetary penalty of up to $100 is the only sanction
Imprisonment for up to one year for each violation
A private warning is the only sanction available
questions.rationale: Sanctions follow a complaint, answer, and possible hearing before an administrative law judge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is disreputable conduct under Circular 230 §10.51?
options: Willfully failing to file his own federal tax return
Appealing an adverse IRS decision for a client
Charging a fee based on the time and effort expended
Taking a reasonable position on a client's return
questions.rationale: Conviction of an offense under the revenue laws or involving dishonesty is also disreputable conduct.

questions.stem: What does Form 2848 authorize a representative to do that Form 8821 does not?
options: Inspect the taxpayer's confidential tax information
Act for the taxpayer, including advocacy and signing agreements
Receive copies of IRS notices sent to the taxpayer
Receive a copy of the taxpayer's IRS transcripts
questions.rationale: Form 2848 must list specific tax matters and years, and may include up to three future periods.

questions.stem: Under what conditions may a representative sign a taxpayer's return pursuant to Form 2848?
options: Whenever the taxpayer is too busy to sign the return
Never; a representative may never sign a return
Any time the representative holds a valid Form 2848
Only for disease or injury, 60 days abroad, or other good cause
questions.rationale: Part II of Form 2848 line 5 must authorize signing a return.

questions.stem: During an IRS interview, a taxpayer decides she wants a representative present. What is the IRS's obligation under Taxpayer Bill of Rights provisions?
options: Continue the interview until it is finished
End the examination and assess the proposed tax
Deny the request unless the taxpayer is already under audit
Suspend the interview and let the representative attend
questions.rationale: A representative may attend, and the taxpayer need not attend unless summoned.

questions.stem: What limited representation rights do Annual Filing Season Program (AFSP) participants have?
options: Unlimited rights equal to those of an enrolled agent
Represent clients whose returns they prepared before revenue agents, not Appeals
The right to represent clients before the Tax Court
No right to represent clients before the IRS at all
questions.rationale: Participants must complete 18 hours of continuing education, including a 6-hour tax course and 2 hours of ethics.

questions.stem: What is a CAF number?
options: An ID number given to a representative in the Centralized Authorization File
A code that identifies the tax year under review
The number of a client's own tax account
The number of years of CE a practitioner completed
questions.rationale: A CAF number doesn't indicate professional status. It is an administrative identifier.

questions.stem: A taxpayer asks the IRS for an installment agreement for a $9,000 balance due. Which type of agreement is guaranteed if the taxpayer meets the conditions?
options: A guaranteed installment agreement, if the liability is $25,000 or less and paid within five years
A guaranteed installment agreement, if the liability is $5,000 or less and paid within one year
A guaranteed installment agreement, if the liability is $50,000 or less and paid within six years
A guaranteed installment agreement, if the liability is $10,000 or less and paid within three years
questions.rationale: Guaranteed agreements require compliance with filing and payment in prior years and a payment plan to pay in three years.

questions.stem: Which form does an individual taxpayer generally use to give the IRS a collection information statement when requesting a non-streamlined installment agreement?
options: Form 9465, Installment Agreement Request
Form 12153, Request for a Collection Due Process Hearing
Form 433-F or Form 433-A, depending on the case
Form 656, Offer in Compromise
questions.rationale: Allowable expenses follow National and Local Standards used by the IRS.

questions.stem: The IRS proposes the trust fund recovery penalty (TFRP) against a corporate officer by sending Letter 1153. How long does the officer have to appeal the proposed assessment?
options: 10 days from the date of the letter, then the tax is assessed
60 days from the date of the letter (75 days if addressed outside the United States)
90 days from the date of the letter, with an extension for foreign addresses
30 days from the date of the letter, with no extension
questions.rationale: The IRS first interviews the responsible person using Form 4180.

questions.stem: For a corporate officer to be liable for the trust fund recovery penalty, which two elements must exist?
options: Being an employee when the corporation's own income tax was unpaid
Ownership of corporate stock together with receipt of a salary
Signing the corporate income tax return and managing the books
Responsibility for collecting and paying over the tax, plus willful failure
questions.rationale: Preferring other creditors over the IRS can establish willfulness.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a CP2000 notice from the Automated Underreporter program. What is the general time to respond?
options: 10 days from the date of the notice
90 days from the date of the notice
30 days from the date of the notice
There is no deadline to respond
questions.rationale: A CP2000 is not an audit but a proposed adjustment from matching data.

questions.stem: Appeals officers evaluate cases using which approach when considering settlement of a docketed or non-docketed dispute?
options: The hazards of litigation, the chance each side would prevail
Whether the examining agent agrees with the taxpayer's view
A fixed 50% discount applied to all penalties in dispute
The percentage of the deficiency that the taxpayer can pay
questions.rationale: Fast Track Settlement allows mediation by Appeals while the case is still in the examination function.

questions.stem: What does the standard for reasonable cause to abate a penalty generally require?
options: Reliance on advice from a friend who is not a professional
Ordinary business care and prudence, yet still unable to comply
Lack of knowledge of the law on the part of the taxpayer
A simple mistake that the taxpayer cannot explain further
