questions.rationale: A person cannot delegate the duty to file on time to an agent and then claim reasonable cause (Boyle).
questions.source: United States v. Boyle, 469 U.S. 241 (1985); IRM 20.1.1

questions.stem: A practitioner's client had a net operating loss and wants a quick refund of tax paid in a prior year. Which form allows a corporation to apply for a tentative refund from an NOL carryback?
options: Form 1139, Corporation Application for Tentative Refund
Form 843, Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement
Form 1045, Application for Tentative Refund
Form 1040-X, Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return
questions.rationale: The application must be filed within 12 months after the end of the year of the loss.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a protective refund claim?
options: To stop the IRS from collecting any assessed tax
To extend the statute of limitations on assessment
To keep a refund right alive when it depends on a future event
To lower the interest rate that applies to a deficiency
questions.rationale: The claim should state the grounds and facts, even if the amount cannot yet be determined.

questions.stem: What are the civil penalties for a non-willful violation of the FBAR reporting requirement?
options: A per-violation penalty, inflation-adjusted, with a reasonable cause defense
A flat $50 penalty for each account, whatever the balance
No civil penalty at all if the violation was non-willful
A penalty equal to 100% of the highest account balance
questions.rationale: Taxpayers with non-willful violations may use the Streamlined Filing Compliance Procedures.

questions.stem: Which privilege does section 7525 provide?
options: Confidential tax advice from a federally authorized tax practitioner, in civil matters
All return preparation work papers, in every kind of proceeding
All communications with a return preparer, even in criminal cases
Communications with any accountant, in any kind of proceeding
questions.rationale: Communications must be for tax advice and made in confidence.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to challenge an IRS determination in a Collection Due Process hearing and proposes an installment agreement. What is the standard of review if the case goes to Tax Court?
options: Clear error review of the decision by a jury of citizens
No judicial review of a CDP determination is available
De novo review of every collection decision Appeals made
Abuse of discretion, except de novo if the liability itself is at issue
questions.rationale: The petition must be filed within 30 days of the Notice of Determination.

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants audit reconsideration for a prior-year assessment made on the basis of a substitute for return. What is a requirement?
options: New information, or an original return the IRS has not considered
Full payment of the assessed amount before the request
A request filed within 30 days after the assessment date
A Tax Court petition filed before the request is made
questions.rationale: Reconsideration does not extend the statutes of limitations.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Streamlined Filing Compliance Procedures is correct?
options: Reduced penalties for U.S. taxpayers whose offshore omissions were non-willful
They erase all of the tax and interest otherwise owed
They cover any violation, whether willful or non-willful
They are open only to business entities, not individuals
questions.rationale: The taxpayer must certify non-willfulness.

questions.stem: A taxpayer has not filed returns for several years. What does the IRS generally require for a taxpayer to be in compliance for collection alternatives like an offer or installment agreement?
options: Only an amended return for the prior year is needed
All required returns filed and current estimated payments made
Only the most recent year's return needs to be filed
No filings are required to be eligible for an alternative
questions.rationale: The IRS may require up to six years of returns, but can request more.

questions.stem: What happens when the IRS prepares a substitute for return (SFR) under section 6020(b) for a nonfiler?
options: The taxpayer may not later file an original return
The assessment statute of limitations starts to run at once
Tax computed with the standard deduction only; assessed after a deficiency notice
The taxpayer is treated as having filed a valid return
questions.rationale: A notice of deficiency allows Tax Court review before assessment.

questions.stem: In a field audit, the IRS agent sends an Information Document Request (IDR). Which form is it commonly?
options: Form 5701, Notice of Proposed Adjustment
Form 4549, Report of Income Tax Examination Changes
Form 872, Consent to Extend the Time to Assess Tax
Form 4564, Information Document Request
questions.rationale: Practitioners should respond to IDRs within the stated time or request an extension.

questions.stem: A return preparer prepares a return with an unreasonable position, and the preparer did not have substantial authority or a reasonable belief that the position would more likely than not be sustained. What is the minimum penalty under section 6694(a)?
options: The greater of $500 or 20% of the tax understatement
The greater of $1,000 or 50% of the income the preparer derived
The greater of $5,000 or 75% of the income the preparer derived
A flat penalty of $250 for each return the preparer prepared
questions.rationale: Disclosure of a position with a reasonable basis on Form 8275 can avoid the penalty.

questions.stem: A preparer fails to sign a return that he prepared for compensation. What penalty applies under section 6695(b)?
options: Suspension from practice before the IRS for five years
A criminal fine of $10,000 plus up to one year in jail
A penalty for each failure (indexed), up to an annual maximum
No penalty applies to a preparer who fails to sign
questions.rationale: The preparer must sign after the return is completed and before it is presented to the taxpayer.

questions.stem: A return preparer discloses a client's tax return information to a third party without the client's written consent, other than as permitted by regulation. What penalties may apply?
options: Only a private reprimand from the IRS, with no penalty
A $250 civil penalty per disclosure, plus criminal penalties for knowing disclosure
A penalty equal to the amount of the client's refund
No penalty applies when the third party is a lender
questions.rationale: Taxpayer consent must be written and must identify the purpose of the disclosure.

questions.stem: A client asks a preparer for a copy of the return the preparer prepared. When must the preparer furnish a copy to the taxpayer?
options: Within 90 days after the date the return is filed
Only if the taxpayer asks for it after the return is filed
Only if the return shows a refund due to the taxpayer
By the time the return is presented for the taxpayer's signature
questions.rationale: A preparer must also keep a copy or list of returns for three years.

questions.stem: For how long must a return preparer retain a copy of each return or a list of the returns prepared, including names and TINs?
options: Until the statute of limitations on assessment ends, plus ten years
One year after filing
Seven years after filing
Three years after the close of the return period
questions.rationale: The return period runs from July 1 of the year the return is filed through June 30 of the next year.

questions.stem: A return is mailed on the due date and postmarked by the U.S. Postal Service on that date, but the IRS receives it three days later. How is the return treated?
options: It is timely filed under the timely mailing rule
It is timely only if sent by overnight courier
It is late because the IRS did not receive it by the due date
It is timely only if the taxpayer paid a fee
questions.rationale: Registered mail provides prima facie evidence of delivery. Certified mail provides proof of mailing.

questions.stem: A taxpayer died before filing the return for the year. Who signs the final return?
options: The paid preparer, signing on behalf of the decedent
The personal representative, or the surviving spouse on a joint return
Any family member of the decedent, whether appointed or not
No one; a decedent's return needs no signature
questions.rationale: Form 1310 is needed to claim a refund due to the deceased taxpayer, unless the surviving spouse files jointly.

questions.stem: A taxpayer chooses to split a direct-deposit refund among accounts. How many accounts can receive a split refund using Form 8888?
options: Up to five accounts, each at a different bank
Only two accounts, one for each spouse on a joint return
Up to three accounts at U.S. financial institutions
Only one account, in the name of the first taxpayer
questions.rationale: The account must be in the taxpayer's name, and the preparer's own account is not permitted.

questions.stem: An electronic return originator (ERO) accepts a return for e-file. Which statement about the ERO's responsibilities is correct?
options: Keep Form 8879 or 8453, the return, and support for three years
Omit the EFIN, since the preparer's PTIN is enough
Keep the records for one year after the return is filed
Transmit the return before the taxpayer has signed it
questions.rationale: EROs must also provide the taxpayer a copy of the return on request.

questions.stem: What does the FTC Safeguards Rule require of tax professionals who prepare returns for compensation?
options: Delete all client data as soon as the return is filed
File an annual data security report with the IRS
Provide credit monitoring to every client each year
Maintain a written information security plan to protect client data
questions.rationale: A data breach should be reported to the IRS Stakeholder Liaison and appropriate state authorities.

questions.stem: On what date must a taxpayer file a federal income tax return to be considered timely if the regular due date falls on a Saturday?
options: The preceding Friday
The next business day
The date does not change
The following Monday, but only with an extension
questions.rationale: The same rule applies to payments and other acts due on that date.

questions.stem: A preparer who files returns on paper because the client elected not to e-file must attach which form?
options: Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization
Form 8453, U.S. Individual Income Tax Transmittal
Form 8867, Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist
Form 8948, Preparer Explanation for Not Filing Electronically
questions.rationale: The client's election should be documented in writing.

questions.stem: A taxpayer needs more time to file because she is a U.S. citizen living abroad. What automatic extension applies to filing and paying?
options: An automatic extension to April 15 of the following year
An automatic two months, to June 15, with interest from April 15
None; there is no automatic extension for taxpayers abroad
An automatic extension to December 31, with no interest due
questions.rationale: The taxpayer must attach a statement to the return explaining the basis for the extension.

questions.stem: A taxpayer files an amended return to correct a previously filed return. Which form is used for an individual's amended return, and how should it be filed?
options: A second Form 1040 with 'amended' written across the top
Form 843, mailed together with the original return
Form 1040-X, filed electronically for recent years or on paper
Form 4868, filed within 30 days of the original return
questions.rationale: Amended returns must be signed, and a paid preparer must sign too.

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives IRS Letter 3219, Statutory Notice of Deficiency. What is the significance of this notice?
options: It is a request for more information about a return
It is a bill for tax that the IRS has already assessed
It starts the 90-day period to petition the Tax Court before assessment
It is a notice of intent to levy the taxpayer's wages
questions.rationale: The notice must be sent to the taxpayer's last known address.

questions.stem: What is the fee to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court?
options: No fee is charged
questions.rationale: The petition can be filed electronically through DAWSON.

questions.stem: Before contacting third parties about a taxpayer's tax liability in an examination, what must the IRS do?
options: Notify only the taxpayer's employer, not the taxpayer
Obtain a court order before any third-party contact
Give the taxpayer reasonable advance notice of third-party contacts
Contact third parties without notice to the taxpayer
questions.rationale: Exceptions exist for criminal investigations and to avoid reprisal.

questions.stem: What is the IRS Fast Track Settlement program?
options: A voluntary Appeals mediation of exam issues, before the case leaves exam
A program that settles criminal investigations quickly
A program that waives late filing penalties for first offenders
A way to skip Appeals and go straight to the Tax Court
questions.rationale: Participation requires agreement of both the taxpayer and the IRS function.

questions.stem: What are the eligibility criteria for an individual to apply for enrollment as an enrolled agent?
options: Be a licensed attorney in any state of the United States
Hold a CPA license and a master's degree in taxation
Hold an accounting degree and five years of audit experience
Pass all three SEE parts (or have IRS experience) and pass a suitability check
questions.rationale: Enrolled status lasts for a three-year cycle, renewed with CE and Form 8554.

questions.stem: Under Circular 230 §10.82, in what circumstance may the OPR institute an expedited proceeding to suspend a practitioner?
options: A client filing an amended return that he prepared
Advertising his practice in a local newspaper
Charging a client a high fee for complex work
Conviction of a revenue-law crime, willful nonfiling of his own returns, or license loss
questions.rationale: The practitioner is given notice and an opportunity to respond.

questions.stem: A taxpayer disagrees with Appeals' rejection of an offer in compromise. What appeal rights exist?
options: Request Appeals review within 30 days of the rejection letter
None; a rejected offer can never be reviewed
Sue in district court within one year of the rejection
Petition the Tax Court within 90 days of the rejection
questions.rationale: The collection statute is suspended while the offer is pending and during the appeal.

questions.stem: In an examination of a return claiming the earned income credit, what typical notice does the IRS send to request documentation by mail?
options: Letter CP2000, proposing changes from third-party data
Letter CP14, a balance due notice
Letter CP504, a notice of intent to levy
Letter CP75, requesting documents to verify eligibility
questions.rationale: A preparer must have complied with Form 8867 due diligence to respond effectively.

questions.stem: A taxpayer's e-filed return is rejected because the dependent's SSN was already used on another return. What is the correct next step?
options: Verify the SSN, fix and resubmit, or file on paper with the reject code
Wait until next year to file the return
Delete the dependent and let the return refile itself
Treat the return as filed, whatever the rejection said
questions.rationale: Taxpayers have an extended period to perfect a rejected return and still be timely if the rules are met.

questions.stem: When must a paid preparer who prepared a return for compensation sign the return?
options: Only after the IRS asks the preparer to sign it
Never; only the taxpayer ever signs a return
Only if the return shows a refund for the taxpayer
After completing it, before giving it to the taxpayer to sign
questions.rationale: A preparer's signature is in the paid preparer use only section of the return.
